data.title: Workforce Retention Funding for Critical Access Hospitals and Clinics
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS)
data.summary: Workforce retention funding specifically for Critical Access Hospitals and their owned and operated clinics in North Dakota. Part of the Strengthen and Stabilize Rural Health Workforce pillar of ND's RHTP five-year plan.
applicantTypes: Clinic Owned by Critical Access Hospital

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014507 - RFA - Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC) Services Focused
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: Texas Health and Human Services Commission is soliciting applications for the Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC) Program focused on improving access to long-term services and supports for older adults and individuals with disabilities. Up to $8,866,200 in federal funding is available to support ADRC activities in seven service areas, including information and referral, respite care referrals, Local Contact Agency services, housing navigation, and outreach for Medicare beneficiaries.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) Services Grant (HHS0014455)
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) / Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS)
data.summary: This grant, funded by the State of Texas, supports local programs to provide services and support for persons with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD), their caregivers, and promotes early detection and diagnosis. The program reflects priorities in the Healthy Brain Initiative Road Map 2023-2027, with priority given to applicants addressing both cognitive decline and social vulnerability, particularly in high-need regions.

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014211 - RFA - Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
data.summary: This opportunity provides grants to establish or expand behavioral health centers and jail diversion centers in rural Texas counties (population <250,000) for adults and children. Up to $9M will be awarded in FY25 to eligible mental health providers partnering with local mental health authorities. Projects must utilize evidence-based or best practices for mental health and substance use treatment.

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014532 - RFA - Houston Preventative and Primary Health Services (PPHS)
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: This Request for Applications from the Texas HHSC seeks to implement a program expanding access to no- or low-cost preventive and primary health services, including medical, dental, diagnostic, specialty, and children’s health services, for low-income adults and children in the Houston area.
applicantTypes: State Controlled Institution of Higher Learning

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014534 - RFA - Nutrition Incentive Program Project
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
data.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) requests applications for the Nutrition Incentive Program Project (RFA No. HHS0014534). This project aims to increase fruit and vegetable purchases among SNAP recipients in Texas using point-of-purchase incentives. The program provides up to $6,000,000 in state funds for projects supporting local economies, Texas farmers, and healthier eating among low-income populations. The grant period is eight months beginning January 2025. No cost share or match is required.

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014610 - RFA -  Intellectual or Developmental Disabilities (IDD) | Multi-Assistance Center Demonstration Project
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: The Multi-Assistance Center (MAC) Demonstration Project provides Single Point of Contact Coordination as well as medical, therapy, and non-medical services for individuals of all ages with special needs, including those with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD), in Bexar County and other South Texas counties in Health Regions 8 and 11.
applicantTypes: Eligible service providers in South Texas Regions 8 and 11

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014609 - RFA - Ryan White Part B Minority AIDS Initiative (MAI)
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC), Department of State Health Services (DSHS), HIV/STD Section, HIV Care and Medications Unit
data.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission, Department of State Health Services (DSHS), is soliciting competitive applications for the Ryan White Part B Minority AIDS Initiative (MAI). The program provides transitional HIV-related services for incarcerated and recently released racial/ethnic minorities, with an emphasis on increasing enrollment in the Texas HIV Medication Program and care linkage in the Dallas and Houston regions. Eligible activities include discharge planning, outreach, health education, emergency financial assistance, and medical transportation.

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014956 - RFA - Children's Hospital Construction Grant Program
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) invites eligible children's hospitals in Texas to apply for funding to construct or renovate facilities to add new inpatient pediatric mental health beds. The grant program focuses on addressing unmet need for youth aged 0-20 requiring mental health services and requires a local cost-sharing match.

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0015357 - RFA - Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Outreach and Application Assistance
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: Texas HHSC seeks applications from government and nonprofit organizations to expand SNAP outreach and application assistance statewide, particularly targeting rural and underserved populations. The goal is to reduce barriers, increase SNAP participation and knowledge, and ensure greater food security throughout Texas.

data.title: TX - 2025 - HHS0015344 BCCS RFA - Breast and Cervical Cancer Services
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
data.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission requests applications for the Breast and Cervical Cancer Services grant program. The program aims to improve access to breast and cervical cancer screening and diagnostic services for underserved and low-income women in Texas, focusing especially on rural and other underserved areas. The funding is federally and state supported, with required matching funds, for a five-year grant term. Estimated total available funding is $54.4 million.

data.title: Texas Rural Hospital Labor and Delivery Grant (HHS0015668)
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: HHSC issued RFA HHS0015668 for Rural Hospital Labor and Delivery grant support using state-appropriated funds for rural obstetrical service stability.

data.title: Texas Rural Hospital Improvement Grant (HHS0015677)
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) is offering the Rural Hospital Improvement Grant (RFA No. HHS0015677) to provide time-limited financial support for rural hospitals in Texas. Up to 33 hospitals may each receive up to $350,000, with a total grant pool of $11,550,000 for FY2025, supporting hospital improvement activities aimed at enhancing financial stability. No local cost share or match is required.

data.title: Texas Rural Hospital Debt Reduction Grant (HHS0015180)
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: HHSC issued RFA HHS0015180 for Rural Hospital Debt Reduction to improve financial stability and reduce closure risk among rural hospitals.

data.title: RFI 34320-21126 - Rural Mother-Infant Welcome Home Initiative Support Services
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: Request for Information issued by the Tennessee Department of Health seeking market input from organizations experienced in supporting rural maternal-infant health through community engagement and events, as part of the Welcome Home Initiative. Responses will inform subsequent procurement and program implementation for rural counties.

data.title: Wyoming Federal RHTP Award (FY2026-FY2030)
data.issuingAgency: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
data.summary: The Wyoming Federal RHTP Award (FY2026–FY2030) is a cooperative agreement funded by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), authorized under Section 71401 of the Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025. Wyoming is awarded $205,004,742.95 for the first funding period (Dec 2025–Oct 2026) as part of the $10 billion annual nationwide RHTP to improve rural healthcare access, workforce, sustainability, and innovation. State initiatives commonly include expanded telehealth, workforce development and retention, new care models for maternal and chronic conditions, and bolstering rural hospital stability. Future years’ funding is contingent on annual performance and compliance with program terms.

data.title: Florida Federal RHTP Award (FY2026-FY2030)
data.issuingAgency: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
data.summary: Florida has been awarded $210 million through the CMS RHTP for FY2026-FY2030. The award aims to bolster rural health care in Florida by expanding workforce development, clinical training and rural rotations; providing start-up funding for rural and satellite clinics; and investing in mobile health units, telehealth, behavioral health telehubs, remote monitoring, and advanced telespecialty services. Over 1.2 million rural Floridians will benefit from improved access to essential health services. The Agency for Health Care Administration administers the award and is implementing a comprehensive transformation plan focused on workforce, innovation, and access.

data.title: Texas Federal RHTP Award (FY2026-FY2030)
data.issuingAgency: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
data.summary: The Texas Federal RHTP Award provides funding to the Texas Health & Human Services Commission to support the 'Rural Texas Strong' initiative, aiming to transform rural healthcare for the FY2026-FY2030 period. With total funding of $1.4 billion over five years, including an initial $281.3 million awarded for FY2026, the program enables Texas to launch statewide efforts to improve rural Medicaid and hospital sustainability through initiatives focused on prevention and wellness, health IT, telehealth, workforce development, cybersecurity, and infrastructure enhancement for rural healthcare providers. The program's objectives include expanding rural care access, advancing technology and digital health, supporting provider sustainability, workforce recruitment and retention, and strengthening overall population health outcomes.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP)
data.issuingAgency: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
data.summary: The Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) dedicates $50 billion in federal funding to transform rural healthcare delivery nationwide from FY2026 to FY2030. The program supports state-based innovation, sustainable care access, workforce development, care coordination, and technology upgrades. Funds are distributed to states via cooperative agreements and focus on improving healthcare access, quality, and outcomes through evidence-based interventions, sustainable rural provider models, and technology-driven solutions.

data.title: Missouri Federal RHTP Award (FY2026-FY2030)
data.issuingAgency: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
data.summary: The Missouri Federal RHTP Award for FY2026-FY2030, as outlined in the CMS 50-State Spotlights, provides $216M in federal funding to support transforming rural healthcare. Missouri’s statewide plan focuses on workforce development, digital infrastructure, improved care integration, telehealth expansion, and targeted outcomes for chronic disease, maternal health, and behavioral health. Key initiatives include expanding digital maternity care, launching regional cancer prevention hubs, and integrating behavioral health. The program aims to modernize healthcare delivery, increase access, optimize health outcomes, and enable sustainable, high-quality care close to home.

data.title: Small Rural Hospital Improvement Program Grants
data.issuingAgency: California State Office of Rural Health (CalSORH) / HRSA
data.summary: SHIP grants provide funding to small rural hospitals for projects that improve quality reporting, develop shared savings/ACO infrastructure, or enhance financial operations. Eligible facilities must have 49 or fewer beds and be located in rural areas. The California State Office of Rural Health collects applications for HRSA funding under Social Security Act Section 1820(8)(3). Awards are based on federal appropriations, typically for one year, with renewal available upon satisfactory performance.

data.title: RHTP 2026: Advancing Technology, Prevention, and Workforce Capacity in Rural New Jersey
data.issuingAgency: Office of Primary Care and Rural Health, Division of Health Promotion, New Jersey Department of Health
data.summary: The RHTP 2026, issued by the New Jersey Office of Primary Care and Rural Health, supports projects that expand preventive services, deploy technology and telehealth, strengthen workforce capacity, and incentivize recruitment and retention in rural New Jersey healthcare settings. A total of $27.5 million is available across four main activity areas, aiming to improve health outcomes in rural census tracts with an emphasis on the uninsured and underinsured. No cost sharing or match is required. Applications are due by January 20, 2026, and must be submitted through the NJDOH SAGE Grants management portal.

data.summary: Supports Local and Tribal Health Departments in developing community health worker networks; Phase 2 will expand to other clinic types.

data.title: TX - 2026 - HHS0016838 - RFA - Maternal Health Outcomes Program
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
data.summary: The Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program (HHS0016838) provides up to $5,000,000 to advance systems, data, partnerships, and coordination to improve maternal health outcomes across Texas. The RFA targets reducing severe obstetric complications, especially in rural and high-need areas. Funds support quality improvement, systems changes, and capacity-building; direct clinical care is not funded.

data.title: Centers of Excellence (RFP PHTHORC26008) — Notice of Intent to Award
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary:
Notice of Intent to Award for Centers of Excellence, RFP PHTHORC26008.

The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will fund approximately three projects to improve rural EMS transport capacity for high-risk obstetric and neonatal patients, equipping EMS agencies with specialized training, tele OB support, and neonatal-specific equipment. Supported by over $209 million in CMS/HHS funding, these projects will establish consistent, reliable maternal and neonatal transfer patterns across a statewide hub-and-spoke network.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Texas Comprehensive Rehabilitation Services Mobile Stroke Unit (MSU) Grant (HHS0016736)
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: This Request for Applications funds deployment or expansion of Mobile Stroke Units through the Comprehensive Rehabilitation Services (CRS) program in Texas. $5,000,000 total is available across an anticipated 8 awards for a two-year project period. Funds support advanced, community-based mobile stroke emergency treatment, including evidence-based pre-hospital care and telemedicine for stroke, traumatic brain injury, or spinal cord injury.

data.title: Rural Health Workforce Pipeline: Pathways, Upskilling, and Retention (Round 2)
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health
data.summary: The Rural Health Workforce Pipeline: Pathways, Upskilling, and Retention (Round 2) RFP funds major investments in developing, upskilling, and retaining healthcare professionals in Ohio’s rural counties. This initiative, part of the Ohio Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), prioritizes integrated workforce pipelines, education partnerships, work-based learning, and retention incentives. Applicants must address workforce shortages, chronic disease, and sustainable rural healthcare through collaboration with schools, colleges, employers, and health facilities. Service commitments in RHTP sites and upskilling strategies are strongly encouraged. Funding is aligned with federal CMS priorities under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Section 71403 of Public Law 119-21).

data.title: Alaska Rural Health Transformation Program – Letter of Interest (LOI) Round 1
data.issuingAgency: Alaska Department of Health
data.summary: First Letter of Interest (LOI) registration period for Alaska's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Community-based organizations and entities submitted LOIs to pursue Planning or Implementation pathways. LOI submission is required to access RHTP funding. Outcomes for LOI applicants communicated May 22, 2026. Program addresses six statewide healthcare initiatives: maternal and child health, healthcare access, preventive care, fiscal sustainability through pay-for-value models, workforce strengthening, and technology innovation.

data.title: GME Fellowship Expansion Grant - Rural Health Transformation Program
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Board of Health Care Workforce (GBHCW)
data.summary: This Georgia Board of Health Care Workforce grant supports expansion of Fellowship positions in Graduate Medical Education (GME) at eligible rural Georgia hospitals/health systems through the Rural Health Transformation Program. Funds support a net increase in filled Fellowship slots in high-need specialties. Up to 12 slots statewide. Each slot: $200,000 per PGY year, up to 3 years. Fellows commit to 5 years combined training and rural Georgia practice. Intent-to-apply deadline is March 15, 2026; first payments begin November 1, 2026. Priority to Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, Pediatrics, OB/GYN, General Surgery, Geriatrics, Psychiatry, Emergency Medicine, Neurology. Full eligibility, application steps, and requirements detailed on program web page.

data.title: Nebraska RHTP Initiative 4.4a: Chronic Disease Management Navigation and Education Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services, Chronic Disease Prevention Program, invited proposals to expand chronic disease management through community-based education, care navigation, and self-management support — helping people with conditions like diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and asthma connect with resources and navigate the health system. Funded under Nebraska's RHTP Initiative 4.4a. Awards were capped at $400,000 per applicant; 24 organizations were selected for award (announced May 6, 2026), totaling $6,594,460.94.

data.title: Delaware Medical School Partnership – Rural Health Transformation Program
data.issuingAgency: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services, Division of Public Health
data.summary: Delaware solicits proposals for a visionary medical school partner to launch its first in-state four-year medical school under the federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), supported by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). Nearly $100 million in anticipated RHTP funding is available over five years, focusing on building a sustainable pipeline of locally trained primary care physicians and workforce in rural Sussex and Kent Counties. The initiative targets long-term health, workforce development, and improved rural access, requiring robust sustainability, compliance, and engagement of rural health facilities.
applicantTypes: Public or private higher education institutions with relevant medical education programs

data.title: NC ROOTS Hub Leads — Rural Health Transformation Program
data.issuingAgency: NC DHHS Office of Rural Health
data.summary: NC DHHS Office of Rural Health sought six regional lead organizations (one per NC Medicaid region) to serve as NC ROOTS Hub Leads, responsible for managing and coordinating rural health transformation initiatives—including primary care, behavioral health, workforce development, value-based payment, and digital health—for roughly 3 million rural North Carolinians. Funding for GAP 1 totals $7,513,062 (approximately $1,252,177 per hub for 17 months). Awards were announced May 1, 2026. Five organizations were selected: Impact Health (Region 1), Trillium Health Resources (Regions 2 & 5), Vaya Health (Region 3), UNC Hospitals (Region 4), and Access East Inc. (Region 6). Program period: June 1, 2026 – October 30, 2027.

data.title: School-Based Health Center Expansion Initiative – Kent and Sussex Counties
data.issuingAgency: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services, Division of Public Health
data.summary: Competitive funding to establish and operate at least four school-based health centers (SBHCs) in rural elementary and middle schools in Kent and Sussex Counties, Delaware. This expansion initiative aims to improve health outcomes, educational success, and reduce disparities by providing comprehensive, integrated physical and behavioral health care directly to students and families. Required services include enhanced behavioral health, preventive screenings, health education, and coordination with community providers. The goal is to serve at least 400 patients by year three. Medicaid billing required for sustainability.

data.title: Delaware Food Is Medicine Infrastructure Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services
data.summary: Delaware's Division of Public Health invites proposals for the Food Is Medicine Infrastructure Initiative. The program funds professional services to implement sustainable, replicable rural health interventions integrating nutrition-based strategies for chronic disease management. Activities include recruitment of community health workers and registered dietitians for Kent and Sussex counties, telehealth and EMR integration, culinary medicine teacher training, and robust data/evaluation strategies. Federal funding is available for non-food expenses. The aim is outcome-driven improvement in rural food security, chronic disease, and establishing long-term payment/reimbursement infrastructure.

data.title: VT DAIL RHT NOFO: Expanding Dialysis & Ventilator Services
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Department of Disabilities, Aging and Independent Living (DAIL), Agency of Human Services
data.summary: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) solicits proposals from licensed Vermont nursing facilities to establish and expand in-state dialysis and ventilator services for long-term care residents, focused on rural access. Funded through Vermont’s Rural Health Transformation (RHT) program and the CMS grant award #RHTCMS332047-01-00, the initiative supports acquisition of specialized equipment and staff training (not facility renovations) with the goal to increase sustainable capacity for high-acuity care in nursing facilities. All dialysis proposals must include partnership with a qualified End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) provider, and ventilator proposals must demonstrate partnership with an Acute Care or Critical Access Hospital. Grants are for 14 months (August 1, 2026–September 30, 2027) with required quarterly reporting and may be extended for up to four additional years with approval. Selection is based on alignment with the RHT program, proposed plan, organizational capacity, partnerships, and sustainability.

data.title: New Mexico Rural Health Care Delivery Fund Stabilization Grant FY27-29
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Health Care Authority
data.summary:
The Rural Health Care Delivery Fund Stabilization Grant FY27-29 offers financial assistance to licensed New Mexico Medicaid-enrolled providers serving Medicaid patients in eligible rural areas. The program aims to stabilize essential rural health care services experiencing operating losses due to ongoing operational challenges. Eligible projects focus on maintaining current services to prevent reductions or closures, with allowable uses including support for staffing, operational costs, and other expenses required to maintain existing services.

The Rural Health Care Delivery Fund (RHCDF) Stabilization Grant provides financial support to rural New Mexico Medicaid-enrolled providers and facilities to maintain essential health care services. Funding offsets documented operating losses for existing Medicaid-reimbursable services at risk of reduction or closure, with the goal of stabilizing service delivery in rural communities. Applicants may propose stabilization projects for clinics, service lines, programs, or sites, with flexibility to request funding for one, two, or three years in FY27–FY29.

$40.6 million awarded to 26 rural health care organizations as part of the Rural Health Care Delivery Fund. This is an award announcement; the application phase is closed.

$20 million is available for rural health care providers to support rural delivery, as allocated by the state. Applications open July 1.

data.title: Make Rural Nebraska Healthy Again Through Food as Medicine
data.issuingAgency: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: This RFA announces up to $10,000,000 in funding for eligible rural food cooperatives, producers, food pantries, and non-profits partnering with schools in Nebraska. The goal is to strengthen the regional and local food hubs supplying school nutrition programs, improve healthy food access, and reduce obesity risk through infrastructure investments, technology, and logistics. Applications must focus on direct or highly ready relationships with schools and may not support food purchases. Request for Applications for the state Rural Health Transformation Program. Submission portal: https://sonvideo.webex.com/sonvideo/j.php?MTID=m3ca85f9199661e908b1ca798e7798708 Total funding available: $80,000.

Approximately five LHDs will receive awards around $470,000 each to improve dental health access in rural communities.

data.summary: This initiative funds implementation of remote patient monitoring technology and programs in Nebraska's critical access hospitals, rural emergency hospitals, regional rural hospitals, and Federally Qualified Health Centers. data.title: Graduate Medical Education (GME) Grant Program, Round VIII (SFY26)
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Hospital Association (NVHA)
data.summary:
The Nevada Graduate Medical Education (GME) Grant Program, Round VIII (SFY26), funds the creation, expansion, or retention of ACGME-accredited medical residency and postdoctoral fellowship programs within Nevada. The goal is to address physician shortages in critical geographic and specialty areas identified through the state's 2025 health workforce analysis. Supported by state general funds and federal RHTP funds (CMS/HHS), the program aims to increase the number of locally trained physicians who are likely to remain in Nevada to practice.

Grants are awarded to institutions for residency or fellowship expansion, new programs, or to prevent loss of accredited positions. Funded projects must directly address provider shortages and align with strategic state needs.

RFA for Nevada Department of Corrections to modernize rural correctional healthcare under RHTP Budget Period 1.

data.title: Public Health Dental Hygiene Teams in Local Health Department RFA
data.issuingAgency: Kentucky Department for Public Health
data.summary: This RFA provides funding for up to five Kentucky Local Health Departments (LHDs) or their authorized contractors to establish or expand Public Health Dental Hygiene (PHDH) teams. Funded teams will deliver preventive oral health services—including school-based, long-term care, and teledentistry-enabled dental hygiene programs—to improve access and outcomes for underserved rural communities. The initiative aims to reduce preventable oral disease, increase rural preventive care access, and promote workforce and technology innovations as part of Kentucky’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Each award is anticipated to be approximately $470,000 for FY2027. Total available funding for similar dental hygiene workforce expansion initiatives across all relevant RHTP programs is up to $9.9 million for FY2026-27 (program-level), but this opportunity is fixed at $470,000 per LHD award.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program 2026: Integrating Community Doulas into Clinical Healthcare Teams in Rural New Jersey
data.issuingAgency: New Jersey Department of Health, Maternal and Child Health Services
data.summary: RHTP RFA (DFHS26RDI) funding integration of community doulas into clinical healthcare teams serving rural New Jersey, issued by NJDOH Maternal and Child Health Services.

data.title: Nevada Rural Veterans Health Transformation
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: The Rural Veteran Health Transformation Request for Applications provides $2,384,094 in federal funds to the Nevada Department of Veterans Services (NDVS) to improve health outcomes for Veterans living in rural Nevada. Supported projects must strengthen rural health systems and address gaps in access to primary care, behavioral health, and coordination with the VA by advancing population health, modernizing health infrastructure, expanding workforce, and implementing health IT solutions. This RFA is issued under the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program, as authorized by H.R. 1 (2025).

data.title: Workforce Retention Grant for Critical Access Hospitals and Clinics (2026)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The North Dakota RHTP Workforce Retention Grant funds projects at Critical Access Hospitals and their owned and operated clinics to promote rural provider retention and workforce stability. Eligible projects must implement measurable strategies addressing retention challenges, including retention bonuses, childcare supports, and professional development. Funding based on CMS-authorized $198.9M state plan; approximately $10M is available in this round, with about 37 awards anticipated.

data.title: Rural Corrections Health Transformation
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: Bolsters and modernizes Nevada’s rural correctional healthcare infrastructure through investments that enhance systems and improve access to care. Supports initiatives in health outcomes, workforce, access, and technology, exclusively for rural populations and correctional sites.

data.title: Nevada Rural Health Systems Flex Fund (RHTP)
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: The Nevada Rural Health System Flex Fund (BP1, Round 1) offers up to $35,986,322 in subawards for projects that modernize, enhance, and expand rural health care infrastructure statewide, including technology, equipment, mobile health units, EMS, renovations/alterations, remote care solutions, and workforce initiatives. Eligible projects address critical gaps and strengthen access and quality for rural, frontier, and tribal populations. Awards are competitive and prioritize measurable outcomes, collaboration, sustainability, and embedded rural partnerships. Infrastructure improvements, capital expenditures, and administrative costs are allowed (admin max 10% of budget; no construction, broadband or indirect costs). Applicants must be Nevada-registered vendors and either serve rural Nevadans directly or demonstrate documented partnerships with rural health providers.
applicantTypes: Organization with partnerships serving rural Nevadans
Non-rural entity (with rural partner MOU/letter of commitment)

data.title: Request For Information: Screening, Brief Intervention, And Referral To Treatment (SBIRT) Training Vendor
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Health Care Authority Behavioral Health Services Division
data.summary: The New Mexico Health Care Authority Behavioral Health Services Division seeks information from qualified vendors to design, develop, and implement a web-based training platform for SBIRT (Screening, Brief Intervention, and Referral to Treatment) in New Mexico. This RFI is to assess vendor capabilities and inform planning for up to $4 million in funding for SBIRT training delivery to eligible providers throughout the state, for State Fiscal Year 2027 (July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027). Statements of Interest will inform future funding and expedited program execution.

data.title: Vermont Rural Health Transformation Fund Grant — Pharmacy Test-to-Treat
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Department of Vermont Health Access (DVHA)
data.summary: Expands pharmacist test-to-treat scope in Vermont, funded from Vermont's $195M Year-1 RHT grant.

data.title: Nebraska RHTP 4.2b: Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) Prevention
data.issuingAgency: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
data.summary: Currently under DHHS review as of the investigation date.

data.title: Mountain State Care Force – Rural Healthcare Apprenticeships (RHTP)
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health
data.summary: The West Virginia Department of Health, through its Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), announces the Mountain State Care Force – Rural Healthcare Apprenticeships funding opportunity (AFA Number: RHT-AFA-04-28-2026-MSC1) for FY 2026. This Year 1 initiative provides $2,000,000 (funded 100% by CMS/HHS) out of the multi-year $200,000,000 RHTP program to expand West Virginia’s rural health workforce. The program will support up to 121 new, entry-level, paid healthcare apprenticeships in rural West Virginia communities, with apprenticeships targeting high-need roles such as EMTs and technicians. Participating apprentices must commit to five years of rural service post-hire. Funding is performance-based and contingent upon meeting employment and retention benchmarks. Grantees must adhere to rigorous reporting and compliance standards, including quarterly programmatic and financial reports. Applicants must demonstrate the capacity to recruit, train, and retain rural health workers, deliver structured apprenticeship training, enforce the service obligation, comply with all reporting, and co-fund apprentice costs as per guidance. Applications must be submitted via the WV OASIS VSS portal by the stated deadline. FAQs will be posted publicly after the question deadline.

data.title: Mountain State Care Force – Early Outreach to Healthcare Careers
data.issuingAgency: Division of Health - Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: The West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is seeking proposals from eligible entities to implement the Mountain State Care Force – Early Outreach & Exposure to Healthcare Careers program. The goal is to engage at least 10,000 high school students statewide in healthcare career pathways through supplemental outreach, student engagement activities, visits to healthcare facilities, and integration with state data systems to track outcomes. Funding is milestone- and performance-based, with a single grantee award of $1,500,000; all funds must be expended by July 31, 2027. Selected applicant must submit a revised line-item budget and narrative shortly after award, provide regular quarterly program reports, and ensure integration with school and healthcare facility partners. Submission is through the WV Oasis Vendor Self Service (VSS) portal. Questions must be submitted by May 5, 2026 to mike.sheets@wv.gov. The award period extends from notification date through July 31, 2027.

data.title: Career Pathway Programs for Clinical Support Roles (HSS-26-075)
data.issuingAgency: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (Office of the Secretary, Delaware Health Care Commission)
data.summary: Delaware RHTP solicitation for non-physician clinical workforce training and career pathway expansion in rural and underserved communities, including support mechanisms described in solicitation appendices.

data.title: RHTP: Career Ladder Advancement Initiative
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health, Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: The West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Career Ladder Advancement Initiative provides $900,000 in one-year funding to expand and advance healthcare career pathways, supporting the career progression of 150 rural healthcare workers across West Virginia. Applicants prioritizing counties with high Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) scores are favored for funding. The initiative requires detailed grant application, line-item budgeting, and compliance with both real-time and milestone-based programmatic and financial reporting under oversight by the West Virginia Department of Health and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). All expenses must be incurred by July 31, 2027, and funded entities are subject to all applicable federal and state requirements outlined in the AFA.

data.title: Technical Assistance Services for RHTP Sub-Awardees
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration
data.summary: Request for Quotes (RFQ) via Florida Department of Management Services (DMS) State Term Contract for technical assistance to support Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) grant sub-awardees in implementation, compliance, and reporting. Responses solicited only from existing STC contract holders under Ch. 287, F.S. as part of a $209 million federal initiative to strengthen healthcare in rural Florida communities.
applicantTypes: Current Florida DMS State Term Contract holders

data.title: RHTP Grant Management Technology Solution
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration
data.summary: Request for Quotes (RFQ) for a Grant Management Technology Solution under the Florida Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The procurement seeks a platform for sub-award administration, expenditure tracking, and deliverable monitoring. Open only to vendors holding a Florida Department of Management Services (DMS) State Term Contract (STC), pursuant to Chapter 287, F.S. The RHTP is a $209 million statewide initiative to strengthen healthcare delivery in rural Florida. The opportunity is part of four distinct RHTP infrastructure procurements announced on April 14, 2026, and responses are solicited only from current STC vendors.
applicantTypes: Limited to prequalified State Term Contract holders

data.title: Train In Place Rural Healthcare Workforce Credentialing
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS)
data.summary: Supports existing rural healthcare workforce in North Dakota in obtaining new credentials, enhancing competencies, or completing approved training programs while remaining embedded in their rural communities. The program covers planning and development of train-in-place models during the first year, with individual skill-building awards available. Participation in credentialing programs requires a five-year service commitment. The initiative is part of North Dakota's Rural Health Transformation program, focused on stabilizing and strengthening the rural health workforce.

data.title: Maryland RHTP Pillar 3 – Empower Rural Marylanders to Eat for Health
data.issuingAgency: Rural Maryland Council
data.summary: This grant opportunity supports the creation and expansion of food system aggregation and hubs and promotes local foods purchasing strategies to advance dietary health for rural Marylanders. Funding is provided under the Maryland RHTP (Pillar 3), emphasizing regional coordination, infrastructure, and healthy food distribution in rural Maryland communities.

data.title: Expand Rural Health Care Rotations Initiative
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: Embeds new learner types (students, residents) into rural communities by expanding rural rotation programs. At least 50% of training must occur in rural or tribal communities. One application per organization. Five-year service commitment applies when housing support or individual awards are offered. Posted April 30, 2026, deadline May 15, 2026.

data.title: Nevada Federal RHTP Award (FY2026-FY2030)
data.issuingAgency: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
data.summary: Federal RHTP state award baseline derived from CMS 50-state spotlights.

data.title: Provider Apprenticeship and Training RFA
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary:
Funds provider apprenticeship and structured training pipeline initiatives to expand healthcare workforce serving rural Nevada. Supports project costs including faculty, stipends, housing, equipment, and instructional materials. Priority goes to applicants with rural partnerships and evidence of documented provider gaps.

Funds for rural training pipelines, high school-to-career pathways, and initiatives to increase retention, reduce burnout, and build local allied health and non-physician provider workforce in rural areas. Projects may include local training partnerships, apprenticeships, and career ladder development.

Funds provider training and rural health care apprenticeship programs.

data.title: 2026 Delta Workforce Grant Program
data.issuingAgency: Delta Regional Authority (DRA), administered in Alabama by Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: The 2026 Delta Workforce Grant Program offers $4 million in project grants to support workforce education and training initiatives across the lower Mississippi River Delta and Alabama Black Belt regions, with a focus on distressed counties. The program aims to expand opportunities for recruiting, training, and retaining a local and diverse workforce, align workforce and economic development strategies, build talent pipelines, and promote sector-based partnerships. Special priority is given to projects serving regional needs and demonstrating economic impact in distressed Alabama counties.

data.title: Indiana RHTP07 Teleconsult and Telehealth Landscape Assessment
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Administration (IDOA) on behalf of Indiana Department of Health (IDOH)
data.summary: RFP 26-87449 (RHTP07) sought a respondent to conduct a comprehensive, statewide landscape assessment of telehealth (provider-to-patient) and teleconsultation (provider-to-provider) services to inform strategic planning, investment, and sustainability under Indiana's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), Initiative 8: Growing Telehealth Access and Infrastructure. Findings from this assessment will support phased telehealth deployment and funding decisions across Indiana’s rural communities. Laurel Health Advisors LLC was named as the recommended awardee on June 3, 2026, with the award conditioned upon contract finalization with the state within 45 calendar days. The selection followed a multi-stage RFP process with technical, business, and cost criteria, including significant subcontracting to certified MBE, WBE, and IVOSB partners. The awarded contract is valued at $860,088 over five years.

data.title: MT RHTP Center of Excellence: Strategy and Analytics Contractor RFP
data.issuingAgency: Montana DPHHS
data.summary: Contractor sought for: data-driven strategy analysis of rural health supply/demand, long-term sustainability roadmaps for rural facilities, and performance incentive program administration for Montana's RHTP Center of Excellence.

data.title: Nevada WRRAP – Provider Recruitment and Retention Program
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: This Request for Applications (RFA) for the Nevada Workforce Recruitment & Rural Access Program (WRRAP) under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) seeks to support rural hospitals, clinics, and healthcare providers in Nevada to recruit and retain new primary and preventative healthcare providers, addressing rural health workforce gaps. Funding is offered on a competitive, tiered basis, focused on primary, specialty, and preventive services in rural areas. Projects should address priority needs such as provider shortages in hospitals and clinics, provider training, and rural specialty care. BP1 (Budget Period 1) runs from December 29, 2025, through October 30, 2026, with funds required to be expended by September 30, 2027. No cost sharing or match is required. Total competitive funding for BP1 is $32,387,689, to be awarded in multiple rounds if necessary. Funding result announced July 29, 2026: NVHA awarded $32.3 million for provider recruitment and retention, supporting primary care, pediatric, behavioral health, OB/GYN, orthopedic, and family medicine capacity across rural and Tribal communities.

data.title: Nevada Workforce Recruitment & Rural Access Program (WRRAP) Provider Apprenticeship and Training Program
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: This RFA, part of Nevada's Rural Health Transformation Program, supports apprenticeship and training pathways to increase rural healthcare workforce capacity, focusing on specialty and subspecialty provider recruitment and retention for rural, frontier, and tribal Nevada. Tiered funding is available for small to regional projects targeting provider shortages, with priority to proposals benefitting rural and frontier health infrastructure. Funding result announced July 29, 2026: NVHA awarded $14.3 million for rural apprenticeships and training, including simulation centers, nursing and EMT pathways, laboratory science, imaging, behavioral health, dental assisting, public health, and K–12 career pipelines.
applicantTypes: Out-of-state Health Organizations serving rural NV

data.title: Distressed Hospital Small Grant Program
data.issuingAgency: California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI)
data.summary: The Distressed Hospital Small Grant Program offers $25 million in funding to not-for-profit and public hospitals in California facing immediate and extreme financial distress. Eligible hospitals may apply for cashflow grants intended to help maintain operational continuity and prevent closure. Applications must demonstrate financial need and detail plans for regaining financial viability.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program – Program Evaluator
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Administration (IDOA), on behalf of Indiana Department of Health and Indiana Family and Social Services Administration
data.summary: The Indiana Department of Administration, on behalf of the Indiana Department of Health and Indiana Family and Social Services Administration, solicited proposals for an independent Program Evaluator for the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The evaluator will perform annual and final reports to assess program outcomes and impact of activities funded by a $206,927,896.80 CMS/HHS award over a five-year period. Scope and deliverables are updated in Addendum #1, including reporting modifications. MWBE and IVOSB subcontractor participation is required in accordance with Indiana state goals and must be documented on the State of Indiana MWBE/IVOSB registry. All respondent eligibility must be met per state registration requirements before award.
applicantTypes: Other entities with relevant program evaluation capacity

data.title: NC Mobile Integrated Health (MIH) and Community Paramedicine Program Grant
data.issuingAgency: NC Office of Emergency Medical Services (NC OEMS)
data.summary: The NC Mobile Integrated Health (MIH) and Community Paramedicine (CP) Grant, administered by the NC Office of Emergency Medical Services, funds licensed NC EMS agencies that provide primary 911 response in rural areas (≤750 people/sq. mile with limited healthcare access). The program supports establishing or expanding MIH/CP programs with an emphasis on behavioral health crisis response, SUD/MOUD treatment access, and reducing emergency department utilization for mental health and substance use crises. Fundable activities in Year 1 include personnel, equipment, program infrastructure, expanded treatment access, behavioral health crisis response, care coordination, and workforce training. Total pool: $10,000,000; estimated 50–100 awards of $75,000–$200,000 (Year 1). Continuation funding in Years 2–5 is contingent on performance.

data.title: AHS Rural Health Grant Management Solution
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services
data.summary: A sealed-bid RFP to develop a grant management solution for Vermont's Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program, issued by the Vermont Agency of Human Services (AHS) via the Agency of Digital Services. The solution supports administration and tracking of RHT Program grants.

data.title: MT RHTP Center of Excellence: Implementation Partner RFP
data.issuingAgency: Montana DPHHS
data.summary: Implementation partner sought to provide hands-on technical expertise and change management resources tailored to each Montana rural community's unique circumstances for RHTP Center of Excellence operations.

data.title: South Dakota Rural Strong Grant
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health (DOH)
data.summary: South Dakota Rural Strong Grant (RFP# 26-09RHT-001), part of the state's Rural Health Transformation Program. The South Dakota Department of Health launched Rural Strong Grants for health care providers, awarding up to $31,750,000 in the first budget period. Eligible applicants include hospitals, FQHCs, RHCs, Tribal 638 clinics, behavioral and dental clinics enrolled with Medicaid. Allowable fund uses include expansion, infrastructure, strategic partnerships, care coordination, minor renovations (excluding new construction or major remodeling), and workforce support. Awarded $31.5M to 28 of 79 applicants (announced 7/23/2026).

data.title: Make North Dakota Healthy Again: Community-Based Walking Program
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS) - Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: Eight-plus week community walking program designed for rural North Dakota communities under the Make North Dakota Healthy Again pillar of the RHTP. Participants commit to regular walking with recorded steps, and each community must host at least one group walk per week. Allowable expenses include purchasing step trackers and physical logs. Funding opportunity aims to promote preventive care and support healthy lifestyles in rural communities.

data.title: Zero-Hour Physical Education (PE) Grant for Rural and Tribal Schools
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: Funding for before-school fitness programs (Zero-Hour PE) for rural and tribal public and private schools, regional education associations, and school consortiums in North Dakota. Applicants must include seven required program components supporting healthy living and preventive care. Targets middle, junior, and high school students, including adaptive PE options. Part of North Dakota’s Rural Health Transformation initiative to promote preventive care and healthy living. Posted April 22, 2026.

data.title: Community-Based Organization Enrollment and Education Facilitator Grants
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority, Consumer Health Services Division
data.summary: This competitive, state-funded grant program aims to expand Medicaid and Marketplace (Nevada Health Link, Public Option/Battle Born State Plans) enrollment assistance by increasing the number of Exchange Enrollment Facilitator (EEF) positions within Nevada community-based organizations. Supported activities include education, compliance, and outreach with an intensive rural focus.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program: Community Gardens Grant
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services is offering $300,000 in federal RHTP funding for rural and tribal community garden projects. The grant opportunity is designed to improve nutrition, wellness, and community collaboration statewide through evidence-based practices and a six-component model for sustainable gardens. Allowable costs include items such as raised garden beds, small storage sheds (not on foundation), minor ADA-accessible improvements, and equipment. Hard-scape paths and any construction that increases property value are unallowable. Approximately ten awards of $30,000 each are expected. Eligible applicants include rural and tribal schools, civic groups, municipalities, health care facilities, parks and recreation entities, public health units, nonprofit organizations, and a range of other community-based entities. The program operates under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), funded by CMS.
applicantTypes: Boys and Girls Clubs of America

data.title: Evaluation Services for Rural Health Transformation Grant (RFP 2026-001) – New Hampshire
data.issuingAgency: GO-NORTH
data.summary: The New Hampshire Governor’s Office of New Opportunities & Rural Transformational Health (GO-NORTH) seeks proposals for independent evaluation services supporting the state’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), funded via CMS Assistance Listing 93.798. The selected vendor will assess implementation, impact, and sustainability of all funded RHTP initiatives. Key tasks include: designing and executing an evaluation plan, collecting and analyzing quantitative and qualitative data, engaging with contracted Hubs and subrecipients, supporting federal/state reporting requirements, and communicating results to GO-NORTH, CMS, and stakeholders. Deliverables include evaluation plans, quarterly and annual reports, mid-course recommendations, performance measurement tools, and ongoing technical engagement with partners. The contract is funded up to $25,000,000. The period of performance commences upon Governor & Council approval through September 30, 2031, with a potential one-year extension at state discretion. All activities must comply with 2 CFR Part 200 and applicable state and federal requirements.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program – Technical Assistance for Health Information Technology
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health
data.summary: This RFP from the Minnesota Department of Health solicits proposals from external vendors to provide technical assistance to rural health care providers and subgrantees participating in Minnesota’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Technical assistance providers will support Health Information Technology (HIT) system assessment, planning, implementation, and sustainability activities for rural hospitals, clinics, federally qualified health centers, tribal organizations, and related subgrantees. The contract will include HIT advisory reviews, conflict-of-interest monitoring, and strategic guidance to support effective rural HIT adoption. Estimated 125-150 provider organizations are anticipated to participate annually. Award amount for advisory services is up to $900,000 in the first round. This is NOT a grant to rural providers, but a technical assistance/vendor opportunity for FY2026-2027.
applicantTypes: Business Owned by Persons with Disabilities

data.title: Rightsizing Health Care Delivery Systems for the Future: Rural Federally Qualified Health Centers and Critical Access Hospitals
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services: Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services, through the Rural Health Transformation Program, offers competitive funding for rural Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) to receive technical assistance and comprehensive financial and operational assessments. The opportunity supports efforts to rightsize infrastructure and care delivery models for future sustainability. Up to 42 awards of $40,000 each are expected, and selected participants will receive assistance from the preferred TA vendor Eide Bailly in year one. Program includes market share analysis, productivity assessment, operational consulting, and development of an action plan for right-sizing services and infrastructure.

data.title: SmartCare Catalyst Provider Productivity Support Fund
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: This opportunity provides up to $29,500,000 in competitive grants under the West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) – SmartCare Catalyst Provider Productivity Support Fund (PPSF) for FY2026-2027. The PPSF aims to drive statewide modernization for value-based care among rural hospitals, clinics, and stand-alone provider offices in West Virginia. Funding supports operational transformation, technology investment, service restructuring, and development of shared service collaboratives. Applicants must detail how proposed activities will reduce provider burden, improve productivity, achieve cost reduction, and promote health system sustainability. Required submissions include a completed application, Detailed Line-Item Budget (DLIB), budget narrative, and Grantee Contact Information Form. Applicants must comply with all program requirements, reporting, and performance measures as outlined in the official guidance. All questions must be submitted via the AFA Q&A Form within five business days of posting. Final applications must be submitted via the WV Oasis Vendor Self Service Portal by the stated deadline. Funding is 100% from CMS/HHS. Contact for program questions: Mike Sheets (mike.sheets@wv.gov, 681-542-4971); contract/buyer: William M Sheets (681-542-4971).

data.title: ROOTS (Rural Opportunities for Optimal Transformation in Students' Health) — Year 1
data.issuingAgency: Oklahoma State Department of Education (OSDE)
data.summary: OSDE's ROOTS Competitive Grant (Rural Opportunities for Optimal Transformation in Students' Health), provided under an RHTP subaward for the Presidential Fitness Test Preparation program. Year 1: a 6-month grant running May–October 2026, for 60 rural PK–12 schools. Schools receive professional development, mentoring, and up to $10,000 for approved equipment, contingent on completing required activities (trainings, coaching sessions, collaborative learning opportunities). Response period has closed.

data.title: Minnesota Rural Health Transformation Program Grants – Tribal Nations
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: Minnesota Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) provides up to $193,090,618.14 in federal funds (100% CMS/HHS funded) as formula-based, non-competitive grants to eligible rural Tribal Nations for transformation initiatives addressing rural health care access, quality improvement, workforce development, technology-enabled care, chronic disease, and provider financial sustainability. Applications are accepted via ORHPC Online Grants Portal on a rolling basis within posted deadlines. No cost share or match required. Approximately 2% of Minnesota’s total RHTP award is allocated to Tribal Nations. Five-year period of performance from award date. Required reporting and compliance with CMS/HHS grant conditions mandatory.

data.title: Minnesota RHTP Grants – Rural Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) and Community Mental Health Centers (CMHCs)
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: Minnesota has been awarded approximately $193 million from CMS/HHS under the Rural Health Transformation Program to support innovative, sustainable, and equitable rural care models. This non-competitive, formula-based grant opportunity is for rural Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) and Community Mental Health Centers (CMHCs) in Minnesota, supporting behavioral health, workforce development, care innovation, and health equity. Up to 16 entities are expected to be eligible. Application is rolling until the deadline.

data.title: Minnesota RHTP Grants – Rural Federally Qualified Health Centers
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: Minnesota was awarded $193 million in federal RHTP funds for FFY2026 to support transformation of rural health care. This opportunity supports Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) in rural areas via formula-based, non-competitive grants. The program aims to improve population health and access, address workforce shortages, invest in partnerships and technology, and stabilize rural providers. Sub-awards to FQHCs are formula-based, with up to $1.9 million per entity in year 1 and continued amendments in future years pending federal awards.

data.title: Minnesota Rural Health Transformation Program Grants – Rural Hospitals
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: The Minnesota Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Grants provide $193,090,618.14 in formula-based, non-competitive funding for eligible rural hospitals in Minnesota. The program, funded 100% by CMS/HHS, supports activities that improve access, quality, and the rural health workforce, and hospitals must address at least two of five designated strategic RHTP initiatives. Approximately 70% of the award is distributed to rural hospitals; other eligible providers include Tribal Nations, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs), and Community Mental Health Centers (CMHCs).

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Catalyst Awards
data.issuingAgency: Oregon Health Authority (OHA)
data.summary: The Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Catalyst Awards support community-driven, ready-to-implement projects with the goal of transforming rural health systems in Oregon. Up to 80 awards are available for projects aligned with five key initiatives: regional partnerships and system transformation, healthy communities and prevention, workforce capacity and resilience, technology and data modernization, and tribal health initiatives. Eligible applicants include rural clinics, hospitals, critical access hospitals, training facilities, tribal health systems, and other qualifying rural entities serving priority populations such as maternal and child health, behavioral health, aging, and chronic disease. Funded projects must address rural needs, demonstrate innovation and sustainability, and align with RHTP's overarching system transformation goals. The program is funded via a federal cooperative agreement and managed by the Oregon Health Authority in partnership with CMS.
applicantTypes: Other eligible rural entities as specified in RFGP

data.title: Rooted and Resilient Rural Maryland: Transformation through Sustainable Access, Innovative Care, and Tech Innovation RFA
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC)
data.summary: Flagship competitive RFA under Maryland RHTP Pillar 2 combining three Transformation Funds (Sustainable Access through Service Expansion and HIT Advances; Behavioral Health Service Expansion; and Innovative Care) into a unified opportunity. Funding will support innovative, sustainable projects to expand access, implement advanced care models, and leverage technology for rural health improvement throughout Maryland. Eligible projects must address transformative change aligning with CMS principles of choice and competition. Approximately $73 million is anticipated for awards under this RFA in Budget Period 1, as part of a broader multi-year program aiming for significant transformational impact in rural health.

data.title: Minnesota RHTP: Identifying Performance Measures for Rural Health Transformation Program Health Information Technology Investments (Quick Call for Proposals)
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health (MDH)
data.summary: Quick Call for Proposals to secure a vendor to develop a comprehensive performance measurement framework for Health Information Technology (HIT) investments under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The selected contractor will review RHTP-funded technology-related activities and CMS reporting requirements, meet with MDH to clarify project details, and deliver a framework to guide how rural health providers’ use of federally funded technology is measured and tied to care improvements, with a strong focus on value-based care readiness. The maximum budget for this project is $25,000.

data.title: Rural Texas Strong Program – Initiative 4: The Next Generation of the Small Town Doctor and Team
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: The Rural Texas Strong Program – Initiative 4 supports eligible rural healthcare providers across Texas by enabling recruitment, training, and retention of healthcare professionals. Funds are used to build local education and workforce pipelines and deliver personnel retention strategies, with an emphasis on behavioral health needs and care team resilience. Program funding is statewide and no cost share/match is required.

data.title: Vermont Insurance Marketplace Affordability Strategies: Technical and Actuarial Assistance
data.issuingAgency: Department of Vermont Health Access
data.summary: The Department of Vermont Health Access and Agency of Human Services seek technical and actuarial assistance to support Vermont Insurance Marketplace Affordability Strategies. The successful vendor(s) will conduct a statewide policy assessment, advance strategies for improved access and affordability, prepare and negotiate federal waivers and applications, and provide subject matter expertise and ongoing technical assistance for program design and implementation. This is part of Vermont's $195 million RHT grant supporting a five-year rural health transformation effort.

data.title: ASO Services for Rural and Behavioral Health Program Administration
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Health Care Authority (HCA)
data.summary: The New Mexico Health Care Authority (HCA) seeks proposals from qualified Administrative Services Organizations (ASOs) for the administration and operational support of state RHT (RHTP) and behavioral health reform (SB3) programs. Services include fiscal management, compliance, and data/reporting functions. Multiple domains and multiple contract awards are possible. The contract may start July 1, 2026, or later, with option for renewal. No explicit funding floor or ceiling is stated; applicants must submit detailed cost proposals for each domain. Proposals must be submitted electronically through the Submittable portal. Questions can be sent to the Procurement Manager by May 16, 2026; the deadline for proposals is May 28, 2026.
applicantTypes: Entities with Rural/Behavioral Health Administration Experience

data.title: Mountain State Care Force Rural Provider Upskilling & Mentorships
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Division of Health
data.summary: West Virginia RHTP AFA RHT-AFA-05-13-2026-MSC1 / GFO-0506-2600000000246-2 sought a grantee to provide ongoing virtual case-based clinical training and mentorship to rural providers under Mountain State Care Force, expanding specialty support and applied learning access.
applicantTypes: Eligible entities able to deliver statewide provider training

data.title: Behavioral Health Promotion Community Grants
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services (NDHHS)
data.summary: Supports creative, evidence-based proposals for behavioral health promotion, with strategies focused on mental health, suicide prevention, and substance use/misuse prevention. Projects target populations not yet identified as needing treatment. Application via Qualtrics required. This program is part of North Dakota's five-year Rural Health Transformation Program, designed to strengthen rural health workforce, promote preventive care, bring high-quality care closer to home, and connect technology, data, and providers.

data.title: Recovery-Focused Clubhouse Grant Program
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary:
The Recovery-Focused Clubhouse Grant Program provides funding to eligible organizations to operate or expand Clubhouse Programs for adults living with mental health challenges in Texas Public Health Regions 2 and 4, following evidence-based standards (Clubhouse International model) to promote recovery, employment, education, and community integration. Approximately $2.48 million is available over four years, with a 25% required cost share. The program aims to enhance recovery-based outreach, services, and programming for individuals with mental illness.

Expands Recovery-Focused Clubhouse programs in Texas, supporting evidence-based peer environments for adults with mental health challenges. Funds operations, expansion, and sustainability in specified regions and counties, with strong emphasis on fidelity to Clubhouse International standards.

Supports expansion of Clubhouse programs for adults living with mental health challenges in specified Texas regions. Funded organizations must operate programs according to Clubhouse International standards, providing recovery-focused, peer-based services, employment, education, and housing supports.

The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) seeks applications for the Rural Texas Strong Initiative 4: The Next Generation of the Small Town Doctor and Team. This program assists eligible rural healthcare providers in recruiting and training healthcare professionals by building education and training pipelines, and developing retention strategies for providers practicing in rural areas. Funding supports workforce shortage initiatives, local partnerships, scholarships, and sustainable collaborations with academic institutions.

Provides up to $725,000 per award to eligible rural healthcare entities for projects to recruit, train, and retain healthcare professionals in rural Texas. Supported activities include building high school health career paths, scholarships, relocation bonuses, and residency/fellowship programs. Retention activities may also be supported.

This grant opportunity from HHSC supports rural healthcare providers in Texas to recruit, train, and retain healthcare professionals by building local education/training pipelines and implementing retention strategies. Eligible projects include career path development for local students, scholarships to recent graduates (with 5-year rural service commitment), relocation/signing bonuses, and creation of rural residency/fellowship programs. The goal is to address rural workforce shortages and strengthen the next generation of healthcare professionals in small towns across Texas.

The Rural Texas Strong Initiative 4 seeks to fund eligible rural healthcare providers to recruit and train healthcare professionals in rural Texas communities. The program supports building local education and training pipelines, scholarships, recruitment bonuses, and the creation of new residency or fellowship programs to address persistent workforce shortages. Applicants can propose projects using at least one of four approaches: student career path development, scholarships, relocation/signing bonuses, or new training partnerships with academic institutions.
applicantTypes: Organizations eligible for business in Texas
Entities eligible to conduct business in Texas

data.title: Colorado Rural Health Center Technical Assistance and Analytics Support
data.issuingAgency: Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF)
data.summary: Colorado Rural Health Center (CRHC) is contracted to deliver statewide technical assistance and analytics support to Rural Health Clinics (RHCs) and Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs). This sole source contract aims to improve health data interoperability and technology adoption for enhanced, data-driven rural patient care. Services leverage analytics and Health Information Exchange (HIE), including CCMCN’s Rural Analytics Platform. Contract runs through June 2031 under a $6.45 million budget and is managed by HCPF.

data.title: Ensuring Safety Net Service Delivery Initiative
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services is launching a competitive RHTP funding opportunity to fill rural behavioral health and safety net service gaps through technical assistance, infrastructure development, equipment, and telehealth expansion. Approximately $15 million in federal funds is available in year one, with about 50 awards expected. Funded projects must serve primarily rural or tribal North Dakota citizens and demonstrate measurable, sustainable improvements in health care access and outcomes.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program Technical Assistance for Ensuring Safety Net Service Delivery Funding Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS)
data.summary: The Ensuring Safety Net Service Delivery funding opportunity, under North Dakota’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), provides up to $15 million in competitive grant funding to rural and tribal health providers and partners to address critical service delivery gaps and improve health and behavioral health outcomes for rural and tribal Medicaid members and other residents across North Dakota. This opportunity, announced May 8, 2026, anticipates approximately 50 awards for projects that may include: expanding access to essential health and behavioral health services, enhancing workforce development, strengthening healthcare infrastructure, deploying telehealth solutions, procuring equipment, conducting limited facility renovations (with costs capped at 20% of a project's total budget), planning, training, and related capacity-building activities. Eligible applicants must directly benefit rural or tribal North Dakota residents. Administrative expenses are capped at 10% of the budget, provider payments at 15%, and renovation/alteration costs at 20%. Unallowable costs include construction, meals/food, and supplanting existing funding. All activities and costs must comply with relevant ND HHS and federal requirements (including 2 CFR Part 200 and 300). Rural/urban eligibility definitions and application requirements are clarified in the primary NOFO, with urban entities eligible only if their application targets rural beneficiaries or rural use of funds. Applicants must articulate measurable and sustainable health improvements, especially for Medicaid members, and applications must be submitted via the Qualtrics portal using all required templates by the published deadline.

data.title: Nevada Rural Tribal Health System Transformation Program
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: Supports improvements to tribal health systems in rural Nevada through community-led, sustainable projects targeting health infrastructure, innovation, and workforce. Eligible applicants are the 28 federally recognized Tribal Nations, Bands, and Councils within Nevada, aiming to complement the state’s Rural Health Transformation Plan. Awards are competitive and focus on strengthening healthcare systems, access to care, and innovative solutions for tribal communities.

data.title: New Hampshire RHTP: Youth Engagement Programs in Healthcare & Allied Health Careers
data.issuingAgency: USNH Rural Health Transformation HUB (University System of New Hampshire)
data.summary: Invites applications from organizations to implement/expand youth engagement programs building interest in healthcare/allied-health careers, rural focus. Funding amount and exact due date could not be independently confirmed in the original investigation.

data.title: Delaware Rural 'Hope Center' Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS)
data.summary: Funds two new Rural Hope Centers in Kent and Sussex Counties, modeled after New Castle County’s homeless-integrated-care hub, to address rural health disparities and workforce shortages. The initiative prioritizes technological innovation, value-based care, and data tracking, with milestones for site acquisition and operational launch. Award is via direct agreement and not a competitive RFP.

data.title: Maryland RHTP: Revenue Cycle Management and Billing Technical Assistance (Pillar 2)
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Health (Office of Population Health Improvement) & HSCRC
data.summary: This RFA provides funding and technical assistance to rural local health departments and area agencies on aging in Maryland. Focus is on enhancing efficiency in revenue cycle management and billing as part of Maryland’s RHTP Pillar 2, which promotes sustainable access and innovative care. Partners include the MD Department of Health and HSCRC.

data.title: Kentucky Rural Community Hubs for Chronic Care Innovation — Lead Organization RFA
data.issuingAgency: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services (CHFS)
data.summary: Funding for a Rural Community Hub Lead Organization in the Big Sandy, Lake Cumberland, or Purchase Area Development Districts. The Foundation for a Healthy Kentucky partners with the state to coordinate community efforts addressing prevention and management of chronic conditions, with an initial focus on diabetes and obesity. 100% funded by CMS as part of Kentucky's RHTP award ($212.9M budget year 1, FY2026-FY2030).

data.title: Rural Health Centers and Critical Access Hospitals Support Program
data.issuingAgency: Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF) - Executive Director's Office
data.summary: This funding opportunity supports Rural Health Centers and Critical Access Hospitals in Colorado. Issued by the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF), the sole source solicitation NPSS1-UHAA-2026000220-1 seeks personal services proposals supporting rural health infrastructure.

data.title: Pennsylvania Rural Health Transformation Plan Rapid Response Stabilization Payments
data.issuingAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (DHS)
data.summary: $25 million direct payment program from the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (DHS) to stabilize or enhance rural health care access. Supports hospitals and rural health facilities with one-time payments ranging from $10,000–$1 million per applicant. Aligned with six RHTP initiatives: Aging and Access, Behavioral Health, EMS and Transportation, Maternal Health, Technology and Infrastructure, and Workforce.

data.title: Rural Health Care Workforce Incentive and Sustainability Model – SNAP E&T Third-Party Partner Capacity-Building Grants
data.issuingAgency: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Economic Assistance
data.summary: Provides grants to establish or expand SNAP Employment & Training (E&T) Third-Party Partners focused on developing health care career pathways in rural, frontier, tribal, and other high-need Nebraska communities. Funding supports organizational capacity building to prepare for ongoing operation using the SNAP E&T 50/50 reimbursement model.
