Applicants must serve eligible Nebraska communities and demonstrate plans for sustainability, employer engagement, and compliance with SNAP E&T regulations.

data.title: RHTP: Wellness Within Reach Initiative
data.issuingAgency: South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (SCDHHS) is launching the Rural Health Transformation Program: Wellness Within Reach Initiative, making $27.7M available via subawards to rural-serving organizations. The initiative focuses on deploying mobile health units and crisis response teams, and expanding community care sites to improve healthcare access, quality, and outcomes in rural areas. Eligible applicants must serve rural SC communities and demonstrate measurable impact for rural residents.

data.title: Maryland Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP): Grant Funding to Expand Primary Care Access in Rural Maryland
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Health Care Commission
data.summary: The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) is offering $6.3 million in Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) grant funding to establish and expand advanced primary care access in Maryland’s 18 designated rural counties. Up to 15 grants of up to $1.6 million each will support readiness, infrastructure, workforce, technology, and operational investments for team-based, whole-person primary care, including integration of behavioral health and social needs navigation. The program seeks to reduce avoidable hospital utilization, improve population health outcomes, and enable rural providers to adopt value-based payment models.
applicantTypes: Health Care Providers (established or new primary care practices)

data.title: Nevada Rural Presidential Fitness Test Implementation
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: Funds implementation of a rural health initiative tied to the Presidential Fitness program in Nevada. Supports community-based health promotion and physical wellness programs in rural areas.

data.title: RHTP: Shoring Up to Sustainability Initiative
data.issuingAgency: South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (SCDHHS) is accepting applications for the FY2026 RHTP: Shoring Up to Sustainability Initiative. Funded with $40,000,000 from a federal cooperative agreement, the initiative supports rural-serving healthcare providers and organizations through three project tracks: facility infrastructure enhancements, masterclass workforce training, and healthcare workforce recruitment/retention incentives. The program aims to build the sustainability and resilience of South Carolina’s rural healthcare delivery system.

data.title: Leveling Up Initiative - Chronic Disease Program Expansion
data.issuingAgency: South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary:
Supports programs expanding chronic disease management in rural SC, focusing on diabetes, hypertension, sickle cell, and similar conditions. Provides funding to scale specialty care, implement tele-specialty and education initiatives, and train providers to improve coordinated care and outcomes in underserved rural areas.

Funds expansion of chronic disease management initiatives to improve health outcomes for rural populations. Supports innovative models and partnerships for chronic care.

data.title: Connections to Care – Expand Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) & Assistive Technology
data.issuingAgency: South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary:
Funds are available for deploying RPM devices for maternal care and chronic diseases, establishing centralized monitoring hubs, staff training, integration of RPM data into EHRs, and implementing assistive technologies for individuals with developmental disabilities in rural communities.

This opportunity funds modernization of health IT infrastructure and expansion of remote patient monitoring and assistive technology for rural healthcare providers, aiming to improve access and outcomes through system upgrades, telehealth, and digital tools.

Funds deployment of remote patient monitoring technologies and assistive devices for individuals with chronic conditions and developmental disabilities in rural SC. Supports centralized monitoring, EHR integration, and staff training. Request for Applications for the state RHTP. Submission portal: https://www.scdhhs.gov/resources/grants. Total funding available: $5,000,000.
applicantTypes: Provider for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities

data.title: Connections to Care – Modernize Health IT
data.issuingAgency: South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary:
This opportunity funds projects to modernize health IT infrastructure for rural healthcare providers through certified EHR platforms, interoperability upgrades, cybersecurity improvements, patient-facing digital tools, and advanced analytics. Applicants must demonstrate measurable impact for rural residents.

Supports modernizing health IT systems and infrastructure for rural healthcare providers in SC, including system transitions, upgrades for interoperability/cybersecurity/AI, and patient-facing digital platforms. Request for Applications for the state RHTP. Submission portal: https://www.scdhhs.gov/resources/grants. Total funding available: $2,000,000.
applicantTypes: Provider for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities

data.title: RHT Enhancing Sustainable EMS: Regional Hub Development and Oversight
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board
data.summary: The South Dakota Department of Health (DOH), under the Rural Health Transformation (RHT) initiative, is seeking qualified organizations to support the development and oversight of Regional EMS Hub models to improve coordination, resource sharing, and EMS system performance statewide. Up to $8,000,000 is available under the RHT Enhancing Sustainable EMS initiative for strategic planning, technical assistance, and implementation support. The contractor will work closely with DOH and must meet all requirements outlined in the RFP, including ongoing oversight activities, regional collaboration, and system sustainability, prioritizing rural, frontier, and Tribal communities.

data.title: South Dakota Integrated Behavioral Health System via CCBHC Certification and Collaborative Care Expansion
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Education, Division of Special Education and Early Learning
data.summary: South Dakota seeks a qualified vendor to deliver professional services supporting statewide implementation of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) and Collaborative Care Models. The program focuses on provider and workforce capacity building, crisis and telehealth infrastructure expansion, payment system transformation, and technology/data infrastructure development. Services include technical assistance to behavioral health and primary care organizations, training, crisis response and stabilization infrastructure, support for payment and billing systems, and modernization of data systems to improve access and quality of care for rural and frontier populations.

data.title: Project ECHO for Maternal and Behavioral Health (Rural Health Transformation Program)
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: The Minnesota Department of Health Office of Rural Health and Primary Care is soliciting applications for Project ECHO programming focused on maternal and behavioral health for rural clinicians and medically underserved communities across Minnesota. This initiative, funded 100% by CMS/HHS, seeks to expand rural provider education and capacity through virtual, case-based sessions (12–24 sessions per grantee, monthly), with an emphasis on health equity, network-building, and workforce development. Partnerships with Tribal Nations and organizations serving underserved rural communities are encouraged.

data.title: Statewide Rural Healthcare Assessment
data.issuingAgency: Mississippi State Department of Health (MSDH)
data.summary: MSDH seeks vendors to conduct a comprehensive statewide rural healthcare assessment to support the Mississippi Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). This assessment will inform capital investments, care gap closure, and long-term strategic improvements for rural access, capacity, and sustainability. Proposals must align with state and CMS priorities and be submitted electronically via the OpenGov portal.

data.title: The Rural Texas Strong Program – Initiative 1 (Part 2): Make Rural Texans Healthy Again
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: The Rural Texas Strong Program – Initiative 1 (Part 2): Make Rural Texans Healthy Again provides grant funding to eligible rural Texas hospitals to enhance or create community-based prevention, wellness, and nutrition programs. Funded activities must implement at least one of eight authorized project methods—such as diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular or chronic respiratory disease management, wellness centers, after-hours clinics, and transportation support—to improve rural health outcomes. The goal is to improve prevention, management, and wellness in rural communities and to build long-term sustainability for rural health systems. No matching funds are required. Project details, eligibility, and requirements are set forth in Section II of RFA HHS0017223: https://hhsgrant.my.site.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068cr00000nzTk2AAE.

data.title: Comprehensive State Health Plan
data.issuingAgency: Mississippi State Department of Health
data.summary: Mississippi State Department of Health (MSDH) is soliciting sealed proposals (RFx 3180002944) from qualified vendors for the development and publication of the Mississippi Comprehensive State Health Plan (MCSHP). The resulting data-driven statewide plan will provide an assessment of health status, healthcare system capacity, and future needs in Mississippi. Key deliverables require a rural health system assessment, review and recommendations regarding Certificate of Need (CON) plan components, multi-sector stakeholder engagement, and a final statewide health planning framework to inform policy, system investment, and alignment with CMS and federal objectives.

data.title: Center for Rural Health Sustainability & Innovation (CRHSI) RFP – New Mexico RHTP
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Health Care Authority (HCA)
data.summary: The New Mexico Health Care Authority (HCA) is soliciting competitive, sealed proposals to establish and operate the Center for Rural Health Sustainability & Innovation (CRHSI), supporting the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) with statewide technical assistance, education, partnership development, operational support, policy advocacy, and data analytics to benefit rural, frontier, and tribal healthcare. The contract is contingent upon federal CMS RHTP funding, with an estimated annual award of $3–$6 million (subject to HCA allocation). Only a single award will be issued, subcontracting allowed, and the Center will not act as a fiscal intermediary or payment processor unless specifically authorized. The initial period of performance may begin as early as August 1, 2026. Applicants must comply with federal and state procurement requirements. CRHSI aims to strengthen the sustainability and innovation of New Mexico's rural health infrastructure under a five-year, federally funded program (RHTP).

data.title: Indiana RHTP Clinical Social Worker Supervision Program
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Family and Social Services Administration (FSSA), Division of Mental Health and Addiction (DMHA)
data.summary: Funds clinical-supervision cost offsets for master's-level therapists pursuing advanced licensure at rural behavioral-health providers, hospitals, and CMHCs.

data.title: Indiana RHTP Rural Provider Recruitment, Retention, and Capacity Project (R&R Grant)
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Family and Social Services Administration (FSSA), Division of Mental Health and Addiction (DMHA)
data.summary: Funds recruitment, retention, and capacity-building for rural behavioral health providers.

data.title: Mobile Integrated Health Consulting & Project Management
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Department of Health
data.summary: The Vermont Department of Health seeks one or more companies to provide consulting and project management services to support the Office of EMS for the Mobile Integrated Health initiative and activities related to the RHTP.

data.title: VDH Mobile Integrated Health Consulting & Project Management RFP
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Department of Health (Agency of Human Services)
data.summary: The Vermont Department of Health is soliciting proposals from qualified firms for consulting and project management services to support the Office of EMS (OEMS) in the development, launch, and evaluation of a statewide Mobile Integrated Health (MIH) and Community Paramedicine (CP) initiative under the Rural Health Transformation Program. Contractors will assist with policy and regulatory development, program design, workforce training, program evaluation, data metrics, and collaborative planning to improve rural health outcomes and EMS system sustainability.

data.title: Building a Sustainable Rural Healthcare Workforce: Education
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board
data.summary: The Rural Health Transformation initiative is a statewide, incentive-based program focused on strengthening rural healthcare systems across South Dakota. Through recruitment incentives and education support—including tiered sign-on bonuses, relocation assistance, rural service stipends, tuition support, paid clinical release, and flexible training—the project aims to build a stable, skilled, and sustainable workforce. The initiative is funded at $62.5 million statewide for FY2026–2031, with $3 million allocated for this specific opportunity. Eligible applicants include licensed healthcare professionals, rural healthcare facilities, tribal health partners, and accredited educational institutions operating within South Dakota. Five-year rural practice service agreements are required for direct education and training awards. The RFP supports expansion of interdisciplinary training and continuing education, rural training pipelines, recruitment and retention aligned to rural needs, and technology-enabled access across the state.

data.title: Vermont Rural Health Transformation – AI Transcription and Scribe Technology
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services – Office of the Secretary
data.summary: Vermont was awarded a $195 million Rural Health Transformation (RHT) grant for the first year of a five-year initiative aimed at strengthening rural health networks. This RFP supports Vermont healthcare providers in purchasing, leasing, expanding, or upgrading artificial intelligence (AI) transcription and scribe technology. The goal is to improve efficiency, reduce administrative burden in rural primary care settings, and increase provider and patient satisfaction by automating clinical documentation.

data.title: Administrative Services Organization (ASO) RFP – New Mexico Rural Health Transformation Program
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Human Services Department (HSD) / Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program
data.summary: This RFP seeks an Administrative Services Organization (ASO) to provide administrative and operational support across New Mexico’s Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program initiatives, including contract management, financial processes, and reporting. The RHT Program is a five-year, federally funded initiative designed to expand access to care, strengthen the rural health workforce, and improve long-term sustainability for providers serving rural, frontier, and tribal communities. The ASO will play a critical role in managing day-to-day operations, supporting provider participation, and ensuring compliance and fiscal accountability for the program. Funding for the ASO contract is part of the $96,103,365 awarded for Federal Fiscal Year 2026, with all program awards 100% federally funded by CMS/HHS. The program is authorized under H.R. 1, Public Law 119-21.

data.title: RHTP Chronic Disease Management Program
data.issuingAgency: Oklahoma State Department of Health (OSDH) / CMS
data.summary: The Oklahoma State Department of Health (OSDH), with support from CMS, invites eligible organizations to apply for the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Chronic Disease Management Program. This competitive opportunity provides $15.2 million for evidence-based or evidence-informed interventions addressing cardiovascular disease, cancer, respiratory illnesses, diabetes, and stroke in rural Oklahoma (see Attachment A for eligible communities). Funding will support personnel, clinical equipment, minor renovations, vehicles, program operations, and program evaluation. Awards must demonstrate compliance with CMS, measurable outcomes, and targeting of underserved rural communities.
applicantTypes: Eligible organizations serving rural communities per Attachment A

data.title: Chronic Disease Remote Monitoring in Schools
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health – Office of Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion
data.summary: The South Dakota Department of Health seeks public, private, and tribal K-12 schools for the implementation of remote monitoring strategies for students with chronic diseases (e.g., diabetes, asthma). Awardees must develop guidance/policies and procure suitable technology/equipment. All communication, including questions or clarifications, must be routed through Kiley Hump at Kiley.Hump@state.sd.us; questions deadline is June 3, 2026. Responses are posted to the ESM Solutions Posting Board event page.

data.title: Rural Clinical Preceptor Stipend Program
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The Rural Clinical Preceptor Stipend Program (RISE 2.2, 2.C), part of Utah's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), provides stipends to licensed physicians (MD, DO), Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (APRNs), and Physician Assistants (PAs) practicing in Utah’s rural counties who serve as uncompensated or first-time clinical preceptors. For Year 1 (July 1–December 1, 2026), $200,000 in stipends is available to expand rural clinical training capacity and enhance Utah’s rural health workforce pipeline. This program is federally funded by CMS/HHS, with a five-year anticipated funding duration and Year 1 overall RHTP awards of $195,743,566.29.

data.title: Statewide Local Health Challenge (Personal Health Accelerator)
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: The West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Personal Health Accelerator Statewide Local Health Challenge, under Announcement of Funding Availability RHT-AFA-05-27-2026-PHA, is offering up to $3.4 million for one-year grants to design, implement, and operate structured, time-bound, outcomes-driven health challenges delivering measurable improvements in nutrition, physical activity, chronic disease prevention, and workforce participation for rural communities across West Virginia. The program prioritizes chronic disease reduction, evidence-based interventions, data integration via the State Data Spine, and scalable county-level pilots tracked through milestone achievements. Selected grantee(s) must execute a replicable model, administer performance-based incentives, and coordinate with local health departments, employers, schools, and community organizations to engage high-risk, at-risk, and general populations. Multi-region or statewide partnerships are strongly encouraged, with preference for consortia offering food-as-medicine, nutrition support, or related wellness delivery capacity. Disbursement is milestone-based: initial pilot launches in 2–3 counties, expansion to 5–8 counties in Year 1, and a required path to 100% county participation by Year 5. All grantees must comply with State-defined reporting, budget, and data standards to ensure accountability, privacy, and impact.
applicantTypes: Local entities able to scale statewide
Consortia or partnerships (single prime applicant required)

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program - Telehealth
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services - Office of the Secretary
data.summary: This subrecipient grant opportunity supports Vermont medical practices and provider consortiums in acquiring, implementing, and using telehealth technology solutions that enable secure, high-quality virtual care delivery. The initiative aims to improve access, continuity, and resilience of Vermont’s rural health system, especially for rural and underserved communities. Funding is available to support secure telehealth platforms, connected diagnostic tools, infrastructure, technical assistance, and training on technology selection, implementation, cybersecurity, and compliance. The grant is part of a five-year initiative begun in 2026, with $195 million available in Year One.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program - Remote Patient Monitoring
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services - Office of the Secretary
data.summary: This subrecipient grant opportunity, under Vermont's Rural Health Transformation Program, provides funds to provider organizations for the purchase or lease of Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) equipment and/or platforms. Eligible RPM technologies aim to build stronger rural health networks, improve care technology, and strengthen the rural health workforce. Implementation may include hardware, software licenses, system integration, and provider/staff training, prioritizing rural ZIP codes and providers serving rural Vermonters. Examples include Bluetooth-enabled, connected scales, blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, glucose monitors, and cardiology RPM devices.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program - EConsult
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services - Office of the Secretary
data.summary: Vermont received a $195 million grant in Year One of a five-year Rural Health Transformation Program to build stronger rural health networks, improve technology and shared operations, and strengthen the rural health workforce. This NOFO provides funds to eligible healthcare providers and consortia to support the purchase or lease of electronic consultation (e-consult) technology. The program aims to improve rural care access by enabling primary care providers to consult with specialists remotely, reduce unnecessary patient travel, and enhance local care capacity. Grants may cover technology acquisition, upgrades, and eligible startup coordination costs. Recurring software costs may be funded over multiple years.

data.title: RHTP Health and Lifestyle (Initiative 9)
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)
data.summary: Initiative 9 of the Florida Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) focuses on food insecurity screening (Hunger Vital Sign), brief nutrition counseling, closed-loop referrals to food assistance, and school-based youth fitness/nutrition interventions. Eligible activities must address quality and outcomes, prevention, and chronic disease reduction for rural communities.
applicantTypes: Other Qualified Entities serving rural communities

data.title: The Rural Texas Strong Program – Initiative 6 (Part 1): Infrastructure and Capital Investments for Rural Texas
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary:
The Rural Texas Strong Initiative 6 (Part 1) provides up to $70,432,073.50 from the federal CMS RHTP for infrastructure and capital investments in rural Texas healthcare facilities. $20 million is prioritized for facilities supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Funded activities include facility upgrades, equipment purchases, emergency preparedness, and workforce-related renovations. Up to 75 awards may be made.

This RFA provides grant funding to eligible rural healthcare providers in Texas for capital investments, infrastructure upgrades, and equipment purchases designed to strengthen rural healthcare access, quality, and sustainability. $70.4 million in total funding is available, with $20 million prioritized for intellectual and developmental disability (IDD) providers. Applicants must submit all required materials by the stated deadline for screening and evaluation.

This grant opportunity funds rural healthcare providers in Texas to strengthen and modernize rural healthcare delivery through infrastructure, facility upgrades, and capital equipment investments. It aims to improve access, quality, and sustainability of care in rural communities, with a prioritization of funding for intellectual and developmental disability (IDD) providers. Total funding available is over $70 million, with up to 75 awards anticipated.
applicantTypes: Facilities serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities

data.title: ToRCH Care Strategic Minor Renovations (Horizon 1)
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Department of Social Services (DSS), Division of Finance and Administrative Services (DFAS), Procurement Unit
data.summary: The ToRCH Care Strategic Minor Renovations (Horizon 1) program, administered by the Missouri Department of Social Services under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), seeks to fund minor modernization and safety renovations at eligible rural hospital facilities across Missouri. Priority is given to projects addressing urgent safety, access risks, regulatory compliance, and issues related to chronic disease, maternal health, or behavioral health. Awards are up to $2.5 million per facility, with a requirement of at least a 10% matching contribution. Applicants must demonstrate community need and alignment with RHTP objectives.

data.title: Rooted in Health: Definitive Mobile Dental Services
data.issuingAgency: Kentucky Department for Public Health (DPH), Cabinet for Health and Family Services
data.summary: This competitive RFA, part of Kentucky's Rooted in Health: Rural Dental Access initiative under the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), provides federal funds for nonprofit organizations to deliver full-spectrum definitive mobile dental care in rural, high-need Kentucky communities. Eligible applicants must demonstrate capacity, experience, and authority to operate mobile dental units and deliver restorative and prosthodontic oral health care. Services must include diagnostic, restorative, exodontia, and prosthodontic care, with strong community partnerships, clinical oversight, and participation in required reporting. The opportunity prioritizes readiness to deploy funds during budget period 1 (October 1, 2026 – September 30, 2027). Continuation funding in subsequent years requires achievement of performance metrics subject to CMS and state guidance.
applicantTypes: Other nonprofit organizations with mobile dental experience

data.title: From Crisis to Care: Education & Training Modernization
data.issuingAgency: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services
data.summary: The Kentucky Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Crisis to Care Education & Training Modernization RFA provides new federal funds to modernize hands-on EMS skills training and establish or expand mobile EMS training units in rural and underserved areas of Kentucky. The program focuses on building the EMS workforce, enhancing training quality, and increasing certified professionals statewide. Supported activities must align with the Rural Health Transformation Plan's strategic priorities, including chronic disease, maternal health, behavioral health, dental access, and emergency response. Funding is available to KBEMS TEI-licensed EMS education agencies, with applications considered on a rolling basis until June 12, 2026.

data.title: Crisis to Care: Establish or Expand Community Paramedicine Program
data.issuingAgency: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services (CHFS)
data.summary: The Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Community Paramedicine RFA provides up to $20 million in competitive awards for Kentucky EMS agencies to establish or expand community paramedicine services in rural areas. This program funds workforce expansion, technology implementation, and the development of partnerships (highlighting integration with behavioral health and community mental health centers). Supported activities include mobile crisis response, preventative and chronic care outreach, care continuity, and the strengthening of EMS as a connector to the broader healthcare system. All funding is federally supplied via CMS/HHS, with a focus on agencies that demonstrate readiness, high rural impact, and sustainable, credentialed models of care coordinated under Kentucky Board of EMS (KBEMS) standards. Grants are intended for KBEMS-licensed, public or nonprofit agencies launching or scaling evidence-based, community-driven EMS care that addresses local needs and sustained system capacity.

data.title: THRIVE - Telehealth, Health Monitoring, and Response Innovation for Vital Expansion (LIFELINE)
data.issuingAgency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DF&A)
data.summary: The THRIVE initiative, a core part of Arkansas’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), funds projects to modernize rural healthcare delivery through telehealth access, EMS modernization, and remote patient monitoring. The LIFELINE sub-initiative specifically supports EMS tele-triage platforms, trauma and stroke response coordination, interoperable EMS communications, ambulance equipment with integrated technology, and tele-consultation networks. Funded projects must clearly align with at least one THRIVE program objective: expanding high-quality telehealth, reducing EMS and trauma response times, improving chronic disease or behavioral health outcomes, strengthening health IT security/interoperability, and supporting data-driven care. Eligible applicants include rural hospitals, EMS providers, clinics, behavioral health providers, clinically integrated networks (CINs), and nonprofit or public entities serving rural Arkansas. Schools and public health entities are not eligible for LIFELINE but may qualify under other THRIVE sub-initiatives. Projects must demonstrate a credible implementation plan, organization readiness, measurable outcomes, and compliance with CMS RHTP requirements (NOFO Sections II–IV).

data.title: Family Support Services (FSS) Community Services Grant
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) is accepting applications for the Family Support Services (FSS) Community Services Grant (CSG) program (RFA No. HHS0016936). This competitive grant funds the provision of coordinated, voluntary crisis pregnancy services, foster care outreach, and family support community services at no cost to participants in nine designated counties in the greater Houston area. Successful applicants will demonstrate capacity for targeted outreach, delivery of direct services, use of data reporting systems, and robust community partnerships. Eligible organizations include Texas-based nonprofits, community-based organizations, and healthcare providers.

data.title: Center for Rural Health Sustainability & Innovation (CRHSI) RFP
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Human Services Department (HSD) / RHT Program
data.summary: This RFP invites proposals to establish the Center for Rural Health Sustainability & Innovation, providing support for rural health systems transformation through sustainability and innovation initiatives in NM.

data.title: Iowa Best and Brightest Medical Equipment Program (RFP PHTHORC26011)
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary:
Best and Brightest Medical Equipment program under Healthy Hometowns (RHT), associated with RFP PHTHORC26011.

Umbrella Iowa RHT program portal. Individual procurements/notices are tracked as separate opportunities.

Notice of intent to release RFP PHTHOET27001 for Mobile Integrated Health projects in Iowa.

data.title: Evaluation of Vermont’s Rural Healthcare Transformation (RHT) Program
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services
data.summary: The Vermont Agency of Human Services is soliciting proposals for the design, implementation, and statewide deployment of an evaluation of Vermont’s Rural Healthcare Transformation (RHT) Program. The evaluation will include developing statewide performance metrics, impact analysis, quarterly updates, annual reporting, an interactive data dashboard, and supporting program compliance and mid-course improvement efforts. Total Year 1 funding is up to $1,000,000, supported by CMS. The contract includes clear deliverables and milestone deadlines.

data.title: Suicide Intervention in Healthcare Systems
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services – Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: The North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services is offering a competitive grant opportunity under the RHTP to support suicide intervention in rural and tribal healthcare facilities. This $400,000 initiative aims to help healthcare systems implement suicide risk screening, standardized care protocols, and connect with behavioral health programs, supporting Initiative 1 ('Make ND Healthy Again') of the state RHTP transformation plan.

data.title: Oklahoma Rural Health Transformation – Rural Regional Reorientation (RRR) Subawards
data.issuingAgency: Oklahoma State Department of Health (OSDH)
data.summary: The Oklahoma State Department of Health (OSDH) Rural Regional Reorientation (RRR) Program, part of the RHTP, will distribute over $223,476,947 in federal funds (100% funded by CMS/HHS) through competitive subawards up to $4,000,000 per project. The RRR program aims to strengthen sustainability, access, and quality of rural healthcare across Oklahoma (excluding Oklahoma and Tulsa counties), focusing on clinical transformation, partnership development, capital improvements, and innovative care models serving communities under 55,000 residents. Eligible applicants include healthcare and social service providers, Tribal organizations, local governments, hospital systems, FQHCs, Critical Access Hospitals, and partnerships of two or more eligible entities. Funds are reimbursement-only; no cost share or match is required. Awards cannot cover direct personnel compensation or vehicle purchases. Subrecipients must comply with federal (2 CFR 200, Buy America) and OSDH program requirements, including reporting and monitoring. Applications must be received via email by 5:00 PM CT on June 12, 2026.

data.title: Maryland RHTP: Post Harvest Infrastructure — Cold Storage for Producers
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Agriculture
data.summary: Food-is-medicine infrastructure grant funding cold storage infrastructure for rural food producers, part of Maryland's Pillar 3 food systems strategy.

data.title: Indiana RHTP Registry and Incentive Management System (RFP 26-87556)
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Administration on behalf of Indiana Department of Health
data.summary: Indiana Department of Administration, on behalf of the Indiana Department of Health, seeks proposals to develop, implement, and maintain a centralized RHTP Registry and Incentive Management System. This system will support the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) goals by managing incentives and registry for rural physicians and clinical preceptors, aiming to expand the rural healthcare workforce, increase Graduate Medical Education capacity, and enhance clinical training in rural Indiana. The system must comply with state IT standards, privacy, and security, facilitating pilot launches, full deployment, and ongoing incentives tracking per award requirements.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation - Shared EHR
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services - Office of the Secretary
data.summary: Vermont has received a Rural Health Transformation (RHT) grant of $195 million in Year One of a five-year opportunity. The purpose of the grant is to build stronger rural health networks, improve technology and shared operations, strengthen the rural health workforce and ultimately ensure that Vermonters receive the right care at the right time for an affordable cost. This subrecipient grant opportunity is to incentivize adoption of a shared electronic medical record (EMR)/electronic health record (EHR) platform, to strengthen statewide data sharing and care coordination. The State of Vermont seeks a qualified third-party organization (“Grant Recipient”) to serve as program manager and implementation lead for the Shared Services – Shared EMR/EHR activity under Vermont’s Rural Health Transformation Program. The intent is to reduce administrative burden, improve care coordination, and advance care integration by supporting adoption and implementation of shared technology services that improve clinical operations and interoperability across rural hospitals and provider entities (including non-hospital providers such as health centers, independent provider groups, and community service agencies using an EMR/EHR). The shared EMR/EHR must complement and strengthen Vermont’s Health Information Exchange (VHIE), optimizing interoperability and promoting a more complete longitudinal health record for Vermonters. Participation for rural providers is voluntary.

data.title: Perinatal and Pediatric Behavioral Health Teleconsultation and Education Project
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: This opportunity supports the expansion of behavioral health education and teleconsultation services for women, infants, and children in rural Tennessee, under the federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The Perinatal and Pediatric Behavioral Health Teleconsultation and Education Project (RFA #34320-19626) aims to build a sustainable statewide system by providing psychiatric consultation, provider training, care navigation, and linkage to community-based services for perinatal and pediatric professionals. The focus is on modernizing technology, extending access, and improving behavioral health outcomes for individuals from pregnancy through 12 months postpartum and children up to age 21. The grant is a part of the TDH strategy to reverse rural hospital decline, strengthen local economies, and support sustainable health systems.

data.title: Indiana Medical Operations Coordination Center (MOCC) Real-Time Healthcare Emergency and Hospital Capacity System
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Administration (IDOA)
data.summary: Indiana seeks qualified vendors to implement and operate a statewide real-time Healthcare Emergency and Hospital Capacity System for the Medical Operations Coordination Center (MOCC) under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), funded by CMS/HHS. The System will aggregate data from all Indiana hospitals and EMS for emergency management, behavioral health triage, support for care transitions, and integration with state/federal platforms. Responsibilities include system design, development, implementation, maintenance, and operation, with a five-year program window. Deliverables are phased pilots, full rollout, and future telemedicine integration. The procurement is funded in its entirety by CMS/HHS ($206,927,896.80).

data.title: Ohio Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Community Health Worker (CHW) Training and Technical Assistance (DOH59679)
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health (ODH)
data.summary: Ohio Department of Health solicits proposals for the Ohio Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Community Health Worker (CHW) Training and Technical Assistance program (RHT-CHWATT). The project develops and delivers targeted skill-building and professional development opportunities to strengthen CHWs' capacity to connect rural Ohioans to essential resources and improve health outcomes. Topics include working with aging/Amish/veteran rural populations, health literacy, consumer technology training, and community outreach. Budget: $750,000. Project period: 07/01/2026–06/30/2027, with up to 4 years renewal through 06/30/2031. One (1) award. Submitted via OhioBuys (requires supplier registration). Solicitation #DOH59679 (Round 2 posted 05/11/2026).

data.title: Dual Track Rural Hospital Remote Critical Care Services (RCCS) RFGA FY26
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health
data.summary: The Georgia Department of Community Health, State Office of Rural Health, announces the FY26 Request for Grant Application for Dual Track Rural Hospital Remote Critical Care Services (RCCS). Up to four awards are anticipated, each up to $225,000 for a one-year funding period, subject to availability of appropriated funds.

data.title: AHEAD Model Pre-Implementation Funding
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH)
data.summary: This funding opportunity launches Budget Period 1 of the GREAT Health Program under the Rural Health Transformation Program. Eligible rural hospitals that have signed an LOI to participate in the AHEAD Model may apply for up to $750,000 to support migration to the new payment system, modernization of technology, workforce recruitment and retention, primary care outreach, and regional collaboration. There are 87 awards available. All funding awarded must be spent by September 30, 2027.

data.title: GREAT Health Pre-Implementation Funding
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH)
data.summary: Pre-implementation funding of up to $750,000 for rural hospitals in Georgia that submitted a Letter of Intent (LOI) to participate in the GREAT Health (Georgia Rural Health Transformation Program, RHTP) AHEAD Model Program. Funding aims to support initial activities ahead of program implementation.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Initiatives
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health
data.summary: The Minnesota Department of Health is offering competitive grants under the Rural Health Transformation Program: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Initiatives. The initiative, funded by CMS/HHS, aims to expand and improve child and adolescent mental health systems in rural Minnesota through regional collaboration, workforce training, outreach, and service infrastructure for crisis services. Approximately $1,782,000 will be awarded this cycle to 5–10 regional collaborations. Eligible applicants are Child and Adolescent Mental Health Collaboratives (including Integrated Children’s Mental Health and Family Services Collaboratives), counties or consortia of counties/county health boards, consortia/regions serving Adult Mental Health Initiatives (strongly encouraged to apply as groups), and Tribal Nations. The program is 100% federally funded, with a total federal funding pool of $193,090,618.14 and no matching requirement. Applications close on June 15, 2026.
applicantTypes: Established Child and Adolescent Mental Health Collaboratives
Counties or consortia of counties/county health boards
Consortia/regions serving Minnesota's Adult Mental Health Initiatives

data.title: RHTP – Healthier Ohio Initiatives: Preventing and Addressing Chronic Disease (Track One)
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health
data.summary: The Ohio Department of Health is seeking proposals for the Rural Health Transformation Program’s Healthier Ohio Initiatives: Preventing and Addressing Chronic Disease (Track One). This program supports evidence-based projects in up to 73 rural Ohio counties targeting chronic disease prevention and management—particularly diabetes and hypertension. Applicants should advance innovative clinical, workforce, and technology strategies, including Lifestyle Medicine training, care team coordination, digital health tools, and patient cohort management, with robust performance tracking. The anticipated project total is $14.6M with a focus on sustainable capacity and holistic care for rural communities.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program - Human Resources Information System
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services - Office of the Secretary
data.summary: Vermont has received a Rural Health Transformation (RHT) grant of $195 million in Year One of a five-year opportunity. This subrecipient grant opportunity will establish a shared human resources information system (HRIS) for Vermont healthcare providers. The unified HRIS will centralize core HR functions such as benefits administration, payroll, recruitment, onboarding, licensure tracking, and compliance, while allowing each participating hospital and community partner to manage specific tasks securely. The system aims to streamline workforce management, reduce administrative costs, improve workforce mobility, enable flexible staff scheduling, and support care across regions. Participation by healthcare providers is voluntary.

data.title: GME Strategic Plan Development (RHTP RISE 2.1, 2.A)
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: Single award up to $1,600,000 for a healthcare consultant or organization with rural GME expertise to develop Utah's statewide 10-year GME strategic plan, advancing rural physician access and workforce capacity. Awardee will engage diverse stakeholders, including tribal and rural health facilities, and deliver rigorous, data-driven planning and technical assistance under Utah's Rural Health Transformation Program. Supported by CMS/HHS funding.

data.title: Idaho Rural Behavioral Health and Pediatric Psychiatry Access Programs (FFY26)
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (DHW)
data.summary: Idaho DHW is soliciting applications for FFY26 competitive subgrant programs in rural behavioral health and pediatric psychiatry. Available opportunities include: (1) Behavioral Health Prevention subgrants for up to 4 rural entities to provide youth behavioral health prevention programs ($400,000 total); (2) School-based Behavioral Health Hubs, awarding up to 15 school districts/partners to place behavioral health professionals in schools ($6,000,000 total); and (3) a lead agency for the Idaho Pediatric Psychiatry Access Line (PPAL), focused on university partnerships ($1,200,000). No awards have been made as of the posting date. Total available: $7.6 million.

data.title: Iowa RHTP: Combat Cancer Health Hubs
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Health and Human Services (HHS)
data.summary: Hub-and-spoke cancer care network program (RFP# COMPADM26008) — Hub sites propose 3 Spoke subcontractor sites (hospitals, RHCs, FQHCs, oncology practices). Sequentially numbered after DB's existing COMPADM26005/26006/26007 records. Supports new chemotherapy lines of service, care coordination between sites, remote consultations and teleoncology services, virtual tumor boards, and referral/telehealth agreements. 5 Hub organizations selected and announced 2026-06-18: Ottumwa Regional Health Center, Wayne County Hospital, Shenandoah Medical Center, Greater Regional Medical Center, and Mary Greeley Medical Center. 100% funded by CMS as part of Iowa's RHTP award.

data.title: Preventive Care & Care-at-Home (Bundle One)
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)
data.summary: Preventive Care & Care-at-Home (Bundle One) of Florida's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is a competitive, federally funded grant opportunity from the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA). It supports integrated, innovative preventive care delivery for rural communities via Mobile Health Units, Community Paramedicine, Remote Telemonitoring, Pharmacy-Based Retail Clinics, and electronic health record (EHR) connectivity with the state Health Information Exchange (HIE). Eligible applicants include clinical and non-clinical health care entities, local governments, tribal organizations, and community-based entities either located in or primarily serving rural Floridians as defined by the RFA. The initiative totals $60,500,000 in Year 1 statewide funding, aims for sustainable, modernized models of rural health care, and requires service launches and core milestones within 90–180 days post-award.

data.title: RHTP Value-Based Purchasing (Initiative 11)
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)
data.summary: Funds will support organizational, technological, and care-coordination infrastructure for rural providers to make the transition from fee-for-service to value-based contracts with Medicaid Managed Care Organizations, under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Initiative 11. This competitive opportunity prioritizes provider quality, service improvement, and system outcomes in designated Florida rural counties.
applicantTypes: Other Qualified Entities serving rural communities

data.title: RHTP Workforce Development (Initiative 8)
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)
data.summary: This standalone RFA, Initiative #8 under Florida’s Rural Health Transformation Program, seeks to build sustainable rural health workforce pipelines through grants supporting two independent tracks: (1) supervised clinical rotations and preceptorships for health professions students; and (2) allied and direct care career technical education (CTE) pathways for high school and college students. Projects must serve designated rural counties within the four RHTP regions, and aim to expand rural health workforce capacity, promote innovation, and ensure lasting impact.
applicantTypes: Other Qualified Entities serving rural communities

data.title: RHTP Rural Satellite Clinics (Initiative 1)
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)
data.summary: Provides startup funding for new or expanded rural and satellite clinics delivering behavioral, dental, or medical care. Supports creation or expansion of rural clinic locations, including eligible urban organizations opening rural service sites, strengthening access to comprehensive health care in underserved Florida rural communities. Refer to RFA 036-25/26 and Addenda for full eligibility, Super Region/county lists, and program priorities.
applicantTypes: Other qualified entities serving rural communities

data.title: RHTP Specialty and Acute Care Bundle (Bundle Two)

Projects must support eligible rural communities across defined regions.
applicantTypes: Other Qualified Entities serving rural communities

data.title: Illinois RHTP Hospital Transformation Planning Grant
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Non-competitive planning grant split equally among 97 eligible rural hospitals (IDPH-licensed acute-care, GATA pre-qualified, CAH or minimum-discharge threshold; LTAC/rehab/psych/children's hospitals excluded as lead applicants). Application platform: Euna/AmpliFund.

data.title: Missouri ToRCH Care Hub Anchor Application
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Department of Social Services (DSS)
data.summary: The Missouri Department of Social Services (DSS) ToRCH (Transforming Rural Community Health) Care initiative selected 27 Hub Anchor organizations from 41 applications, announced July 17, 2026, subject to execution of a Hub Anchor Participation Agreement. Hub Anchors serve as the coordinating organization for a regional rural health transformation network under Missouri's RHTP award. Distinct from the existing DB 'ToRCH Care Strategic Minor Renovations (Horizon 1)' record (due 2026-06-11), which is a separate building-renovations construction/IFB program.

data.title: Community Health Worker + Accountable Food Is Medicine Grant Program (CHW+AFIM)
data.issuingAgency: Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE)
data.summary: Kansas's CHW+AFIM grant program, funded by the federal Rural Health Transformation Program, provides over $1 million in competitive awards to rural healthcare organizations for integration of Community Health Workers (CHWs) and expansion of Accountable Food is Medicine interventions. The initiative supports validated screening for health-related social needs and chronic disease risk, sustainable CHW employment, and increased coverage for evidence-based food-as-medicine programs. The Request for Applications targets rural Kansas healthcare organizations to develop tailored billing workflows, deliver AFIM interventions targeting chronic conditions (primarily diabetes and hypertension), collaborate with KDHE, and submit required documentation. Approximately seven subrecipient organizations statewide will be funded in this initial project year. Award range: $95,000–$150,000 per organization.
applicantTypes: Native American Sovereign Tribe healthcare facility
Primary care clinic in rural KS

data.title: RHTP FFY2026 Infrastructure & Operations Competitive Solicitations
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
data.summary: Seven competitive contractor RFPs released under the Idaho Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) FFY2026: (1) Evaluation & Analytics contractor ($2M, 1 award), (2) Project Management Support ($1.3M, 1 award), (3) Workforce Ladder Payments Administrator ($800K, 1 award), (4) Facility Technology Assessment ($2.2M, 1 award), (5) Independent Renovation Verifier ($2M, 1 award), (6) Rural Health Needs Assessment for Idaho universities ($2.8M, 1 award), (7) Emergency Communications HAN replacement ($100K, 1 award). Total funding for Year 1: ~$12.2M. Solicitations address evaluation, analytics, project management, facility assessments, workforce administration, health needs assessment, and emergency communications for rural health transformation.

data.title: Alaska RHTP Implementation Pathway — Full Application, Round 1
data.issuingAgency: Alaska Department of Health
data.summary: Full-application round covering all 6 of Alaska's official RHTP strategic initiatives (Healthy Beginnings, Health Care Access, Healthy Communities, Pay for Value: Fiscal Sustainability, Strengthen Workforce, Spark Technology & Innovation) — these are funding categories within ONE application round, not 6 separate RFPs. 403 organizations advanced from the earlier LOI stage to apply. Part of Alaska's $272,174,856 Year-1 RHTP award.

data.summary: Through this RFP, Vermont's Agency of Human Services, Department of Vermont Health Access seeks contractor(s) to strengthen Blueprint’s transformation network capacity via implementation supports provided by clinical champions. Supported by Vermont’s $195 million Rural Health Transformation grant, this effort aims to build stronger rural health networks, improve technology and operations, and strengthen the rural health workforce to ensure Vermonters receive coordinated, patient-centered, population-focused care at an affordable cost.
