data.summary: The Delaware Division of Public Health is soliciting proposals from qualified vendors to provide administrative, oversight, and evaluation services for the Rural Health Transformation Program Support Services (HSS-26-078), in accordance with detailed requirements outlined in the official RFP document.

data.title: Enhancing Blueprint Transformation Network Capacity: Workforce Support and System Development via Clinical Case
data.issuingAgency: Department of Vermont Health Access
data.summary: This solicitation is one of five sub-RFPs initiated under Vermont’s Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program, supporting the Blueprint Transformation Network. The RFP focuses on workforce support and system development for rural healthcare providers in Vermont, with an emphasis on enhancing clinical case capacity. All Year 1 funding opportunities are closed; announcements for Year 2 will be made when available on the official program website.

data.title: Enhancing Blueprint Transformation Network Capacity: Workforce Support and System Development via Training
data.issuingAgency: Department of Vermont Health Access
data.summary: This solicitation is part of the Vermont Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program, offering targeted support to rural healthcare providers—including Critical Access Hospitals—through workforce development and system training. The RHT Program aims to enhance network capacity by investing in workforce support initiatives and system transformation via specialized training. This opportunity is one of several under the Blueprint Transformation Network, focused on advancing healthcare efficiency and access for rural populations in Vermont.

data.title: Enhancing Blueprint Transformation Network Capacity: Workforce Support and System Development through Learning Collabs
data.issuingAgency: Department of Vermont Health Access
data.summary: This opportunity is one of several targeted solicitations under the Vermont Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program, administrated by the Department of Vermont Health Access as part of the AHEAD (Achieving Healthcare Efficiency through Accountable Design) Model. The solicitation focuses on strengthening Blueprint Transformation Network capacity in workforce support and advancing system development through learning collaboratives. RHT aims to support rural healthcare providers, including Critical Access Hospitals, by funding system-level innovation, workforce development, and strategic planning to improve health care delivery in Vermont.

data.title: Minnesota Rural Health Transformation Program: Healthcare Workforce Retention Program
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health
data.summary: This RFP seeks proposals from Minnesota-based organizations to identify and address systemic factors driving healthcare provider burnout in rural Minnesota and to design, pilot, and scale evidence-based interventions that increase workforce retention and improve rural health outcomes. Up to 10 rural healthcare organizations per year may be selected as pilot sites over five years. Funding is provided through the federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), established by H.R.1 (Section 71401 of Public Law 119-21), administered by the Minnesota Department of Health, and funded by CMS/HHS.

data.title: Healthy Active Rural Tennessee (HART)
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: Healthy Active Rural Tennessee (HART) is a competitive grant opportunity under the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), administered by the Tennessee Department of Health. The program aims to improve health outcomes in Tennessee's 89 rural and suburban counties (outside the state's metropolitan counties) through built environment, assessment, planning, demonstration, placemaking, and policy promotion for health and wellness. Target projects advance health equity, serve historically underserved communities, and foster community resilience. Construction and capital asset expenditures are not permitted. Activities must align with evidence-based, outcomes-driven strategies and the grant's primary objectives, emphasizing cross-sectoral partnerships and local engagement. Approximately $6 million is available to fund an estimated 48-120 projects. Maximum award is $150,000 per project, with no matching or cost share requirement.

data.title: PATH 1.5: Rural Behavioral Health Integration Grant
data.issuingAgency: Utah DHHS — Office of Rural Health
data.summary: Grant opportunity through Utah Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) PATH Initiative 1.5 for rural and frontier Utah health facilities to implement evidence-based behavioral health and primary care integration models. Emphasis areas include collaborative care, workforce and training support, EMR enhancement, and sustainable billing workflows. Program is 100% CMS funded with strict eligibility verification and structured, multi-phase review process as outlined in the RFGA.

data.title: Michigan Rural Health Tribal Initiative - 2026
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary: The grantee will serve as the subrecipient to establish a baseline that can be used to establish targets and demonstrate CHW-related outcomes. The funds will support coordinated outreach, data collection, analysis, and reporting necessary to produce a reliable workforce inventory and needs assessment, ensuring efficient use of resources while avoiding duplication of existing efforts.

data.title: Michigan Rural Health Partnership Collaborative Care FQHC - 2026
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary: The grantee will serve as the subrecipient to establish a baseline that can be used to establish targets and demonstrate CHW-related outcomes. The funds will support coordinated outreach, data collection, analysis, and reporting necessary to produce a reliable workforce inventory and needs assessment, ensuring efficient use of resources while avoiding duplication of existing efforts.

data.title: Michigan Rural Health High School to Healthcare Pipeline - 2026
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary: The grantee will serve as the subrecipient to establish a baseline that can be used to establish targets and demonstrate CHW-related outcomes. The funds will support coordinated outreach, data collection, analysis, and reporting necessary to produce a reliable workforce inventory and needs assessment, ensuring efficient use of resources while avoiding duplication of existing efforts.

data.title: RISE 2.1: Rural Workforce Expansion Program
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Rural Health
data.summary: Forecasted grant for rural workforce expansion initiatives under Utah's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Opening date to be determined; program will partner with organizations to implement Year 1 initiatives in rural Utah. The RHTP program is fully funded by CMS/HHS with an award total of $195,743,566.29 for FY2024. Applicants are encouraged to monitor the official funding opportunities table for timelines and operational details.

data.title: Rural Clinician Credit Bank: Recruitment & Retention Funding for Rural Louisiana Providers
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Department of Health, Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability
data.summary: The Rural Clinician Credit Bank, funded by the Rural Health Transformation Program, provides matching funds to rural healthcare employers in Louisiana for recruitment and retention payments to eligible clinical staff who commit to a 5-year term. Providers may claim reimbursement for sign-on bonuses, retention incentives, relocation assistance, and career development stipends. The program aims to strengthen the rural health workforce, improve retention, and expand access to care across rural communities. Employers must provide a cash match and meet reporting requirements. Total Year 1 available funding: $75,000 per award. Program-level funding exceeds $5.6 million.
applicantTypes: Program for All Inclusive Care of the Elderly

data.title: Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program (ARHTP) 2025–2030: Statewide Strategy and Project Narrative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: The Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program (ARHTP) is a statewide, comprehensive blueprint targeting transformation of rural health systems for over 1.6 million residents in 58 rural counties (2025–2030). Strategies are focused on workforce development, telehealth, IT/cybersecurity infrastructure, EHR integration, maternal health services, and payment/policy reforms. ADECA (lead), in cooperation with CMS/HHS, oversees a five-year, $203M (Year 1) cooperative agreement, with multiple NOFOs released annually. The document covers initiative descriptions, strategic goals, policy alignment, review metrics, and detailed budgets ($125M for IT/cybersecurity; $275M for telehealth/clinical transformation over five years).

data.title: Green Mountain Care Board Health Data Infrastructure Transformation
data.issuingAgency: State of Vermont Office of Purchasing & Contracting on behalf of Green Mountain Care Board (GMCB) and Agency of Digital Services
data.summary: The State of Vermont Office of Purchasing & Contracting, in coordination with the Agency of Digital Services and Green Mountain Care Board (GMCB), seeks proposals for Health Data Infrastructure Transformation support. This project is part of the Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Grant, seeking comprehensive vendor support to improve statewide health data reporting, interoperability, and analytics, contingent upon Year 2 federal grant funding. Vermont Business Registry Bid 73756.

data.title: Alabama Rural Health Practice Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: The Alabama Rural Health Practice Initiative is a competitive funding opportunity under the Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program (ARHTP), funded by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Rural Health Transformation Program and administered by ADECA. A total of $6,935,000 is available for competitive subawards to support projects that expand rural clinic capacity, recruit and retain rural healthcare workforce, implement telehealth, and develop school-based health clinics. This initiative aims to advance rural healthcare access, innovation, and the long-term sustainability of health services across Alabama's rural communities. For questions, contact info@alabamarhtp.com. Round 1 results announced Aug 24, 2026: $7,786,128 awarded across 14 grants under this initiative.

data.title: Alabama RHTP Collaborative EHR, IT, and Cybersecurity Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: ADECA is making $31.6 million available through the Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program for rural providers and partners to modernize IT infrastructure, strengthen cybersecurity, and improve EHR interoperability statewide. The NOFO defines multiple strategy categories, including referral hubs, EHR upgrades for health information exchange, and targeted cybersecurity enhancements. Projects must directly benefit rural Alabama communities and align with strategic goals including improved care coordination, compliance readiness, and network sustainability. Key contacts: info@alabamarhtp.com. Additional application support is available via ARHTP workshops on June 9, 2026 (see NOFO and workshop memo). Round 1 results announced Aug 24, 2026: $32,948,000 awarded across 29 grants under this initiative.

data.title: Alabama RHTP Rural Workforce Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) launches Alabama’s first competitive RHT Program rural workforce funding round with approximately $25 million available. Eligible applicants include hospitals, health systems, EMS agencies, educational institutions, and rural healthcare providers proposing projects to increase rural workforce capacity. The Rural Workforce Initiative prioritizes Graduate Medical Education (GME) expansion, EMS workforce training, education, and recruitment incentives tied to rural service. ADECA administers ARHTP, Alabama’s statewide framework under the CMS Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program authorized by Public Law 119-21. Key points: projects must strengthen rural workforce capacity, support provider sustainability, and address rural access. Application and event schedule are detailed in the NOFO. Round 1 results announced Aug 24, 2026: $35,148,363 awarded across 25 grants under this initiative.

data.title: Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program (Mental Health Initiative)
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: The Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program Mental Health Initiative (administered by ADECA) will award up to $7.55 million in competitive funding to expand and strengthen rural mental health services in Alabama. This NOFO specifically prioritizes school-based tele-mental health programs and the conversion of Community Mental Health Centers (CMHCs) to Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs). The initiative targets rural youth, underserved populations, and seeks to fill structural service gaps, with a focus on sustainable access and care coordination. All awards are contingent on the state’s receipt of CMS Rural Health Transformation funds. Projects funded through this opportunity must be completed by July 31, 2027. Eligible applicants include nonprofit CMHCs, rural health clinics, public school districts, public hospitals, and local government agencies located in rural-designated Alabama counties. Round 1 results announced Aug 24, 2026: $7,881,052 awarded across 13 grants under this initiative.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program - Adoption of a Statewide Closed Loop Referral System
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services - Office of the Secretary
data.summary: This subrecipient grant supports a statewide closed-loop referral system for Vermont, strengthening coordination among health care, mental health, substance use disorder, and social service providers. The platform must facilitate real-time data sharing, referral outcome tracking, improved access to community social supports (housing, food, transportation), and increased cost-efficiency. It aims to reduce duplication of services, improve provider accountability, and advance seamless, person-centered care for rural Vermonters. Solution must comply with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, and federal interoperability standards. Implementation includes stakeholder engagement, onboarding, training, quarterly reporting, operational readiness, and a sustainability plan.

data.title: Nevada WRRAP – Rural Medical Residency Program
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: Sub-program of the Workforce Recruitment and Rural Access Program (WRRAP). Funds rural medical residency programs to train and retain physicians in underserved Nevada communities. Funding result announced July 29, 2026: NVHA announced $4.8 million for rural medical residency investments, including a rural obstetrics fellowship, an APRN fellowship, a rural family medicine residency track in Fallon, and a statewide Rural GME Consortium.

data.title: Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program (ARHTP), Rural Health Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: ADECA will make $60.9 million in federal RHTP funds available through competitive subawards to eligible Alabama rural health providers. Projects may include telehealth service expansion, provider infrastructure improvements, network development, and transportation access. Quarterly and final reporting is required for compliance and performance tracking. The Rural Health Initiative, under ARHTP, aims to strengthen provider networks, improve service access, and promote sustainable rural healthcare delivery across Alabama. Key contacts: info@alabamarhtp.com. Round 1 results announced Aug 24, 2026: $59,982,278 awarded across 57 grants under this initiative.

data.title: Nevada Rural Health Transformation Outcomes Accelerator Program
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: Funds evidence-based, innovative initiatives to improve rural health outcomes in Nevada, focusing on chronic disease, primary care, behavioral health, and maternal and infant health. Emphasizes digital/hybrid care, population health infrastructure, workforce incentives, technology modernization, and sustainability. Subawards support Nevada's rural hospitals, clinics, non-profits, CAHs, healthcare providers, and eligible technology partners working with rural providers. Funding is provided through the CMS One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, P.L. 119-21, Sec. 71401).
applicantTypes: Technology Company (with executed LOA/MOU/contract with eligible rural lead applicant)

data.title: Connected Care Grid – Interoperable Provider Directory and Scheduling Platform
data.issuingAgency: WV Department of Health
data.summary: Solicits proposals to design and implement an interoperable provider directory and scheduling platform to improve care coordination, provider availability visibility, and patient access for the West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Connected Care Grid initiative.

data.title: Maternal/Infant and Child Health Healthcare Resiliency Program
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The Tennessee Department of Health (TDH) is seeking applications under RFA #34320-19426 to implement projects that strengthen maternal, infant, and child health systems of care for rural communities through service expansion, targeted interventions, workforce training, education, and improved access to quality care. Grants of up to $12,500,000 will be awarded for a project period of 50 months, with up to 100 awards anticipated. The program, a key component of the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program, focuses on expanding access, modernizing technology, strengthening the rural health workforce, and innovating in service delivery, with robust outcome reporting requirements. Priority is given to evidence-based, locally relevant projects for women of reproductive age, pregnant and postpartum individuals, infants, and children through age 18, including those with special healthcare needs in HRSA-designated rural areas. This opportunity is aligned with TDH's 2026–2030 Priorities and Maternal/Infant Health Strategic Plans. No cost share or match is required.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program: Statewide Tele-buprenorphine Access Line
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health
data.summary: The Minnesota Department of Health is soliciting proposals for the Rural Health Transformation Program: Statewide Tele-buprenorphine Access Line. The program supports planning, development, and implementation of a centralized tele-buprenorphine (telebupe) access line to deliver on-demand medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) via phone or video, with particular emphasis on rural and underserved populations. The selected grantee must ensure the service operates at least 60 hours per week, provides rapid clinical assessment and prescription access, facilitates warm handoffs to local providers, and establishes a sustainable billing model by the end of the 5-year award period.

data.title: Mobile Mammography Unit Acquisition Funding Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: Provides up to $1,500,000 through the Rural Health Transformation Program to support purchase and deployment of a mobile mammography unit with 3D technology, focused on expanding breast cancer screening for rural, low-income, and medically underserved populations in western North Dakota.

data.title: RISE 2.2, 2.C: Rural Clinical Preceptor Stipend Program
data.issuingAgency: Utah DHHS — Office of Rural Health
data.summary: Re-opened (second chance window: June 22–29, 2026). This program recognizes rural clinical preceptors who provide training to healthcare students in rural Utah settings. Period of performance for second chance applications: August 1–December 1, 2026.

data.title: RHTP Telehealth Access Points
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: Competitive grants for Minnesota rural organizations to establish Telehealth Access Points—dedicated spaces in community sites (schools, pharmacies, libraries, tribal clinics, etc.) where rural residents can access telehealth for primary care, behavioral health, and oral health. Funding supports technology, site upgrades, staff, and care navigation to reduce barriers to healthcare access.

data.title: To Provide Additional Long-Term Care Nursing Facility Capacity in SD
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board
data.summary: 25RFP-26-0903002-0002 To Provide Additional Long-Term Care Nursing Facility Capacity in SD. South Dakota Department of Health is seeking proposals from licensed long-term care providers for reallocating up to 991 nursing facility beds statewide, pursuant to SDCL §§ 34-12-35.6–35.8. Proposals are evaluated as received and must address special care needs. Providers are also encouraged to expand home and community-based services. Contracts may be awarded for one year with up to four one-year renewals, subject to funding availability and performance benchmarks.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program: Rural Clinical Rotations Expansion Grant Program
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: RFP for the Rural Clinical Rotations Expansion Grant Program under Minnesota's Rural Health Transformation Program.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program: Physician Rural Residency Training Program
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: RFP for the Physician Rural Residency Training Program under Minnesota's Rural Health Transformation Program.

data.title: RHTP Competitive Funding Opportunity: Rural Hospital Clinical Equipment (Solicitation 210-312)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS) is offering up to $2,000,000 per eligible rural hospital through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Competitive Funding Opportunity for Rural Hospital Clinical Equipment (Solicitation 210-312). Approximately $40 million in total funding will support the purchase, installation, and minor renovations associated with advanced clinical equipment at rural hospitals—including critical access hospitals, rural emergency hospitals, and general acute hospitals (including eligible non-federally operated Indian Health Service Hospitals). The opportunity advances Initiative 3: Bring High-Quality Healthcare Closer to Home by modernizing rural physical infrastructure, strengthening service capacity, improving clinical outcomes, reducing patient outmigration, and enabling more efficient and resilient care delivery. Eligible equipment includes, but is not limited to, diagnostic imaging, surgical, emergency department, inpatient, swing bed, cardiology, lab, pharmacy, environmental, rehabilitation, OB, oncology, home health, and department-specific advanced clinical and capital equipment. Associated installation and minor renovations integral to equipment are allowable. Unallowable costs include equipment or renovations for non-clinical purposes, supplanting of existing funding, major facility renovations, general facility improvements, and items outside clinical scope. One application per organization is permitted; all applications must be submitted via Qualtrics by June 30, 2026 (5:00 PM CT).
applicantTypes: Rural Hospital (Critical Access Hospital, Rural Emergency Hospital, eligible General Acute Hospital, non-federally operated Indian Health Service Hospitals meeting ND HHS definition)

data.title: Wisconsin RHTP CTE Rural Healthcare Workforce Grant
data.issuingAgency: Wisconsin Department of Public Instruction (DPI)
data.summary: Competitive grant program administered by the Wisconsin DPI CTE Team to assist rural school districts and LEAs in developing and expanding health-related and human services career and technical education (CTE) career pathways. Funded under the Rural Health Transformation Program with federal Medicaid transformation funds distributed via Wisconsin DHS. Grant supports partnerships with local healthcare employers, transcripted course development, and increasing work-based learning opportunities.

data.title: Digital Health Modernization and Technology Grant Program
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health / South Dakota Health Link
data.summary: The Digital Health Modernization and Technology Grant Program, as part of South Dakota's Rural Health Transformation (RHT) initiative, provides approximately $89M in grants to rural and underserved providers statewide. Priorities include EHR adoption, system upgrades, technology and workforce training, telehealth, interoperability, cybersecurity, and regional innovation centers. Eligible applicants are healthcare entities and providers serving rural and underserved South Dakota communities, including critical access hospitals and clinics. Applicants must meet state and federal requirements for subrecipients. Reference RFA #26-09RHT-020 in all applications.

data.title: Administrator for Health Information Technology Rural Infrastructure Fund
data.issuingAgency: Rhode Island Executive Office of Health and Human Services (EOHHS)
data.summary: Vendor delivers technical assistance and financial administration for RI's HIT Rural Infrastructure Fund: evaluates rural-provider applications, ensures compliance, manages fund distribution. Two-year initial term from Sept 2026, renewable up to 3x 12-month periods.

data.title: Growing Rural Opportunities for Well-being (GROW) Regional Grants Program
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Family and Social Services Administration (FSSA) & Indiana Department of Health (IDOH)
data.summary: The Growing Rural Opportunities for Well-being (GROW) Regional Grants Program, administered under Indiana's RHTP, provides $600 million in federal funding over five years to support regionally coordinated, community-driven health transformation initiatives across eight designated rural regions in Indiana. The program aims to address rural health disparities in maternal health, chronic disease management, healthcare access, technology modernization, and workforce development. One Regional Coalition per region may apply, representing partnerships among local health departments, hospitals, FQHCs, schools, employers, and other stakeholders. Projects must address at least one funding category and required health outcomes, including pre/postnatal care, chronic disease, and access to care/unmet needs. Success is measured by transformative potential, measurable outcomes, collaborative structure, impact, and sustainability. No cost-share is required; grants are 100% federally funded through CMS. Applications are due by July 1, 2026. Awards per region are based on population, health needs, and application evaluation.

data.title: Sustainable Rural Healthcare Workforce: Stakeholder & Project Mgmt
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board
data.summary: The South Dakota Department of Health, Office of Rural Health and Emergency Services (ORHES) seeks a contractor to provide strategic leadership and operational support advancing rural healthcare transformation initiatives statewide. Services include strategic planning, stakeholder coordination, program development, operational support, grant and contract administration, technical assistance, evaluation, and reporting. Scope encompasses strengthening rural health systems, workforce development, EMS capacity, and supporting rural, frontier, and tribal communities. Anticipated contract is not to exceed $500,000 for the first year (August 1, 2026 – July 31, 2027), with options for up to three additional one-year renewals.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program: Rapid Response to Recovery – Telebehavioral Health Support
data.issuingAgency: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services, Office of Administrative Services
data.summary: This RFA provides funding of up to $500,000 per applicant for participation as a telebehavioral health hub under Kentucky's RHTP Rapid Response to Recovery initiative, supporting a statewide network to improve behavioral health crisis response, coordination, and recovery. Funds support technology, provider training, and improved regional integration, with emphasis on partnerships among rural hospitals, EMS, law enforcement, behavioral health, and primary care.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Fund Grant - Enhancing Primary Care Focused Data and Analytics
data.issuingAgency: Department of Vermont Health Access (DVHA)
data.summary: The Department of Vermont Health Access (DVHA) is soliciting applications for the Rural Health Transformation Fund Grant focused on enhancing statewide primary care data and analytics infrastructure. This grant seeks to expand access to electronic clinical quality measures (eCQM) calculation tools and community health team (CHT) tracking tools among Vermont Blueprint for Health recognized practices and administrative entities. Funding will support implementation, workflow redesign, training, and data reporting improvements for care coordination and performance improvement. All notifications and addendums are posted on the Vermont Business Registry website.
applicantTypes: Vermont Blueprint for Health recognized primary care practices
Critical Access Hospital–affiliated primary care practices

data.title: AFA - Mobile Medical Primary Care & Dental Care - FY2027
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Health Right Free Clinic Mobile Unit
data.summary: Announcement of Funding Availability for Health Right Free Clinics - Mobile Medical Primary Care and Dental Care Service. Up to six awards available, maximum funding $1,000,000, supporting mobile primary and dental care for underserved and rural communities across WV, especially Medically Underserved Areas and Health Professional Shortage Areas. Performance period July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Funding prioritizes regional diversity, capacity for outcome tracking/reporting, and incentivizing healthy behaviors. The scope includes primary medical care, oral care, obstetrical care, mental health/substance use disorder services, hearing screening, physical/occupational therapy, pharmacy, diagnostic laboratory/x-ray procedures, and must complement (not duplicate) other funded activities. Applicants must propose only the amount reasonably needed and will enter a 12-month subrecipient grant agreement, with possible renewal.
applicantTypes: Current Health Right Free Clinics operating in West Virginia

data.title: Kentucky RHT: Rapid Response to Recovery — CMHC Support
data.issuingAgency: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services (CHFS)
data.summary: Funding for Community Mental Health Centers (CMHCs): follow-up care after EmPATH (Emergency Psychiatric Assessment, Treatment and Healing) visits, plus EMS behavioral-health training and coordination support. Distinct from the existing DB 'Rapid Response to Recovery – Telebehavioral Health Support' record, which funds a separate telebehavioral health initiative.

data.title: Healthy Horizons RFA (New Mexico RHT Program)
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Health Care Authority (HCA)
data.summary: The Healthy Horizons RFA under New Mexico's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funds Regional Hub Organizations to expand specialty, maternal, behavioral health, and chronic disease services in rural, frontier, and tribal communities. Projects must demonstrate sustainability, include cross-sector partnerships, and comply with clarified budgeting and allocation methodologies (see amendment and FAQ documents). Maternal health allocations apply specifically to Region 3. Applications must document organizational structure and partner roles; future subrecipients need not be fully identified at submission.

data.title: Growing Clinical Training and Readiness – Certified Nurse Midwife Training Program
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Health
data.summary: The Indiana Department of Health, through Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Initiative 10, invites Indiana institutions of higher learning to apply for startup grant funding to establish an ACME-accredited Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM) training program culminating in a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) degree with Indiana APRN-CNM licensure. This initiative addresses critical shortages in the rural maternity care workforce, seeks to develop an in-state CNM education pipeline, and emphasizes development of rural clinical training partnerships and long-term workforce retention in underserved Indiana communities. Funding is supported by Indiana’s $207 million/year (Year 1) federal RHTP award.

data.title: Creating Healthier Rural Communities Through the End Zone for Chronic Disease Prevention
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The End Zone for Chronic Disease Prevention competitive grant supports population health improvements and chronic disease prevention in rural Tennessee, specifically through sustainable policy, systems, and environmental changes such as Healthy Food Environment strategies. Funded through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), this opportunity is open to rural hospitals, health systems, FQHCs, and community-based organizations serving maternal/infant health or coordinating rural health events. Applications may include activities in up to three eligible counties and must demonstrate how projects align with evidence-based interventions for nutrition security and chronic disease risk reduction.
applicantTypes: Other organizations experienced in maternal/infant health and event coordination

data.title: Nevada Rural Health Innovation and Technology (RHIT) Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: Funds technology and health innovation projects in rural Nevada. Intended to expand digital health tools, telehealth infrastructure, and data-driven care improvements. Projects must address practical, real-world technology needs in rural or frontier health care delivery and align with one of three tracks: core health IT, provider-facing digital health, and consumer-facing tools. Strong focus on interoperability, security, and sustainability.

data.title: Indiana ACO Feasibility Study (RHTP) RFP 26-87667
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Administration (IDOA) on behalf of Indiana Family and Social Services Administration (FSSA)
data.summary: The Indiana Department of Administration (IDOA), on behalf of the Family and Social Services Administration (FSSA), is soliciting proposals under RFP 26-87667 for a statewide Accountable Care Organization (ACO) Feasibility Study as part of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The contractor will assess provider readiness, analyze Medicaid ACO and bundled payment models, integrate managed care components, evaluate fiscal impacts, conduct stakeholder engagement, and develop recommendations for value-based care transformation in Indiana's rural communities. The contract is fully funded by CMS/HHS as part of a $206,927,896.80 federal award supporting the RHTP. Minority, Women, and Veteran-Owned Business (MWBE/IVOSB) participation is strongly encouraged, with set goals of 8%, 11%, and 3% respectively. Proposals must be submitted through the Indiana Supplier Portal. A pre-proposal conference will be available in person and virtually. Evaluation is based on technical proposal, qualifications, cost, MWBE/IVOSB commitments, and compliance. IV&V may be applied to all deliverables. See Attachments F, L, D, A, A1, and Addendum #1 for official requirements.
applicantTypes: Organizations with relevant large-scale healthcare feasibility and payment reform experience

data.title: RHTP Initiative 10 - OB Fellowship for Family Medicine Physicians
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP)
data.summary: On December 29, 2025, Indiana was awarded a federal grant of nearly $207 million for the first year of a five-year Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). This opportunity will provide funding to Indiana institutions to establish an OB Fellowship for Family Medicine Physicians in year one and support salaries for OB fellows for four additional years. The program aims to address rural maternity care provider shortages by training family medicine physicians in comprehensive obstetric care, including prenatal care of low- and high-risk pregnancies, inpatient labor and delivery, surgical obstetrics, contraception management, OB ultrasound, NICU rotations, and Maternal Fetal Medicine experience.

data.title: Connecticut RHTP – Health Care Coordination and Remote Patient Monitoring Using Artificial Intelligence (NOFO #26OHS001)
data.issuingAgency: Connecticut Office of Health Strategy (transferring to Office of Policy and Management, July 1, 2026)
data.summary: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) supports provider-led initiatives to implement Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled health care coordination and remote patient monitoring (RPM) models serving rural populations in Connecticut. Funded under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) and supported by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the program aims to expand access, improve outcomes in chronic and complex conditions, reduce avoidable utilization, and integrate innovative virtual care and RPM technologies with clinical workflows and the state health information exchange (Connie). Projects must deploy sustainable, technology-driven solutions that advance integration with EHRs, support measurable improvements in health outcomes, and address rural workforce and access barriers. Eligible applicants must demonstrate operational capability, financial stability, and experience with health IT or care coordination tools. Funding is performance-based and limited to new or meaningfully expanded activities directly serving rural residents.
applicantTypes: Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and FQHC Look-Alikes
Behavioral health and substance use disorder providers
Municipal and state/local public health agencies (delivering clinical services)
Maternity care programs with licensed clinical staff
Connecticut-based academic medical centers (or those formally partnered with a Connecticut clinical lead)
Multi-entity consortia with a Connecticut clinical lead
Federally recognized Tribes delivering health care in Connecticut

data.title: Missouri DHSS Rural Medical Student Clerkships Funding Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services
data.summary: Missouri DHSS is offering funding to support the development of new or expansion of existing medical student clerkship programs in rural health facilities. Eligible organizations must either establish a new medical school clerkship commitment serving at least three students annually or expand an existing clerkship program by two additional students each year. At least half of all clerkship rotation time must occur in Missouri’s ToRCH Care counties, defined as all Missouri counties except Boone, Cass, Clay, Greene, Jackson, Jefferson, Platte, St. Charles, St. Louis County, and St. Louis City. Applicants may receive up to $115,000 per contract, with the opportunity for two renewals. Any new partnership with a medical school must be operational no later than August 2027.

data.title: Expanding Worksite Clinics for On-the-Job Support
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: Solicits proposals from vendors to support the establishment, expansion, and operation of employer-aligned healthcare clinics across West Virginia, delivering preventive, occupational health, and limited acute care services along with care coordination and referral support to help employees manage their health and reduce work disruptions.
applicantTypes: For-profit or nonprofit organizations able to scale statewide

data.title: RHT-AFA-06-12-2026-CCG County Community Grant
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Office of Emergency Medical Services
data.summary: The RHT-AFA-06-12-2026-CCG County Community Grant, under West Virginia's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), provides funding to support the implementation and scaling of EMS-led community paramedicine, mobile-integrated health, and treat-in-place models across all counties in WVOEMS Region 1 (McDowell, Mercer, Monroe, Raleigh, Summers, Wyoming). Eligible state-licensed EMS agencies or partnerships must deliver protocol-authorized on-scene assessment, treatment, care navigation, and referral services; coordinate with primary care, behavioral health, and social service providers; and participate in the Connected Care Grid data exchange and reporting system. Key program goals include reducing avoidable emergency department utilization, improving timely access to care, and demonstrating measurable improvements in cost, quality, and outcomes. This competitive sub-award is a one-year opportunity with a required detailed budget, milestone-based funding, and robust monthly/quarterly reporting obligations. A County Level Service Form specifying covered counties and estimated population served is required.

data.title: West Virginia Connected Care Grid (CCG) – EMS Community Paramedicine and Treat-in-Place
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: The West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Connected Care Grid – EMS Community Paramedicine and Treat-in-Place Grant (RHT-AFA-06-12-2026-CCG) provides a total of $1,033,840 in Year 1 for state-licensed EMS agencies to implement and expand EMS-led community paramedicine, mobile-integrated health, and treat-in-place models in WVOEMS Region 1 (McDowell, Mercer, Monroe, Raleigh, Summers, Wyoming counties). Funded activities include protocol-authorized on-scene assessment and treatment, care navigation and referral, coordination with primary care and behavioral health providers, and full participation in statewide data sharing and evaluation. The program aims to reduce avoidable ED utilization, improve rural care access, and strengthen EMS integration statewide. Funding is milestone-based with strict CMS/HHS compliance, Maintenance of Effort, and rigorous monthly/quarterly reporting requirements. Applications are accepted only from eligible EMS agencies serving Region 1.

data.title: Behavioral Health Integration – Medications for Opioid and Alcohol Use Disorder
data.issuingAgency: Oklahoma State Department of Health (OSDH)
data.summary: Funding opportunity to expand access to medications for opioid and alcohol use disorder in rural Oklahoma, supporting provider upskilling, integrated/alternative care models, and telehealth. Competitive, RHTP/CMS/HHS supported, opportunity for subrecipient awards to grow behavioral health capacity.
applicantTypes: Other organizations serving rural Oklahoma communities

data.title: Rural Health Facilities Capital Improvement Program
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Department of Health (LDH)
data.summary: The Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), through the Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability, issues this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) to support capital investments for rural healthcare providers. The program aims to strengthen rural health infrastructure, expand access to diverse healthcare services (including primary, specialty, maternity, behavioral health, cancer, and emergency care), modernize clinical facilities and equipment, and support sustainable innovation in care delivery. Funding prioritizes ready-to-implement projects with measurable outcomes that address local health challenges and improve long-term sustainability for rural providers.

data.title: Telehealth Infrastructure for Rural Access Program
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Department of Health (LDH)
data.summary: The Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), through the Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability, is issuing this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) to support targeted investments in telehealth infrastructure for rural Louisiana. The program funds upgrades and implementation of telehealth networks, remote patient monitoring (RPM), and connected care platforms to expand access to specialty, behavioral health, prenatal, and chronic care services in rural and underserved parishes. Projects must demonstrate measurable improvements in rural health outcomes.
applicantTypes: Behavioral health agencies serving rural populations
Other eligible organizations serving rural patients (see NOFO Section C and Eligibility Definition doc)

data.title: Promoting Access, Coordination, and Transformation (PACT)
data.issuingAgency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DF&A)
data.summary: The Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DF&A) requests proposals for the Promoting Access, Coordination, and Transformation (PACT) initiative, a core part of the Arkansas Rural Health Transformation Program. PACT is designed to modernize Arkansas’s rural health system, expand access to care, and improve provider coordination through integrated networks, workforce alignment, and technology-enabled infrastructure. Competitive, multi-category grants are available to eligible rural entities demonstrating collaborative and system-wide impact.

data.title: Mobile Integrated Healthcare Implementation Services
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services, Department of Health
data.summary: The Vermont Agency of Human Services, Department of Health, is soliciting Letters of Interest from qualified Vermont EMS agencies and hospital-based EMS programs for Mobile Integrated Healthcare (MIH) implementation at up to five rural sites, as part of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Year 1 grant funding ($3,750,000 total) will support operationally ready EMS organizations delivering post-discharge in-home care for Congestive Heart Failure, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, or Joint Replacement Care. Funding is intended for personnel, training, vehicles, technology, clinical equipment, and implementation expenses. Project goals are to improve care quality, reduce costs, and strengthen the rural health workforce. Initial grant performance period is August 1, 2026 – September 30, 2027. Grants may be extended for up to four additional one-year periods, pending CMS and state approval.

data.title: Emerging Technology Program – Rural Health Transformation Plan (Kansas Program Year 1)
data.issuingAgency: Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE)
data.summary: The Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) is soliciting applications for the Emerging Technology Program, a key component of the Kansas Rural Health Transformation Plan under the federal CMS Rural Health Transformation Program. Year 1 provides $9.5 million in FY26 for 5–10 rural provider-led projects deploying proven technology solutions that improve care delivery, sustainability, and benefit to rural Kansans. Awards are $1–3M per project. Eligible providers include rural hospitals, clinics, health centers, tribal facilities, community behavioral health clinics, SUD providers, and long-term care, plus others if projects directly benefit rural areas. Non-rural entities may participate only if activities are focused on rural impact. Technology firms may only participate as vendors. Applications, with required supporting documentation, must be submitted via the designated Smartsheet portal by 12:00 PM CT, July 10, 2026. Award announcements are tentatively scheduled for August 7, 2026, with a project period from August 15, 2026 to September 30, 2027. Indirect and admin costs are capped at 10%. Awards contingent on KDHE’s receipt of federal funds. All other program and procurement requirements per 2 CFR are incorporated.
applicantTypes: Native American Sovereign Tribe Healthcare Facility

data.title: Wild, Wonderful and Healthy WV
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health, Bureau for Public Health, Office of Community Health Systems and Health Promotion, Division of Rural Health and Recruitment / State Office of Rural Health
data.summary: The West Virginia Department of Health is soliciting grant applications for the State Office of Rural Health Community Development Program under the 'Wild, Wonderful and Healthy WV' initiative. The program funds evidence-based health and economic development proposals to advance rural health transformation and local economic outcomes. Eligible applicants must submit through the WV Oasis Vendor Self-Serve portal by the deadline. Reviewers will score on program experience, budget detail, and adherence to federal and state guidelines.

data.title: Maternal & Perinatal Health Lead Agencies - Idaho RHTP (FFY26)
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Dept of Health and Welfare (DHW)
data.summary: The Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (DHW) is soliciting applications for two lead agencies: (1) Maternal Health - Obstetrics Lead Agency to support rural obstetric readiness through quality improvement (QI) initiatives and deployment of the Emergency Readiness Resource Kit; (2) Perinatal Quality Collaborative Lead Agency to expand rural hospital participation in perinatal collaboratives, aiming to add 8 new rural sites by 2030. Year 1 funding is $1,200,000 for the Obstetrics Lead Agency and $2,400,000 for the Perinatal Quality Collaborative, totaling $3,600,000 for FFY26. These initiatives target enhanced maternal and infant outcomes in Idaho's rural populations.

data.title: State Fiscal Year 2026 Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas (HHS0017228)
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
data.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) is soliciting applications for the State Fiscal Year 2026 Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas. This $10 million grant program aims to connect Rural Hospitals (RHs) and Rural Health Clinics (RHCs) in Texas with pediatric specialists, pediatric subspecialists through telemedicine medical services, and institutions affiliated with the Texas Child Mental Health Care Consortium. Funding may be used for technology, equipment, service contracts, training, and minor facility renovations to expand pediatric and mental health access in rural areas.

data.title: Healthcare Resiliency Program (HRP): Service Line Expansion & Co-Location
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The Healthcare Resiliency Program (HRP): Service Line Expansion & Co-Location is a competitive grant through the Tennessee Department of Health supporting rural hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs), and co-located clinics to implement or expand primary, specialty, behavioral, and social health service lines. The program aims to improve access and quality of health services for rural Tennesseans by facilitating service integration, care collaboration, and sustainability through digital models and value-based care, with emphasis on perinatal, behavioral health, emergency, pediatric, and chronic care coordination services.

data.title: New York Rural Community Health Integration (RCHI) Funding Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: New York State Department of Health
data.summary: New York State Department of Health is allocating $76,190,022 in Budget Period 1 (Sept 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027) of the Rural Health Transformation Program to support Rural Community Health Integration (RCHI) — Initiative 1 of NY's five-year RHTP. RCHI establishes coordinated rural health partnerships to improve care coordination, patient access, financial sustainability, and health outcomes across rural communities. Applications may request up to $500,000 per county for planning and up to $3,000,000 for up to three implementation projects. The minimum geographic unit is a county; multi-county collaborative applications are encouraged. Funded by CMS/HHS as part of a $212,058,207.80 total federal award.

data.title: WV Birth to Three Regional Administrative Unit (RAU)
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health, Bureau for Public Health, Office of Maternal, Child and Family Health, WV Birth to Three
data.summary: The WV Birth to Three Program is seeking applicants to operate Regional Administrative Units (RAU) for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. RAUs are responsible for implementing local System Point of Entry functions, administrative oversight of data entry into the WVBTT Online data system, and facilitating child find, interagency and family engagement activities. Activities must align with WVBTT policy and program requirements. Funding is for one year (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027) with potential for renewal based on performance, program success, and continued availability of state and/or federal funds. The grant agreement requires compliance with applicable federal regulations (2 CFR 200) and is managed via the WVOASIS Vendor Self-Service Portal.
applicantTypes: Other eligible entities as described in solicitation

data.title: GREAT Health Workforce Retention Technology Grant (Surgical Robots)
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH)
data.summary: This grant, under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), provides up to $2,000,000 per award to rural Georgia hospitals for the acquisition and implementation of robotic surgical technology, aiming to expand access, retain surgical workforce, and support current and future GME programs. All funds must be fully expended by September 30, 2027. Only technology-ready rural hospitals with a history or plan for surgical robotics and compliance with outlined clinical, facility, and administrative requirements may be considered.

data.title: Rural Health Telehealth Enhancements Grant
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH)
data.summary: The Georgia Rural Health Transformation Program (GREAT Health) Initiative 3: Connecting to Care to Improve Healthcare Access – Telehealth Enhancements supports projects that modernize digital infrastructure, expand specialty and behavioral health access, and build workforce capacity for rural healthcare providers in Georgia. Up to $10,000,000 is available in Year 1, with funds to expand telehealth delivery and sustainability. Priority will be given to rural hospitals previously participating in the AHEAD Model pre-implementation. All awarded funds must be expended by September 30, 2027; unallowable costs include new construction, services reimbursable by insurance, food/meals, pre-award costs, or duplicate funding sources. Applicants must demonstrate sustainability beyond the grant period.

data.title: 2026 Telehealth Hub Connectivity, Equipment & Education Grant Program (TCE)
data.issuingAgency: Mississippi State Department of Health (MSDH)
data.summary: The Mississippi State Department of Health Telehealth Hub Connectivity, Equipment & Education Grant Program (TCE) supports telehealth hubs, equipment, connectivity, platform integration, technical support, provider training, patient outreach, multilingual education, and community demonstrations serving rural Mississippi. TCE is part of the Rural Health Transformation Plan (the Plan) and is funded under the Cooperative Agreement with the Federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHT Program). The amended NOFO lists $5.7 million for Program Year 1 and anticipates 25–30 connectivity/equipment awards averaging $70,000 and 25–30 education awards averaging $110,000. Awards will be made to subrecipients, subject to Federal and State requirements, on a reimbursement basis except where advance funding is demonstrated to be necessary and is limited as a percentage of the total award. Funds must be obligated by October 30, 2026 and project costs incurred by July 31, 2027. Indirect and administrative costs may not exceed 5%. All funded projects must provide meaningful benefit to rural Mississippi as defined in the NOFO, and subrecipients are required to participate in the Statewide Health Information Exchange.
applicantTypes: Native American Sovereign Tribe healthcare facilities

data.title: 2026 Rural Provider Technology Grant Program (RTG)
data.issuingAgency: Mississippi State Department of Health (MSDH)
data.summary: The Mississippi State Department of Health Rural Provider Technology Grant Program (RTG) funds rural provider technology hardware and software, interoperability and statewide HIE onboarding, cybersecurity, data integrity, workflow and operational technology, implementation, integration, and training. The amended NOFO lists $47.5 million for Program Year 1. It anticipates 75–100 general-technology awards of $200,000–$400,000 and 60–100 cybersecurity awards of $100,000–$300,000. Telehealth, EHR, broadband, new construction, major expansion, lobbying, and provider payments are excluded.
applicantTypes: Native American Sovereign Tribe healthcare facilities

data.title: 2026 Rural Capital Project Care Gap Closure Grant Program (RCGC)
data.issuingAgency: Mississippi State Department of Health (MSDH)
data.summary: The Mississippi State Department of Health Rural Capital Project Care Gap Closure Grant Program (RCGC) provides Program Year 1 capital funding for facility renovations, infrastructure projects, equipment, service-capacity expansion, and operational improvements that close documented rural healthcare gaps. The amended NOFO lists $28.5 million available and anticipates approximately 20–30 awards, with individual awards described as up to $3 million. Telehealth, cybersecurity, EHR, broadband, new construction or major building expansion, lobbying, provider payments, and other prohibited costs are excluded.
applicantTypes: Native American Sovereign Tribe healthcare facilities

data.title: Rural BH Modernization (CCBHC) Infrastructure & Sustainability Grant
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board
data.summary: The South Dakota Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Initiative is soliciting applications for the Rural BH Modernization (CCBHC) Infrastructure & Sustainability Grant (RFA #26-08RHT-016), with $9.7 million in federal funds available for Budget Period 1. This opportunity supports system-level behavioral health improvements for development, expansion, and sustainability of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHC), explicitly strengthening access and quality of care in rural and frontier South Dakota. Funding priorities include provider capacity building, crisis services expansion, IT infrastructure development, and workforce development. Eligible applicants are exclusively organizations selected for the 2026 CCBHC Planning Grant Cohort. Applicants must demonstrate readiness, advance CCBHC certification progress, report measurable outcomes, and describe sustainability plans post-award. There is no cost share/match requirement. Applications are due July 15, 2026, via the South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board portal. The grant support period runs from agreement execution (~Aug 1, 2026) through July 30, 2027, with potential renewals up to five years. See https://dss.sd.gov/behavioralhealth/grantinfo.aspx for further guidance and certification requirements.

data.title: Rural Physician/APP Recruitment, DLI-RFP-2026-0088DL
data.issuingAgency: Montana Department of Labor and Industry
data.summary: Montana Department of Labor and Industry seeks proposals for integrated talent attraction, marketing, and direct recruitment services to support healthcare employers in rural and frontier counties, including recruitment of physicians, advanced practice providers, and registered nurses.

data.title: Statewide Emergency Medical Dispatch System for Montana Public Safety Answering Points
data.issuingAgency: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS) / State Procurement Services Division (SPSD)
data.summary: The State of Montana is soliciting proposals from qualified vendors to provide all labor, materials, equipment, software, licensing, implementation, integration, training, maintenance, and support to establish a statewide Emergency Medical Dispatch System for participating Montana Public Safety Answering Points (PSAPs). The goal is to enhance emergency medical dispatch capabilities across Montana in alignment with rural health transformation initiatives. The system must serve 35 PSAPs and meet national EMS standards, including NENA, ASTM, NHTSA, NFPA, AHA, and CPR-related criteria. Federal funds are involved and awarded contractors are required to be registered in SAM.gov and comply with all mandatory prerequisites and documents.

data.title: RHTP CHANT Care Coordination Case Management Information System (CMIS)
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health, Division of Family Health and Wellness
data.summary: RFP 34347-04626. Selecting a contractor to install, operate, and maintain the CHANT Care Coordination Case Management Information System (CMIS) for the Community Health Access and Navigation in Tennessee program. Confidential solicitation requiring NDA before full details disclosed.

data.title: Rural Cybersecurity Modernization Assessment
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health & Welfare
data.summary: Seeks a qualified contractor to assess and modernize cybersecurity for approximately eighty rural healthcare facilities (focus on skilled nursing). Includes security assessments, architecture recommendations, and training.

data.title: Request for Information (RFI): Implementation Partner Services for a State-Managed EHR
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Department of Health, Office of Rural Health (Louisiana Rural Health Transformation Program - LA RHTP)
data.summary: This Request for Information (RFI) seeks input from organizations with experience in EHR implementation, systems integration, provider onboarding, and staffing to support the rollout and ongoing support of a new state-managed, CMS-certified electronic health record for rural Louisiana providers. The State is seeking information to inform upcoming competitive solicitations for implementation partners. Responses should address expertise, approach, phasing, and indicative costs, focusing on rural and safety-net provider environments.

data.title: Enhancing Sustainable EMS, EMS Workforce, Infrastructure, etc.
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board
data.summary: The South Dakota Department of Health is soliciting proposals for the Enhancing Sustainable Emergency Medical Services (EMS): EMS Workforce, Infrastructure, and System Modernization Initiative under the Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Project. Up to $8,000,000 in total funding is available for project-based awards to support rural, frontier, and Tribal EMS system transformation. Projects may address workforce development, specialized equipment/technology integration, regional EMS coordination, and clinical quality improvement. Successful applicants will propose solutions that improve sustainability, readiness, and quality of care in South Dakota's EMS systems. Depending on project type, contract forms may include grant agreements or other state-approved mechanisms. The anticipated contract period is August 5, 2026 – July 31, 2027, with up to three possible one-year renewals.
applicantTypes: South Dakota Tribal governments, Tribal EMS agencies, or Tribal healthcare organizations
South Dakota hospitals, health systems, and critical access hospitals
South Dakota public safety agencies, emergency communications centers, and dispatch organizations
Educational institutions, technical colleges, universities, and EMS training programs
Nonprofit organizations with relevant EMS, healthcare, workforce, or public health expertise
Healthcare technology vendors and interoperability partners

Consultants or organizations with demonstrated expertise in EMS system development, clinical quality improvement, workforce development, healthcare integration, operational coordination, or EMS sustainability initiatives

data.title: North Carolina Minority Diabetes Prevention Program – Region 8: RHT Grant FY 2026
data.issuingAgency: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities
data.summary: The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (NCDHHS), Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities, seeks qualified applicants to deliver the Minority Diabetes Prevention Program in Region 8 (Bladen, Brunswick, Columbus, Duplin, New Hanover, Onslow, Pender, Robeson, Sampson counties). Grantees must screen at least 165 residents for prediabetes, enroll a minimum of 50 participants in a CDC-recognized 12-month lifestyle change program, ensure at least 60% participation from minoritized populations, and coordinate at least 4 12-month lifestyle class series. The project must maintain CDC DPRP recognition, establish collaborative partnerships (including Tribal engagement when applicable), provide outreach and quality improvement, submit a Project Plan per Division guidance, and comply with fiscal/programmatic reporting requirements. Year 1 funding is $195,105 (100% federal via CMS RHT Program). Per Addendum 1 (issued June 19, 2026), the submission deadline was extended to July 10, 2026, 5:00 PM ET, and participant eligibility was clarified to require CDC DPRP eligibility (qualifying prediabetes blood test, history of gestational diabetes, or a positive prediabetes risk screening) in addition to BMI/age/no-prior-diagnosis criteria. Per Addendum 2 (issued July 2, 2026), Year 1 award amount is revised to $195,105 and the application deadline is extended to July 17, 2026, 5:00 PM ET. Applications are due via email to OMHHD@dhhs.nc.gov.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation School-Based Health Center (RT27)
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health, Bureau of Maternal, Child, & Family Health
data.summary: The Ohio Department of Health, Bureau of Maternal, Child, & Family Health invites competitive applications from local or public non-profit healthcare agencies for projects to plan, establish, expand, or sustain school-based health centers (SBHCs) in designated rural Ohio counties. Supported activities include SBHC business planning, site renovations, equipment purchase, outreach, staffing, evaluation, and participation in ODH technical assistance. SBHCs must provide accessible medical, mental, dental, and vision care directly in schools for rural populations. Projects may target new sites, start-up operations, or the expansion/sustainability of existing SBHCs.

data.title: HFS Social Health Care Network (SHCN) Program
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
data.summary: The Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS) released NOFO #3997-20-26-SHCN for the Social Health Care Network (SHCN) Program. HFS is seeking one statewide 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization to serve as a lead entity responsible for developing, maintaining, and strengthening a network of community-based organizations (CBOs) delivering health-related social needs (HRSN) services to Medicaid beneficiaries under the Illinois 1115 waiver. The SHCN will be responsible for building provider network capacity, supporting CBOs (including small, culturally-competent, and regionally distributed organizations) in becoming Medicaid providers for HRSN, community health worker, maternal health, violence prevention, reentry, and related services. Responsibilities include technical assistance, onboarding for Medicaid billing and closed-loop referral platforms (ICARRS and billing/claims), infrastructure and capacity building, contract management with MCOs and CBOs, and reporting on network adequacy and performance. A minimum of $3M (of up to $8M available for the 9-month first cycle) must be subgranted to CBOs for capacity building. The SHCN must be able to process philanthropic grants. The contract is anticipated to begin October 1, 2026, with an initial 9-month term (through June 30, 2027), renewable subject to budget appropriations.

data.title: Establish the Tennessee Memory Care Assessment Network (MCAN)
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The Tennessee Memory Care Assessment Network (MCAN) is a statewide hub-and-spoke initiative under the Tennessee Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). MCAN is designed to expand access to memory assessment and diagnostic services, advance early dementia detection, and promote provider education throughout rural and underserved Tennessee communities. Through a single-award, one organization will manage MCAN implementation, subcontract with four to five rural clinics (five satellite sites minimum), develop and disseminate standardized dementia diagnosis protocols, and coordinate care navigation and referral to Dementia Navigators. Additional responsibilities include IT platform development for secure health information sharing, evaluation data infrastructure, provider engagement, and participant/caregiver referral management. The maximum total funding is $16.5 million for MCAN over a 50-month project period, with annual and clinic-expansion allocations as stipulated. Quarterly reporting and compliance with TDH and federal requirements are mandatory. Applicants must demonstrate organizational capacity to deliver required network activities; detailed receipts, payment overviews, and compliance documentation are required with invoices.

data.title: Indiana Rural Physician Incentive Grant Opportunity (RHTP Initiative 10)
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Health (IDOH)
data.summary: This competitive grant, administered by the Indiana Department of Health under the Rural Health Transformation Program, provides up to $300,000 in incentives for eligible Indiana-licensed physicians (MD/DO) who commit to full-time clinical practice at a HRSA-designated rural site for a 5-year period. Funds are awarded to the employer for distribution to the physician, with annual reporting required regarding disbursement, employment, and program compliance. The program addresses critical rural workforce shortages statewide; awards are made each year of RHTP funding.

data.title: West Virginia Newborn Hearing Screening Project
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health, Bureau for Public Health, Office of Maternal, Child and Family Health, Division of Children's Specialty Care
data.summary: Supports West Virginia Hands & Voices in delivering statewide parent-to-parent follow-up services, parent support education, and family activities for infants referred to the Newborn Hearing Screening (NHS) Project. These services are provided to deaf and hard-of-hearing (DHH) children and families across the state to help guide them through the EHDI system and to offer emotional support as they process their child's diagnosis of hearing loss. The grantee must provide timely outreach, parent education, and required data and financial reporting in compliance with NHS and Early Hearing Detection and Intervention guidelines. Funding is available for April 1, 2025, through March 31, 2026. Services help meet objectives including initiation of follow-up services within two business days of referral, support for DHH families, timely and accurate data maintenance, and collaboration with the NHS Project Director.
applicantTypes: West Virginia Hands & Voices Parent Support Program
Entities with valid West Virginia business license

data.title: HTP Restoring WV's Workforce
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health – Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: This Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA) seeks applications for the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) – Health to Prosperity: Restoring WV’s Workforce through Health-to-Work Programs for Substance Use Disorder (SUD). The program aims to reduce unemployment and avoidable absenteeism in West Virginia by supporting the implementation and expansion of return-to-work (RTW) and recovery-to-work coordination models for individuals whose substance use disorders are barriers to employment. Funded activities must focus on strategies such as liaison-based coordination, employer engagement, clinical and recovery support referrals, standardized RTW planning, and robust data reporting to the statewide RHTP data spine. The grant emphasizes preventative, root-cause approaches and requires demonstration of scalability and sustainability beyond Year 1. Funding is performance-based with reimbursement tied to milestone deliverables, and grantees are expected to coordinate across RHTP’s other initiatives to maximize outcomes and data integration. Applicants must demonstrate both operational readiness and governance capacity for rapid program launch and ongoing compliance with reporting requirements. This opportunity is funded via CMS/HHS and supports Governor Morrisey’s ‘Four Pillars of a Healthy West Virginia’ and the ‘Making America Healthy Again (MAHA)’ initiative.

data.title: Improve Health Outcomes Through Nutrition and Lifestyle AFA 1
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA) RHT-AFA-06-24-2026-PHA under the West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Personal Health Accelerator (PHA) initiative. Approximately $24,020,000 is available to fund clinically integrated nutrition and lifestyle intervention programs serving high-risk and rural populations throughout West Virginia. The primary aim is to reduce the state's chronic disease burden—including diabetes, obesity, hypertension, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, substance use disorder, and long-term care needs—while improving measurable health outcomes, increasing workforce participation, and advancing value-based care. Funded projects must demonstrate evidence-based, scalable, and sustainable solutions that address upstream root causes through prevention, nutrition, physical activity, behavior change, and integration with healthcare technology and coordinated care models. All funded interventions are performance-based and tied to achieving State-defined milestones, outcome targets, and timely reporting. Grantees must coordinate with the State's Connected Care Grid Data Spine, comply with all CMS/HHS requirements, and deliver population-level impact consistent with the Seven RHTP flagship initiatives. The award offers seven Program Options, with applicants required to submit option-specific narratives, detailed budgets, and county-level service forms per option. All counties in West Virginia are eligible, with priority for high-need rural areas identified by chronic disease burden and access gaps. Full program details, funding requirements, and reporting schedules are provided in the AFA and Q&A.
applicantTypes: Local partners (health alliances, home health agencies, pharmacies, multi-partner collaboratives with a single accountable lead)
Other third-party vendors supporting clinical and wellness interventions and navigation in WV

data.title: RHTP HRP: Rural Non-Emergency Transportation
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: This opportunity supports rural non-emergency medical transportation for eligible health care partners in Tennessee. It is part of the Tennessee Department of Health’s RHTP second-wave RFP series, with anticipated release July 6–20, 2026. Opportunity will be posted and applications accepted through the TN Department of General Services Procurement Portal.

data.title: West Virginia RHT-AFA: Health to Work Program for Substance Use Disorder (SUD)
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health
data.summary: Part of Governor Morrisey's $10.5M 'return-to-work' announcement (solicitation RHT-AFA-07-06-2026-HTP). Provides $2,000,000 for recovery-focused return-to-work programs for people whose substance use disorder has contributed to unemployment or workforce disruption — proposals may include peer recovery support, recovery navigation, coordination of treatment and recovery services, employer engagement, and structured pathways back into employment. Distinct from the already-tracked Chronic-Conditions track (RHT-AFA-06-30-2026-HTP, ~$8.5M, same due date), which is a separate solicitation under the same Health-to-Prosperity/Health-to-Work umbrella.

data.title: Michigan Rural Health Partnerships Healthy Aging - 2026
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary:
Synopsis 
 As part of RHTP’s Care Closer to Home Blueprint Initiative, the Promoting Healthy Aging in Rural Communities Blueprint aims to transform access to care in rural communities by creating sustainable, community-based pathways that bring health services closer to where people live and work. By connecting partners across health and social sectors, the initiative reimagine care delivery, improve transportation access, and simplify access to primary and behavioral health. Through innovative approaches to chronic disease management, maternal and child health, and behavioral health, it seeks to improve outcomes while making care more efficient, coordinated, and person-centered. This funding opportunity will help rural residents age in place and access health care in their communities, while reducing costly visits to higher acuity settings and emergency departments.

data.title: Michigan Rural Health Hub and Spoke Mobile Health - 2026
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary:
Synopsis 
 As part of RHTP's Care Closer to Hime Blueprint Initiative, the Rural Health Care Delivery Hub and Spoke Model aims to transform access to care in rural communities by creating sustainable, community-based pathways that bring health services closer to where people live and work.
