data.title: Personal Health Accelerator (PHA) Wellness Data & Referral Program
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: The Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA) solicits applications for a single, statewide program operator to design, implement, and operate the Personal Health Accelerator (PHA) Integrated Wellness Data & Closed-Loop Referral Program. The awardee will be responsible for end-to-end program performance, including deploying a closed-loop referral system supporting statewide integration of wellness, nutrition, and lifestyle interventions with core medical data systems. Responsibilities include provider and CBO onboarding, change management, technology implementation, evidence-based referral tracking, quantitative and qualitative reporting, and real-time State access to all program data. The program must not duplicate activities funded by Medicaid MCOs, Medicare, other grants, or any payer/entity legally responsible. All activities shall support the Governor’s Four Pillars of a Healthy West Virginia, align with RHTP/CMS priorities, and require integration with State platforms and CMS-aligned data/reporting. The primary grantee must demonstrate capacity for milestone-based performance management, sustainability planning, verified engagement and completion of referrals, county-level reporting, and measurable impact within defined timeframes in referral utilization, completion, participant health outcomes, healthcare cost/utilization reduction, and workforce/economic impact. Minimum platform functionality within 60 days of contract execution includes live referral initiation, CBO receipt and disposition, audit-log of referral status, and readiness for real-time State access. All grantees must rigorously document non-duplication controls, data integration readiness (including interface standards and security), and commitment to privacy and data governance. Scalability and sustainability beyond Year 1 must be demonstrated. Applications must clearly justify budget allocations, distinguishing healthcare provider payments (subject to 15% cap) from programmatic/infrastructure costs, and comply with performance-based milestone reimbursement.
applicantTypes: Multi-Partner Collaboratives/Coalitions/Consortiums (single lead applicant) with ability to scale statewide
Third-Party Vendors (with closed-loop referral platform and demonstrated operational capacity)
Other Entities demonstrating statewide operator capacity (see eligibilityText for full restrictions)

data.title: West Virginia Connected Care Grid (CCG) Hub & Spoke Model Grant
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health – Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP)
data.summary: The Connected Care Grid – Hub & Spoke Care Delivery Initiative is a competitive funding opportunity under West Virginia’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) to design, implement, and scale hub-and-spoke care delivery models that expand access to coordinated, high-quality care for rural West Virginians. Centralized hubs (hospitals, academic medical centers, specialty providers, or regional health organizations—physical or virtual) deliver clinical expertise, care coordination, workforce support, and standardized protocols to community-based spokes (e.g., schools, employers, libraries, community centers, mobile units) targeting counties lacking adequate healthcare access. The program aims to (1) reduce preventable emergency department use, (2) improve chronic disease and behavioral/mental health outcomes, (3) increase workforce participation, and (4) build sustainable models aligned with public/private payment systems and the broader RHTP ecosystem. Initiatives must be scalable, designed for long-term commercial sustainability, and prioritize measurable impacts on health and workforce participation. All funded models are required to fully integrate with the State’s data systems (RHTP data spine and WVHIN), support rigorous milestone-based accountability, enable county- and statewide reporting, and strictly comply with CMS/HHS, state, HIPAA, and 42 CFR Part 2 (as applicable) requirements. Funding is disbursed in milestones: 25% advance for start-up, 25% upon hub launch/half of spokes operational, and 50% upon full spoke network and integration with the WVHIN. Funds cannot supplant existing efforts or serve as cost-share for other programs without approval. Grantees must submit regular financial and programmatic reports, actively participate in CMS/state governance and data activities, and collaborate with concurrent RHTP initiatives and regional partners. Failure to achieve milestones or meet compliance may result in suspension or reallocation of funds.

data.title: Statewide Data Spine

The Data Spine will create a unified, secure, and interoperable data infrastructure to integrate, standardize, and enable exchange of multi-source data across clinical, claims, community, workforce, and public health systems to advance rural health transformation. Supported by CMS (HHS) financial award #RHT26*4 totaling $199,476,098.72 (100% federally funded). Proposals are evaluated based on best value, not lowest cost. Submission through WV Oasis Vendor Self Service (VSS) portal required. Additional instructions for eligibility, preferred vendor status, bonds, insurance, privacy/security compliance, and background checks are included. Key deadlines: Questions due June 25, 2026, 1:00 p.m. EDT; proposals due July 7, 2026, 10:30 a.m. EDT.

data.title: Improve Health Outcomes Through Nutrition and Lifestyle
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health, Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: The State of West Virginia, through its Department of Health's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), announces this competitive Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA) for qualified organizations to design, implement, and operate clinically integrated nutrition and lifestyle intervention programs statewide, targeting rural, high-risk populations. Supported by CMS/HHS under the Personal Health Accelerator (PHA) flagship initiative, funded programs must deliver measurable health improvements in key domains including chronic disease reduction, enhanced workforce participation, and reduced healthcare utilization and costs. All programs must establish provider referral pathways; deliver structured, evidence-based interventions; track participant engagement and outcomes; regularly report performance metrics; and integrate data with the state’s Connected Care Grid Data Spine. Funding is milestone-based, time-bound, and subject to performance accountability, with clear requirements for scalability and long-term sustainability through payer/value-based care alignment. Programs will be held to administrative cost limitations, matching/cost share preferences, and stringent privacy/security standards. Applicants may propose one or more of seven defined program options spanning metabolic & cardiovascular health, respiratory health, SUD, and senior care, each with specific engagement, outcome, and reporting benchmarks.

data.title: Rural Dental Efficiency and Access Grant

data.title: Healthcare Resiliency Program: Health Technology and Innovation (Short Range) RFA #34320-20327
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The Tennessee Department of Health (TDH) will award competitive grants under RFA #34320-20327 to support the implementation, procurement, or expansion of health technology solutions addressing rural healthcare needs in Tennessee. The Healthcare Resiliency Program: Health Technology and Innovation (Short Range) opportunity is open to a wide range of applicants including rural hospitals, community-based organizations, non- and for-profit technology vendors, local governments, educational institutions, FQHCs, behavioral health providers, and others serving Tennessee’s 89 designated rural counties (all except Shelby, Madison, Davidson, Hamilton, Knox, and Sullivan). Projects may focus on adoption and expansion of telehealth, remote patient monitoring, digital health, data interoperability, EMR/EHR systems (with limits), technology infrastructure, workforce training, and technology-enabled care coordination. Purchases of first-time certified EMR/EHR systems are allowable; EMR/EHR replacements are limited to a statewide 5% funding cap of the total RHT funding awarded to the state during a budget period. Upgrades, enhancements, and modules to existing EMR/EHRs are allowable and not subject to the 5% cap. Equipment, software, interoperability, cybersecurity, provider and patient engagement technology, mobile or community-based innovations, and related training/support are eligible. No construction or capital expenditures that materially increase asset value or building life span are allowed; minor renovations or alterations may be allowed, capped at 20% statewide of total RHT funding, and require prior approval. There are no minimum or maximum award amounts set for individual projects, but awards are capped by the available total program funding of $33,000,000 for the one-year period (2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31). Indirect and administrative costs combined are capped at 10%. Both for-profit and nonprofit entities may apply; all applicants must be registered with the TN Secretary of State unless excepted. Activities must benefit rural counties as defined by TDH. Applicants headquartered outside rural counties may apply but all funded activities must serve eligible areas. Quarterly and annual reporting, as well as eligibility and audit compliance, are required. All federal and state procurement and cost principles apply.

data.title: MSCF Rotational Staffing Pools AFA
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: This Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA) under the Mountain State Care Force (MSCF) and Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) seeks proposals for the design, implementation, and operation of rotational staffing pools for rural healthcare providers across West Virginia. The aim is to increase workforce participation, stabilize rural health system capacity, reduce reliance on external staffing agencies, and expand access to WV-licensed clinicians. Models should prioritize both immediate gap coverage and long-term workforce stability, using innovative approaches such as telemedicine and partnerships with residency programs. Funding will be awarded to entities demonstrating scalable, outcome-driven models for staffing pool operations and governance, with accountability for end-to-end staffing performance, measurable outcomes, and integration with State data platforms and reporting requirements. Applications must include a detailed governance strategy, operational model, workforce strategy, budget, and demonstrate readiness to deploy WV-based workforce. The program is tied to milestone deliverables and structured to promote regional scalability and cross-system collaboration. All data, reports, and operational products must be accessible to the State in real time for oversight, analytics, and reporting.

data.title: North Dakota Harnessing Artificial Intelligence Innovation Funding Opportunity (Solicitation 210-430)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services - Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services, through the Rural Health Transformation Program, is offering a competitive funding opportunity to support rural organizations implementing artificial intelligence (AI) innovation projects that expand rural healthcare delivery capacity. Funded solutions must serve rural North Dakota residents, including rural tribal communities, and demonstrate measurable improvements in early detection, access, patient experience, and care quality via AI-enabled approaches. This funding is aligned with Initiative 4 of North Dakota’s RHTP. Approximately $1,000,000 is available for Year 1, with anticipated awards of around $200,000 per organization. Applications are due July 29, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. CT, and projects must be completed by September 30, 2027.

data.title: Electronic Medical Record Enhancement Funding Opportunity (Solicitation 210-411)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS), through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), offers competitive funding to support enhancements to existing Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems among eligible rural and tribal health providers. This funding opportunity, as outlined under Initiative 4: 'Connect Tech, Data and Providers for a Stronger North Dakota', Theme 1: 'Breaking Data Barriers—Enhance existing EHRs with additional technology and AI add-ons,' is focused on proposals that directly strengthen service delivery, improve patient outcomes and experience, increase access to care, reduce wait times, and reinforce cybersecurity. Only projects enhancing established EMR systems are eligible—EMR replacements are addressed in separate, future opportunities. Up to $10 million is available in Year 1, with estimated average awards of $500,000 and approximately 20 anticipated recipients. Projects must use the ND HHS Itemized Subrecipient Budget Template (Excel; one tab per strategy) with cost justifications. Projects must be fully implemented and all funds expended by September 30, 2027. Priority is given to applications demonstrating measurable improvements in patient outcomes, expanded access, and reductions in wait times for rural/tribal residents. Awardees are ineligible for subsequent RHTP EMR replacement funding. Only one application per eligible organization is permitted.
applicantTypes: Non-federally operated Indian Health Service facilities

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program - Centralized Tool to Guide Interfacility Transfers
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services, Central Office
data.summary: The Vermont Agency of Human Services seeks proposals under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) for a subrecipient grant to assess, plan, and implement a centralized tool guiding interfacility transfers statewide. Supported by CMS/HHS funding ($195.05M total in year one, 100% CMS-funded), the project’s initial 11-month award period expects the selected organization to conduct a comprehensive feasibility assessment, develop an implementation-ready blueprint, and execute a live pilot deployment at an independent hospital. Required tasks include evaluating care coordination infrastructure, stakeholder engagement, and designing a scalable operating, governance, and technology model for capacity management and transfer coordination across Vermont’s health system (hospitals, EMS, rural providers, etc.). Deliverables: statewide operating model, governance framework including EMS integration, technology/interoperability strategy, performance measurement plan, phased implementation roadmap, and sustainability plan for scaling post-grant. The solution must prioritize rural and unaffiliated organizations, enable equitable participation, streamline transfer coordination, and strengthen system resilience and integration. Award is for planning, feasibility, and initial implementation; future expansion subject to available funding and State/CMS review.

Up to 10 awards expected, approximately $50,000 each. Equipment requested should be specific and include brand, model, features, cost information, and justification of need. Application via Qualtrics, one per organization. Performance period starts upon execution and ends September 30, 2027. Funded by CMS/US HHS.

data.title: School-Based Wellness Equipment funding opportunity (Solicitation 210-122)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services is accepting competitive applications for the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) School-Based Wellness Equipment funding opportunity. Eligible rural, tribal, public, and private schools in North Dakota may apply for funds to strengthen student physical, mental, and emotional well-being through new wellness equipment purchases. Approximately $500,000 in federal funds will support about 20 awards, estimated at $25,000 each. The funding aligns with Initiative 1: Make North Dakota Healthy Again and aims to create healthier learning environments, foster supportive spaces, and improve student academic success and engagement.

data.title: North Dakota Self-Serve Dispensing Kiosks in Pharmacies Funding Opportunity (Solicitation 210-441)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services, through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), is offering a competitive funding opportunity named 'Self-Serve Dispensing Kiosks in Pharmacies' (Solicitation 210-441). This grant, funded via Public Law 119-21 and administered with federal CMS approval, aims to improve access to medication dispensing, support medication adherence, and reduce transportation barriers for rural and tribal North Dakotans, with a particular emphasis on Medicaid members. Eligible projects will establish self-serve prescription pickup kiosks in rural and tribal community pharmacies or pharmacies located in rural critical access hospitals. Funds may support technical assistance, equipment, and remodeling. Priority is given to projects offering expanded-hours access (preferably 24/7), interoperability with prescription databases, and demonstrated enhancement of rural/tribal medication access in previously underserved areas. Awarded projects must secure North Dakota Board of Pharmacy written approval prior to fund release. Approximately $600,000 is available in total; additional awards may be made depending on applications and available funding. The operating period begins upon agreement execution and must conclude by September 30, 2027. Only one application per organization is allowed; funds must be expended by the period end date. Applications must include narrative responses and a completed Itemized Subrecipient Budget Template uploaded via Qualtrics. Monthly reporting and ongoing performance tracking per RHTP requirements are mandatory. Applications are due July 30, 2026, 5:00 p.m. CT.
applicantTypes: Pharmacies in rural critical access hospitals

applicantTypes: Other entities providing health services to/within rural counties

data.title: Interfacility Transport Project Request for Applications (Kansas RHTP 4.3.1)
data.issuingAgency: Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE)
data.summary: The Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) invites eligible organizations to apply for funding to support interfacility transports/transfers as part of the Kansas Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) 4.3.1. The Interfacility Transport grant project aims to improve health outcomes and transport times among rural Kansas facilities by supplementing current resources or creating dedicated rural interfacility transfer solutions. Eligible applicants must currently provide, or can provide as part of their application, rural interfacility transport/transfer services. The project explicitly excludes funding for services currently reimbursable by insurance and emphasizes collaboration with EMS, sustainable program design, and compliance with state and federal (including CMS) requirements. Awardees (expected 1–2 total for Year 1) must propose clear project goals, robust implementation and evaluation plans (including performance metrics and reporting), and a sustainability strategy for post-grant operations. Grant funds may be used for allowable costs only, with an indirect cost cap of 10%. Applications must be submitted via the KDHE online portal and include a proposed workplan, evaluation methodology, budget template, and required attachments. Applicants are required to comply with local EMS 'first right of refusal' for transports and must coordinate with KDHE throughout the award period.

data.title: Rural Clinical Fellowship for Advanced Practice Providers and Other Clinicians
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health – Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: RFP for rural clinical fellowship support for advanced practice providers and other clinicians through the Minnesota Rural Health Transformation Program. The program is funded by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) as part of a financial assistance award totaling $193,090,618.14, with 100 percent funded by CMS/HHS. Eligible applicants include accredited clinical training programs within accredited institutions of higher education in Minnesota, as well as various rural clinical practice settings. Training programs in Advanced Practice Registered Nursing, Certified Nurse Midwifery, Dental Therapy and Advanced Dental Therapy, a range of mental health professions, and Physician Assistant programs are eligible. Eligible practice settings include Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs), Community Mental Health Centers (CMHCs), Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), health systems, hospitals, long-term care facilities, other clinics, private practices, and tribal clinics located in rural Minnesota communities.

data.title: Michigan Rural Health Intensive Outpatient Program - 2027

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Healthcare Resiliency Program: Health Technology and Innovation (Long-Range) (RFA #34320-21427)

data.summary: Request for Application (RFA) #34320-21427: Rural Health Transformation Healthcare Resiliency Program: Health Technology and Innovation (Long-Range) supports health technology modernization and interoperability activities for rural health in Tennessee. The program targets technology innovation to strengthen healthcare delivery, expand access, improve efficiency, and promote health outcomes in rural and underserved parts of the state, as outlined in official Tennessee Department of Health procurement and RFA amendment documentation. Funding may support technology procurement, adoption, integration, interoperability, and pilot testing or evaluation of emerging health technologies—including but not limited to health information exchange integration, population health management, electronic records modernization, data analytics, cybersecurity, and workforce tools. data.title: RISE: 2.5 Recruit and Retain Rural Clinical Workforce RFGA
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services (Utah DHHS)
data.summary: The Utah Department of Health and Human Services, under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), is soliciting applications for the RISE Initiative 2.5: Recruit and Retain Rural Clinical Workforce RFGA. This opportunity makes available up to $20 million in total funding for eligible Utah-based entities to increase recruitment and retention of rural clinical providers. Grantees will implement structured financial incentives, ensure mandatory distribution of tribal rider funding for Indian Health Service, Tribal, and Urban Indian (I/T/U) organizations per designated Tier, and monitor fulfillment of 5-year service commitment requirements. data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS)
data.summary: The Maternal Health Provider Training – 2027 (MHPT-2027) grant supports the recruitment, retention, and training of maternal health providers serving rural Michigan communities, as part of Michigan's Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program Workforce for Wellness Initiative. Funded at $5,000,000 (per opportunity) through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), this opportunity seeks public agencies, 501(c)(3) nonprofits, local health departments, Michigan-based tribes or Indian Health Clinic programs, and universities to implement evidence-based workforce solutions that expand access to high-quality, integrated maternal health care across rural and partially rural counties. Applicants must submit a comprehensive project plan, budget, proof of eligibility, and other required documents through the EGrAMS portal by the deadline. The award period runs October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027. Pre-application technical assistance is available via a webinar on July 15, 2026.

data.title: Maine Healthcare Careers Exploration Program
data.issuingAgency: Maine Department of Education
data.summary: RHTP-funded Maine DOE opportunity to build sustainable career pipeline programming for grades 9-12, with up to four awards supporting healthcare career exploration, foundational skills, and connections to healthcare professionals and employers.
applicantTypes: Other organizations supporting grades 9-12 career exploration

data.title: Kansas Healthworks — Centralized Verification Organization (CVO) RFP
data.issuingAgency: HEALTHWORKS, KHA Foundation Inc. (Kansas Hospital Association) — administering RTSO/workforce projects under Kansas's RHTP plan
data.summary: HEALTHWORKS (KHA Foundation Inc.) seeks a Centralized Verification Organization to support Kansas's Centralized Credentialing Verification Pilot (CCV) under a hosted model — centralizing provider credentialing intake and primary source verification statewide while preserving payer credentialing authority and hospital privileging decisions. Funded by RHTP.
applicantTypes: 501(c)(3) and other qualified organizations with NCQA-equivalent status

data.title: Louisiana RHTP: Rural Collaborative Provider Models Program
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability
data.summary: Funds rural-provider-sharing/rotation models (specialty, behavioral health, dental, pharmacy, care coordination). Explicitly excludes clinician recruitment bonuses, capital improvements, telehealth infrastructure, EHR modernization, and value-based-care arrangements. 10% match required. Funding supports provider rotation programs, regional scheduling/referral systems, partnership development, operational redesign, and startup/implementation costs tied to collaborative care delivery. Applicants must demonstrate rural eligibility, documented access-related need, measurable outcomes, and a sustainability plan.
applicantTypes: Rural behavioral health or substance use provider
Independent rural practice (rural physician or physician group, pharmacy, dentist)

data.title: Rural Health Facility Renovation Independent Verification – RHTP
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
data.summary: Request for proposals to provide independent verification of rural health facility renovation projects under the Idaho Rural Health Transformation Plan and Program (RHTP) for FFY 2026. Scope includes site inspections, documentation of completed renovations, compliance assessment with RHTP standards, risk assessments, and detailed reporting to state oversight. RFP seeks entities with direct experience in facility project verification and compliance reporting.

data.title: Kentucky RHT Funding Opportunity to Develop Community Health Worker Specialized Certificates
data.issuingAgency: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services
data.summary: Kentucky is soliciting Kentucky-based training organizations to develop new specialized Community Health Worker (CHW) certificates in four priority areas: Healthy Lifestyle Management, Perinatal and Infant Health, Mental and Behavioral Health, and Dental/Oral Health. Maximum award is $200,000 per certificate, up to $800,000 total for all four, paid via milestone-based payments. Training will be delivered free through Kentucky's TRAIN platform. Applications due August 5, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET; anticipated funding period begins October 7, 2026. Part of Kentucky's Rural Health Transformation Plan, funded by CMS.

data.title: West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program Workforce Catalyst Employer Subsidy Program – Third-Party Administrator
data.issuingAgency: State of West Virginia
data.summary: The State of West Virginia’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), through the Health to Prosperity (HTP) Workforce Catalyst initiative, is seeking a qualified Third-Party Administrator (TPA) to serve as fiscal agent and program administrator for the Employer Subsidy Program. The TPA will establish and operate a structured, milestone-based employer incentive model to increase rural and high-need area workforce participation. Employers hiring individuals returning to work from State-approved Return-to-Work (RTW) programs may receive subsidies for Employer-Sponsored Insurance (ESI) premium offsets and other approved hiring costs. The TPA is responsible for eligibility verification, application processing, tracking milestone-based subsidy disbursement (hire, 90 days, 12 months), preventing supplanting/duplication of funds, and compliance with reporting, auditable documentation, and integration with the State’s data systems. All activities must support rigorous accountability, risk mitigation, sustainability planning, and measurable workforce outcomes, with oversight and decision-making retained by the State. This award is intended to supplement, not supplant, current employer funding and staffing, and cannot be used for matching other federal/state programs without prior written approval.
applicantTypes: Agency or Organization with Workforce/Grant Administration Experience

data.title: KR27-4 - Utah Health Information Network - Rural Health Transformation Program
data.issuingAgency: Utah Public Procurement Place (U3P)
data.summary: Utah’s Division of Purchasing and Department of Health and Human Services intend to award a $3,000,000 sole source contract to the Utah Health Information Network (UHIN) under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), specifically supporting LINCS Initiative 7.1 and 7A-7B. The contract scope includes conducting a comprehensive healthcare interoperability needs assessment of rural and frontier providers; diagnosing technical, workflow, and data quality gaps; managing non-competitive sub-grant funding; and delivering technical assistance and electronic health record (EHR) optimization training. Additional deliverables include onboarding rural providers to recognized health data exchange networks using HL7® FHIR® APIs and tracking point-of-care clinical metrics to improve rural care coordination. UHIN is Utah’s statutorily designated Health Information Exchange (HIE) and exclusive owner of the infrastructure and legal framework necessary to immediately execute this project’s requirements.

data.title: SPRINT Consortium RHTP Grant Application (2026)
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: This opportunity invites eligible lead entities to apply for up to $59.2 million in Year 1 federal funding as part of Utah's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) under the SPRINT Consortium. The grant supports rural health infrastructure, workforce development, technology modernization, and care innovation through a consortium model. Eligible applicants must demonstrate operational status, fiscal capacity, geographic diversity, and engage rural hospitals, clinics, FQHCs, and independent rural providers as stakeholders. Applications must propose activities aligning with strategic RHTP goals and comply with specific category limits. The agreement period runs from September 11, 2026, to September 30, 2031, and future funding is outcome-dependent. Only one lead entity is the primary recipient, with partners as subrecipients. The SPRINT Consortium aims to drive strategic advances in infrastructure, sustainable provider revenue, and network technology for rural Utah.

data.title: Rural Medicaid Alternative Payment Model Program (Initiative 3)
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability
data.summary: The Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), through the Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability, will provide up to $30M in Year 1 funding for rural providers to implement the target primary-care-led Medicaid value-based care (VBC) model in rural Louisiana. The program supports investment in infrastructure, care coordination, care delivery transformation, performance monitoring, and provider readiness for value-based payments with the long-term goal of progressing toward total cost of care (TCOC) accountability.
applicantTypes: Independent rural primary care providers or provider groups
Provider coalitions or collaboratives (ACOs, CINs, IPAs, hospital-led partnerships, FQHC/RHC networks)

data.title: Community Health Workers Grants: Strengthening the Rural Health Workforce in Wisconsin
data.issuingAgency: Wisconsin Department of Health Services
data.summary: Funding opportunity listed on Wisconsin DHS Current Grant Funding Opportunities.

data.title: Pennsylvania lines up FQHC & FQHC Look-Alikes - Modernizing Healthcare Technology and Enabling Interoperability opportunity
data.issuingAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services
data.summary: The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (DHS) offers up to six program payments of up to $300,000 each (total cap $1.8 million) for FQHCs and FQHC Look-Alikes to implement certified EHR systems and fully onboard to one of Pennsylvania's five certified Health Information Organizations (HIOs). This is a non-competitive program payment and will be made in the order that complete and eligible applications are received. Eligible use of funds includes purchasing and implementing a CEHRT system in accordance with federal requirements and fully onboarding to the Pennsylvania Patient and Provider Network (P3N HIE). All activities and expenditures must be completed by June 30, 2027, and recipients must return any unused funds by July 31, 2027. The program is open to Medicaid-enrolled FQHCs and look-alikes operating in Pennsylvania with at least one physical location, in full operation since at least December 29, 2025, and not at risk of closure. One payment per entity is permitted. Documentation requirements and monitoring/audit provisions apply; funds cannot supplant other federal/state awards.

data.title: Healthy Eating, Active Recreation, and Transformation (HEART)
data.issuingAgency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DF&A)
data.summary: Supports rural Arkansas prevention and wellness projects across six HEART sub-initiatives: GROW Kids, FARM, MOVE, FAITH, HEAL, and IMPACT. HEART focuses on coordinated, community-driven strategies targeting nutrition, physical activity, and chronic disease prevention, integrating schools, faith organizations, health providers, and community partners. The initiative aims to expand preventive care, promote healthy lifestyles, reduce chronic disease, improve behavioral health outcomes, strengthen workforce capacity, and support data-driven monitoring. The program encourages diverse applicants to propose measurable, scalable models that strengthen rural health systems and address underlying health disparities.

data.title: Mental Health Urgent Care- Rutland County
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Department of Mental Health
data.summary: The Vermont Department of Mental Health (DMH) is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to provide mental health urgent care services in Rutland County. This effort is funded under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) to build comprehensive, accessible, 24/7 crisis services that reduce emergency department usage for mental health crises, strengthen rural health networks, upgrade technology and shared operations, and enhance the rural health workforce. Successful bidders will establish an alternative care setting for all ages and implement innovative, sustainable approaches to urgent care delivery.
applicantTypes: Other legal entities eligible to contract with the State of Vermont

data.title: Minnesota RHTP: Technical Assistance for Rural Health Care Entities in Support of Community & Clinical Linkages
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health (MDH)
data.summary: SWIFT Event ID 2000018473. Provides up to $4,000,000 in technical assistance to rural health care entities in support of community and clinical linkages, funded under Minnesota's RHTP award. The Minnesota Department of Health seeks qualified vendors to provide statewide technical assistance to up to 125 rural health care organizations, including hospitals, clinics, Tribal Nations, FQHCs, and CCBHCs/CMHCs. Technical assistance may include consulting, training, strategic planning, and tools to support implementation of RHTP activities focused on chronic disease management, preventive care, expanding access to community-based services (including mobile units), and integrating frontline workforce models. Example activities include supporting evidence-based models for frontline workers (e.g., community paramedics, health workers, doulas) and local care delivery with mobile units. Tasks include developing and implementing TA plans, supporting culturally relevant guidelines, providing bimonthly (every other month) summaries to MDH of TA requests and solutions, annual progress reporting, collaborating with other TA vendors and MDH, developing scalable tools and resources, and participating in regular meetings with MDH. TA must be available virtually and in-person, at minimum once monthly per organization.

data.title: Alabama RHTP Simulation Training Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: Supports the development, expansion, and implementation of specialty-based simulation workforce training programs designed to improve healthcare provider skills and readiness in rural Alabama. The initiative funds structured programs incorporating simulation equipment, instructional materials, and coordinated training activities, enabling trainees to experience critical, high-risk, and rare medical scenarios in a safe environment. Funding may be used for curriculum development, training delivery, simulation equipment and materials, and program coordination to ensure that rural healthcare providers and trainees have access to effective, practical training environments aligned with rural healthcare needs. The goal is to strengthen provider capacity, improve access to high-quality hands-on training, and enhance care quality and preparedness in rural Alabama healthcare facilities. Projects must align with the Simulation Training Initiative’s scope and clearly demonstrate how the project advances specialty-based simulation training capacity, provider readiness, and healthcare delivery improvement in rural communities.

data.title: Alabama RHTP Maternal and Fetal Health Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: Supports practical, scalable strategies that strengthen maternal healthcare delivery systems across rural Alabama through the establishment and enhancement of regional maternal and fetal referral hubs, expansion of telerobotic ultrasound capacity, and facility readiness upgrades to improve access and outcomes for expectant mothers and infants.

data.title: Alabama RHTP Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Treat-in-Place Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: Supports the implementation of EMS treat-in-place pilot programs, including protocol development, telehealth consulting equipment, software, training, and related needs to reduce unnecessary transport and emergency department burden in rural Alabama. Projects must align with the ARHTP EMS Treat-in-Place strategy and directly benefit rural communities.

data.title: Alabama RHTP Statewide Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Trauma and Stroke Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: Funds practical, scalable strategies to expand and improve statewide EMS trauma and stroke response systems in Alabama. This initiative supports the initiation or expansion of hospital-referral services, protocol implementation, EMS/hospital care coordination, training, system development, and operational support with a mandatory focus on direct benefit to rural Alabama communities. Projects must align with the designated strategy: Initiation/Expansion and Operation—enhancing EMS system capacity, expanding trauma and stroke response capabilities, broadening statewide hospital-referral service reach, and improving care coordination and patient outcomes. Awardees must serve rural Alabama, propose projects feasible within the eligible implementation period, and clearly show advancement of ARHTP initiative goals.

data.title: Alabama RHTP Cancer Digital Regionalization Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: Funds support the Alabama Rural Health Transformation Program (ARHTP) Cancer Digital Regionalization Initiative, focused on expanding access to cancer screening and early detection in rural Alabama. The program advances objectives of the CMS Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program and emphasizes four strategy areas: (1) expanding proven cancer detection capabilities in rural healthcare settings; (2) establishing and operating regional hubs for cancer screening to coordinate services and referrals; (3) deploying mobile cancer screening units in underserved rural areas; and (4) community activation, outreach, and education to boost awareness and participation in screening. Eligible projects must clearly show benefits to rural Alabama through improved access, stronger regional service coordination, and the creation of community partnerships aimed at better health outcomes. Funding is limited to direct project costs, including technology, equipment, mobile unit operations, outreach, and education; administrative or indirect costs are not allowed. Projects are competitively selected as subawards and are subject to federal, state, and program requirements under ADECA’s CMS cooperative agreement, with quarterly and final reporting, procurement controls, and compliance monitoring required.

data.title: LINCS 7.3–7.4: Semantic Data Model
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services (Utah DHHS)
data.summary: Forecasted Utah RHTP grant opportunity to support development and implementation of a statewide, cloud-based, semantically interoperable data platform harmonizing EHRs, claims, and public health data for Utah rural providers. Up to $11,000,000 available in Year 1 (up to $65,000,000 over 5 years); one anticipated award. Estimated open date July 10, 2026; no Letter of Intent required. Project start: September 1, 2026. Only Utah-based 501(c)(3) health organizations are eligible. Applicants must partner with rural Utah health facilities and demonstrate experience in managing state/federal awards for rural partners.

data.title: SPRINT Consortium (Sustainable Provider Revenue, Infrastructure, and Network Technology)
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
data.summary: Forecasted multi-initiative Utah RHTP grant opportunity. Up to $59,200,000 available in Year 1 (up to $291,800,000 over 5 years), broken down by component, to support sustainable provider revenue, infrastructure, and network technology initiatives for rural Utah health care providers. Estimated open date July 10, 2026. A Letter of Intent is due July 27, 2026, 5:00 PM MT, ahead of the full RFGA release.

data.title: AHCCCS Opioid Antagonist Distribution Initiative RFGA
data.issuingAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)
data.summary: The Opioid Antagonist Distribution Initiative is supported by the Arizona Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), funded via the federal One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1, Title VII, Sec. 71401). The initiative provides competitive funding for the distribution of opioid antagonists (including naloxone/Narcan), training of first responders and healthcare professionals, and support for opioid overdose prevention in rural Arizona, especially targeting rural counties, Tribal communities, and small fire districts. The program may also focus on rural health innovation and partnerships, and must operate within the indirect cost cap requirements mandated under RHTP. Applications must include clear activities for overdose prevention and an implementation/distribution plan, with cost share/match not required unless otherwise specified.

data.title: Opioid Antagonist Distribution Initiative (AZRHTP)
data.issuingAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)
data.summary: AHCCCS's first public RHTP grant solicitation: expands access to opioid antagonists (e.g. naloxone) and strengthens overdose response capacity across rural and Tribal communities in Arizona. Funds procurement/distribution of opioid antagonist kits, overdose recognition and response training, and coordinated regional overdose response systems, across three funding tiers (community, regional, multi-county system-level).

data.title: HTP Health-to-Work Programs
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health, Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: This funding opportunity supports the design, implementation, and operation of field-based Return-to-Work (RTW) programs that advance the Health to Prosperity (HTP) initiative under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) in West Virginia. The initiative seeks to restore workforce participation by improving the health and employment outcomes of adults with non-behavioral chronic physical health conditions (e.g., diabetes, cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, musculoskeletal conditions, and other high-prevalence chronic disorders) whose health presents a barrier to ongoing employment. Funded programs must deliver proactive RTW coordination through dedicated liaisons, employer engagement, individualized work-health transition planning, job placement support, data integration with the State’s RHTP data spine, and ongoing workforce retention activities, while strictly not duplicating clinical services billable to other payers. Direct clinical service delivery is excluded. RTW projects will be performance-based, with funds tied to achieving and documenting milestones including operational readiness (within 60 days of award), participant intake and engagement, employer partnership, job placement, 6-month employment retention, and program scalability. Applicants must show proven experience in employer partnership, prior RTW coordination, payer duplication avoidance, sustainable scaling, and provide a clear sustainability plan for long-term support beyond the grant period. Only non-employer organizational entities with demonstrated employer engagement and service delivery capacity may apply; employers must be implementation partners, not grantees or direct recipients. Programs targeting primary behavioral health (SUD or mental health disorders) as the employment barrier are funded by separate mechanisms and are not eligible under this AFA.

data.title: North Dakota RHTP Parents Lead: Assessment and Train-the-Trainer Curriculum Development (210-133)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
data.summary: North Dakota HHS seeks a vendor/organization to conduct a statewide behavioral-health-promotion needs assessment and develop a new Train-the-Trainer curriculum for the state's existing 'Parents Lead' program, under RHTP Initiative 1 (Make North Dakota Healthy Again). Approximately $500,000 available, one award expected, funding period through September 30, 2027. The initiative aims to engage parents, caregivers, professionals, and community organizations addressing youth behavioral health concerns using evidence-informed strategies. Annual renewals may be possible depending on progress and funding availability.
applicantTypes: Other organizations serving rural or tribal North Dakota residents

data.title: Smart Care Catalyst – Implementation Support to Strengthen Value-Based Care (VBC) Participation (RHT-AFA-07-27-2026-SCC1)
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health
data.summary: The State of West Virginia is releasing up to $1,500,000 under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) for Smart Care Catalyst implementation support to help rural providers in southern counties build readiness for substance use disorder (SUD)-focused value-based care (VBC) models. This opportunity will fund provider onboarding, technical assistance, workflow redesign, and data integration — targeting practical enablement of providers and payers for VBC participation. Milestone-based subawards will prioritize measurable outcomes, rapid implementation, and regional engagement, including stakeholder assessment, defining provider training needs, and reducing barriers to SUD-focused VBC participation. All implementation support must supplement, not supplant, existing activities and comply with federal and state reporting and data privacy regulations. Activities must be focused in rural and underserved southern West Virginia counties with a strong requirement for integration of data into the State’s RHTP data architecture. Funds will be awarded to one or more qualified grantees able to demonstrate experience in provider enablement, VBC implementation, technical assistance, and healthcare analytics. Continuation of funding beyond the one-year term is contingent on State and CMS decisions, performance, and compliance.

data.title: Maryland RHTP: RISE (Recruiting, Inspiring, Supporting, and Educating) — Pipeline Training Programs and Advance Provider Pathways
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Labor — Division of Workforce Development & Adult Learning
data.summary: Bundled RFP funding Pipeline Training Programs and Advance Provider Pathways — building healthcare workforce pipelines and expanding provider training capacity in rural Maryland. The program is 100% funded by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services as part of a financial assistance award to bolster and retain healthcare professionals who intend to build careers, lives and families in rural Maryland.

data.title: Maryland RHTP: Apprenticeship Intermediaries and RAMP Expansion for Allied Health Employers
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Labor
data.summary: Bundled RFP funding two Pathways to Health Careers workforce initiatives: Apprenticeship Intermediaries (building employer apprenticeship pipelines) and RAMP (Rural Allied health Mentorship Pipeline) Expansion for Allied Health Employers. Part of Maryland's RHTP Pillar 1 workforce strategy. Total available funding for this round is up to $7,500,000, with awards ranging from $250,000 to $500,000 per project. The program is supported by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services as part of a financial assistance award, 100 percent CMS/HHS funded.

data.title: North Dakota RHTP Rural Ambulance Modernization (Solicitation 210-342)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS) – Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS) is offering a competitive grant opportunity under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) to modernize licensed rural ambulance services and improve the delivery of emergency medical care through equipment modernization, telehealth, and electronic medical record (EMR) integration. Approximately $22,000,000 in total federal funds are available for this year (Year 1), with an estimated 110 awards of approximately $200,000 each, supporting projects such as ambulance retrofits, telemedicine-enabled equipment, LTE routers, SIRN radios, and related upgrades to EMS communications and interoperability. Eligible projects are prioritized if they focus on new equipment not currently utilized by the applicant. All awarded funds must be expended by August 31, 2027. Eligible applicants include ND-located licensed ground ambulance districts and providers (including non-federal tribal services) serving rural or rural tribal residents outside urban centers (Bismarck, Fargo, Grand Forks, West Fargo unless at least 50% rural focus). Applications are due through Qualtrics by August 9, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CT. Only one application is allowed per organization.

data.title: Michigan Rural Health Best Practices - 2026
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary: The grantee will serve as the subrecipient to establish a baseline that can be used to establish targets and demonstrate CHW-related outcomes. The funds will support coordinated outreach, data collection, analysis, and reporting necessary to produce a reliable workforce inventory and needs assessment, ensuring efficient use of resources while avoiding duplication of existing efforts.

data.title: West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program Start-Up Funding for SUD Evidence-Based Practices (2026)
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health – Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: The West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), administered by the West Virginia Department of Health under the Smart Care Catalyst initiative, is soliciting applications for Year 1 start-up funds and provider incentives to implement or expand evidence-based practices in substance use disorder (SUD) prevention, treatment, and/or recovery. The program seeks to fund provider organizations, behavioral health and SUD treatment providers, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), hospitals, community-based organizations, and cross-sector partnerships with capacity to deliver SUD-focused interventions that align with future value-based care (VBC) models. Funded activities must represent net new or expanded efforts beyond existing reimbursable services and demonstrate measurable, near-term improvements in SUD health outcomes, access to care, care coordination, and readiness for VBC. Required strategies prioritize upstream, root-cause-focused solutions over episodic, downstream care and include explicit integration with the State’s RHTP data spine, use of non-duplicative and non-billable activities, robust operational and outcome metrics tracking, and ongoing participation in State-led VBC design workgroups. Funds are awarded and released in milestone-based tranches: (1) program design/operational readiness, (2) initial implementation/service delivery, and (3) achievement of performance thresholds and sustainability. The goal is to expand rural/underserved service capacity, reduce avoidable emergency/crisis-related system utilization, improve population-level SUD metrics, facilitate workforce reintegration, and strengthen long-term system transformation consistent with State MAHA principles and the Governor’s Four Pillars. All grantee data, reports, and workflows become State assets for analytics, oversight, and continuity. This one-year funding opportunity, totaling $6,000,000, ends July 31, 2027; continued funding is contingent on State/CMS appropriations and demonstrated grantee outcomes, as defined by RHTP and CMS/HHS requirements.

data.title: SCC2 VBC Design & Administer
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: This opportunity supports the Smart Care Catalyst initiative under the West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), funded via CMS/HHS as part of an approximately $200 million federal grant. The SCC2 VBC Design & Administer grant, RHT-AFA-07-27-2026-SCC2, solicits applications from qualified entities to design and administer standardized, multi-payer value-based payment models targeting substance use disorder (SUD) in rural West Virginia, beginning with initial implementation in the southern counties and structured for statewide scaling. The awarded entity will: (1) define standardized, multi-payer VBC model structures and deliver implementation-ready model packages; (2) establish performance measurement and data-sharing frameworks (with integration to the State RHTP data spine and WVHIN); and (3) convene, align, and develop governance with Medicaid MCOs, other payers, and providers. Funding will be tied to milestone and deliverables approved by the State—focused on health outcomes, reduced avoidable utilization, and improved workforce participation. All work products must be accessible to the State as assets; data reporting must conform to CMS and RHTP requirements; and non-performance will trigger reallocation of funds. Awards are milestone-based and for Year 1 only (through July 31, 2027); future funding is contingent on State receipt of federal continuation funds and satisfactory grantee performance.
applicantTypes: Other organizations with payment model design/administration expertise

data.title: Michigan Diabetes and Hypertension Management and Education - 2027
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS), Policy, Planning, and Access Administration
data.summary: The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) announces the 2027 Diabetes and Hypertension Management and Education (DHME) grant opportunity. The DHME program, part of the Rural Health Transformation Program’s Chronic Disease Collaborative Care Fund, supports collaborative, community-based projects to improve diabetes and hypertension management and education in eligible rural and partially rural Michigan communities. The program funds evidence-based interventions to enhance care coordination, build sustainable rural health partnerships, strengthen the chronic disease workforce, promote data and information sharing, and increase access to chronic disease prevention and management services. Awardees must demonstrate organizational capacity, partnerships among local health providers, and a clear plan for addressing health disparities in diabetes and hypertension outcomes. MDHHS will provide up to $500,000 for selected projects with an implementation period from October 1, 2026, to September 30, 2027.

data.title: North Dakota RHTP Childcare for the Rural Health Workforce (210-223)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS)
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS), as part of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Initiative 2: Strengthen and Stabilize the Rural Health Workforce, solicits applications from rurally located hospitals—including critical access hospitals, rural emergency hospitals, and general acute hospitals, as well as non-federally operated Indian Health Service hospitals and tribally run 638 facilities—for planning grants to develop sustainable childcare solutions geared at recruiting and retaining the rural health workforce. Projects funded will conduct a workforce and community childcare needs assessment, evaluate models for embedding or expanding childcare services within or through hospital partnerships, carry out financial and facility planning, craft operational and nutrition policies compliant with state childcare licensing regulations, and develop actionable, sustainable implementation plans. Applicants must ensure their proposal addresses a novel, non-duplicative strategy and must involve local partners such as licensed childcare providers or economic development organizations as appropriate. The planning process must include required assessments, detailed facility and staffing plans, a meal/nutrition plan, a timeline, and sustainability projections. Approximately $3,000,000 in federal funds is available, with an estimated 38 grants around $78,000 each to be awarded. No more than one application per eligible organization is permitted, and all planning activities must be completed and funds expended by September 30, 2027. Completion of these activities is required to qualify for a subsequent implementation opportunity anticipated in early 2027. Projects must serve rural areas outside the urban centers of Grand Forks, Fargo, West Fargo, and Bismarck.
applicantTypes: Non-federally Operated Indian Health Service Hospital

data.title: Expanding School Health Centers to Rural Areas Funding Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (NCDHHS) Division of Child and Family Well-Being
data.summary: This funding opportunity, part of the NC Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), provides up to $1,250,000 in federal funding to expand School-Based Health Centers (SBHCs) in rural North Carolina. The goal is to increase access to integrated physical and behavioral health care for youth in HRSA-defined rural census tracts with limited health care access. Eligible applicants are entities currently under contract or with a grant agreement with the Division of Child and Family Well-Being operating a School Health Center Program and who have been expressly notified to apply. The RHTP was established under H.R. 1 to support innovation, infrastructure, partnerships, and workforce development in rural health care delivery.
applicantTypes: Current NCDHHS School Health Center Program grantees/contractors

data.title: Michigan Improving Care and Access Through Transportation - 2027
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary:
The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) has issued a grant funding opportunity (GFO) for the Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program that will 
support the Care Closer to Home Blueprint: Improving Care Delivery and Access through Transportation Grant Program.
Michigan’s RHT Program focuses on building a strong and innovative rural health system that ensures every resident has access to high-quality care close to home. The program advances this goal through coordinated, community-driven strategies implemented across four core initiatives:
Strengthening partnerships that support rural health transformation.
Expanding and stabilizing the workforce needed to sustain community wellness.
Advancing interoperability so providers can share information and coordinate care effectively.
Developing models that bring essential services closer to where people live. 
The Improving Care and Access through Transportation Program will help rural residents get the care they need by improving transportation options and bringing services closer to where people live and work. Funding will support technical assistance and commu

data.title: CCG1 Outpatient RPM
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health - Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP)
data.summary: This Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA), under the West Virginia Department of Health Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) – Connected Care Grid (CCG1), invites qualified healthcare providers and digital health partners to apply for competitive Year 1 milestone-based grants (totaling up to $9,070,862) to launch evidence-based Outpatient Remote Patient Monitoring (OP RPM) programs. Funded projects must deploy FDA-cleared connected devices (e.g., blood pressure cuffs, glucose monitors), implement integrated clinical care-coordination models, and prioritize high-need rural West Virginians living with diabetes and/or hypertension in alignment with Governor Morrisey's Four Pillars of a Healthy West Virginia and MAHA principles. Projects must achieve rapid operational launch within 60 days, embed nutritional tracking and root-cause-focused behavioral supports (e.g., food-as-medicine, produce prescriptions), and aim to reduce long-term healthcare dependency and promote workforce participation. Integration with the State-led RHTP data spine or interim data transfer methods is required, adhering to HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 standards. Programs must demonstrate quantifiable clinical improvements (such as HbA1c reduction and blood pressure stabilization), support monthly and quarterly reporting using State and CMS templates, and comply with robust data-sharing requirements—granting the State real-time access to all generated programmatic assets. Funding advances will be provided for start-up, with further disbursements strictly tied to validated achievement of key programmatic milestones. Grantees must collaborate with other RHTP initiatives (e.g., Rural Health Link, Mountain State Care Force), support job creation or economic expansion in West Virginia (preferred), and expend all funds and submit invoices by July 31, 2027. Applications must be submitted through the WVOASIS VSS Portal and include a Detailed Line-Item Budget (DLIB) Worksheet and budget narrative. Preference is given to applicants manufacturing, commercializing, or expanding operations in West Virginia. Cost share/match is welcomed, not required. Award decisions will be based on stringent review criteria, including capacity, impact, plan feasibility, sustainability, and budget, with a minimum score of 80% required for funding consideration.

data.title: Delta States Rural Development Network Program (HRSA-26-045)
data.issuingAgency: Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Federal Office of Rural Health Policy (FORHP)
data.summary: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) announces the availability of funds for the Delta States Rural Development Network Program (Delta Program). The purpose of this program is to support established networks in the eight Delta Region states (Alabama, Arkansas, Illinois, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, and Tennessee) to address unmet local health care needs and improve health outcomes through collaborative activities. Funded networks are expected to implement evidence-based or innovative approaches to improve access, coordination, and the quality of essential health care services in rural communities. Applicants must demonstrate organizational capacity to serve rural Delta areas and propose projects that align with HRSA priorities, including addressing health care disparities, strengthening the rural health workforce, and enhancing health system capacity.

data.title: CCG Inpatient RPM
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health - Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: The State of West Virginia has released an Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA) for Year 1 grants under its Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), specifically for the Connected Care Grid (CCG) Inpatient Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) initiative. Up to $4,915,066 is available in total for 3–4 grantees to implement inpatient-anchored RPM models leveraging connected monitoring technologies and virtual clinical workflows. These models aim to improve care delivery for high-risk and rural populations, reduce hospital length of stay, accelerate care transitions, reduce unnecessary readmissions and emergency department utilization, and generate actionable data to inform statewide performance monitoring. Grants are performance-based, reimbursed by milestones: start-up, 50% bed deployment, and full bed deployment with health outcome improvement. All core capabilities must be live, integrated, and actively used by the end of Year 1—this is not a planning or pilot effort. Activities executed under this AFA must not duplicate or supplant existing value-based or mandated programs, nor replace current funding or staffing. Required operational metrics include device deployment and utilization, patient adherence, provider satisfaction, and reductions in length of stay and ED visits. Eligible applicants include acute care hospitals, critical access hospitals, hospital-based behavioral health facilities, skilled nursing operators, or other entities approved by the State. Funding must be expended and invoiced by July 31, 2027. Proposed activities must demonstrate supplemental enhancement consistent with RHTP goals, CMS requirements, and the State's evaluation framework. Applicants must submit monthly and quarterly quantitative and qualitative reports. CMS and State reporting, governance participation, and real-time State access to all generated data are required.
applicantTypes: Other entities approved by the State

data.title: Louisiana RHTP: Regional Care Conveners and Navigation Networks Program
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability
data.summary: The Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), through the Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability, is offering funding under the Regional Care Conveners and Navigation Networks Program to develop regional care conveners and networks coordinating physical, behavioral, and social service providers (including community and school-based navigators) for rural populations. Funding prioritizes evidence-based convener models with measurable outcomes that align with RHTP strategies and long-term sustainability. Core functions to be supported include network orchestration, data integration and reporting, population engagement, and program oversight and accountability. Awards will be made in the form of a Cooperative Endeavor Agreement (CEA), with a mandatory 10% cost share/match contribution. Eligible applicants must be LDH-defined rural organizations able to document financial, infrastructure, or access-related need, and must submit a sustainability plan as part of their proposal. Award size ranges from $500,000 to $2,000,000 annually. Indirect costs are capped at 1.5% of direct costs. Reimbursement is made for eligible expenses incurred; construction/renovation costs may not be grant-funded but may count toward match. Applications will be reviewed and scored against criteria including documented need, projected impact, feasibility, sustainability, and cost effectiveness.

data.title: Food is Medicine (FIM) Programs NOFO
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), Office of Rural Health Transformation and Sustainability
data.summary: LDH Food is Medicine (FIM) program funds rural projects integrating nutrition into healthcare — partnerships between healthcare providers and community organizations connecting rural residents to healthy foods via clinician referral, plus nutrition education for chronic disease prevention/management. Year 1 Food FARMacy program funding: $2,700,000. Award size per project: $10,000–$500,000, reimbursement-based with a mandatory 10% in-kind match.

data.title: DHHS26117 - Mobile MRI and CT Services
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: Utah DHHS is seeking one qualified vendor for a five-year contract to provide self-contained mobile MRI and CT diagnostic imaging services at the Utah State Correctional Facility. The solicitation requires mobile MRI units with at least 1.5 Tesla capability, mobile CT units with at least 64-slice technology, Utah-licensed ARRT-certified technologists, onboard medical-grade HVAC, and board-certified radiology interpretation with final reports within 24 to 48 hours and STAT preliminary results within 4 hours. Proposals must be submitted through Bonfire, with technical and cost proposals separated as directed in the RFP.

data.title: North Dakota Clinics without Walls: Remote Patient Monitoring Funding Opportunity (Solicitation 210-334)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services, through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), announces competitive funding under Clinics without Walls: Remote Patient Monitoring (Solicitation 210-334). Approximately $1.6 million in federal funds will be awarded to eligible rural healthcare providers—including rural hospitals, critical access hospitals and their partner clinics, federally qualified health centers, rural clinics, rural PPS systems, and eligible tribal organizations—to implement and expand remote patient monitoring (RPM) technology. Projects must serve rural North Dakota residents, with priority for new RPM equipment and Medicaid-focused initiatives. Fundable activities include purchasing and implementing new RPM devices/applications, integrating monitoring and telehealth with electronic health records, technical/training support, and patient coaching. Awards average $80,000, with an operating period through August 31, 2027. Applications are due August 14, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. CT via Qualtrics. Only one application per organization is permitted.

data.title: North Dakota RHTP Clinics without Walls: Telehealth Infrastructure (Solicitation 210-331)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS) — Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: This is a competitive funding opportunity through North Dakota Health and Human Services' Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), supporting the expansion of telehealth infrastructure in rural and tribal communities lacking local healthcare providers. The goal is to create and enhance telehealth access points—such as telehealth pods in community facilities, mobile telehealth units, and technology upgrades—that enable rural Medicaid members and other underserved residents to access preventive services, behavioral health, specialty care, and chronic disease management. Approximately $3.6 million is available in this cycle, with an estimated 25 individual awards averaging $144,000 each. Funded projects are expected to strengthen rural care delivery capacity, increase access, and improve measured health outcomes. The operating period concludes August 31, 2027, and all awarded funds and equipment must be expended and received by that date.
applicantTypes: Tribes and tribal organizations (excluding federally operated IHS)

data.title: CalRHT Family Medicine Obstetrics (FM-OB) Fellowship Subaward Program RFA
data.issuingAgency: California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) — CalRHT (California Rural Health Transformation Program)
data.summary: HCAI's California Rural Health Transformation Program (CalRHT) invites applications from aspiring or existing graduate medical education (GME) sponsoring institutions to establish or expand Family Medicine Obstetrics (FM-OB) fellowship capacity in rural California. The purpose is to build and sustain a skilled rural maternal health workforce by funding fellowship programs that equip family physicians with advanced obstetric competencies and prepare them to serve rural and underserved communities, addressing critical workforce shortages and improving maternal and infant outcomes. As fellows complete their training, the program encourages placement in rural collaboratives, including CalRHT primary and maternity care regional collaboratives. Supported under CalRHT Initiative 1: Transformative Care Model — Expand and Support Rural Workforce Capacity, the program provides up to $6.5 million in Budget Period 1, with estimated awards ranging from $150,000 to $500,000 per fellowship program per year for eligible programmatic and infrastructure expenses.

data.title: CalRHT Accelerator Partners RFA (Initiative One: Transformative Care Model)
data.issuingAgency: California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI)
data.summary: California's Rural Health Transformation Program (CalRHT), funded by a $233,639,308.46 CMS federal award for FFY 2026, has released its first Request for Applications: Accelerator Partners, under Initiative One (Transformative Care Model). HCAI (California Department of Health Care Access and Information) is making up to $39,000,000 available for Budget Period 1, with an expected 5–25 partners to receive funding. Applicants are required to apply as a partnership or consortium, with the submission demonstrating partner organizations, estimated funding allocation for each partner, and signed partnership documentation, along with a mandatory Excel budget workbook. All applications and required attachments must be submitted via the official Submittable portal before August 14, 2026, at 3:00 PM PT. Late or incomplete applications will not be considered for Budget Period 1 but may be eligible for a future Budget Period 2.

data.title: SHIFT: 3.2 Rural Health Provider Networks RFGA
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: This opportunity offers up to $2.5 million in federal funding for Utah-based multi-facility rural health provider networks to expand services, strengthen operational and clinical integration, improve emergency medical services, and promote financial sustainability. Applications are sought from partnerships including at least three different rural facility types, such as CAH, REH, RHC, I/T/U, or FQHC facilities. Up to six awards may be made for Budget Period 1 (September 21, 2026, to September 30, 2031). Bonus scoring is available for projects strengthening tribal health infrastructure. Key deliverables and expectations include tracking implementation metrics, continuous progress reporting, and developing a sustainability plan for the rural health network beyond the grant period.

data.title: SHIFT 3.2: Rural Health Provider Networks
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: Utah Rural Health Transformation Program grant to establish or expand integrated rural health provider networks (e.g. rural health clinics, pediatric trauma, or maternal health networks). Awardees build a comprehensive resource directory of physical and behavioral healthcare services across rural Utah. Funding type: grant agreement. Up to $2,500,000 available for Year 1 (approximately 6 awards anticipated; individual Year 1 awards range $250,000-$1,250,000 depending on project scale and network complexity); up to $18,500,000 over a 5-year period for the full agreement, contingent on availability of funds. Eligible applicants: Utah-based strategic partners with extensive expertise in rural health systems, existing relationships with rural hospitals, clinics, and healthcare organizations, and demonstrated technical capacity to develop a comprehensive resource directory tailored to rural Utah.
applicantTypes: Utah-based strategic partners / rural health systems organizations

data.title: Arizona RHTP: Telehealth Digital Transformation, Adoption, & Care Coordination Grant
data.issuingAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)
data.summary: This RFGA is the third public solicitation of several competitive grants released by AHCCCS under the Arizona Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), within the Making Rural Healthcare Accessible Initiative, funded by the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program. It supports projects establishing or expanding telehealth hubs, mobile health units, and remote monitoring in underserved rural and rural Tribal Arizona communities. Eligible activities include digital infrastructure modernization, acquisition of telehealth equipment, care coordination platform integration, and tele-behavioral health/chronic care service integration. These investments are designed to strengthen access by reducing travel for advanced services and integrating advanced technologies in care settings. Funding is offered in 4 tiers ($10,000–$75,000, $75,001–$500,000, $500,001–$2,000,000, $2,000,001–$5,000,000) based on project scope and organizational type. Up to $17,000,000 is available per budget year in Budget Period 1 (Dec 29, 2025–Oct 30, 2026); continuation for Years 2–5 depends on annual CMS non-competing continuation approval.

data.title: Pennsylvania RHTP Modernizing Healthcare Technology and Enabling Interoperability — EHR/HIO Program Payments
