data.issuingAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services
data.summary: The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (DHS) offers program payments, capped at no more than $25,000,000 total (with possible increase at DHS discretion), to qualified entities—including hospitals, long-term care nursing facilities, home health care agencies, behavioral health providers, ID/A adult homes, and ID/A intermediate care facilities—to implement Certified EHR Technology (CEHRT) and/or onboard to one of Pennsylvania’s five certified Health Information Organizations (HIOs) within the P3N network. Payments are authorized in the order complete and eligible certifications are received; this is a non-competitive, initial round program payment request under the RHTP Technology and Infrastructure initiative. Per-entity payment caps are set by provider type, site, and activity: $20,000 (HIO onboarding only, most types), $70,000 (HIO onboarding only, hospitals), $100,000 (CEHRT update + HIO onboarding), and $150,000 (CEHRT implementation + HIO onboarding). All approved funds must be expended by June 30, 2027. Unused funds must be returned to DHS by July 31, 2027. This is the general opportunity for all qualified rural entities; a separate track covers FQHCs and FQHC Look-Alikes (up to $300,000 each, $1.8M pool). Additional requirements include specific licensure/certification, proof of rural Pennsylvania location, and, for EHR/HIO tiers, submission of vendor quotes and budget documentation.

data.title: RHTP Statewide eConsult Platform
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The Tennessee Department of Health is soliciting proposals for statewide asynchronous provider-to-provider electronic consultation (eConsult) services. This RFP (RFP # 34320-19927) seeks suppliers capable of providing an integrated, secure platform that enables healthcare providers across Tennessee to engage in asynchronous consultations. The procurement is coordinated by the Department of Health and the State Central Procurement Office. Access to detailed RFP materials is restricted; interested suppliers must execute a state-mandated nondisclosure agreement before the full solicitation documentation can be disclosed. The project is part of Tennessee’s broader Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) initiative to improve healthcare access, outcomes, and technology infrastructure in rural and underserved areas. Proposers must comply with strict data security and confidentiality safeguards and all standard state procurement requirements.

data.title: MT DPHHS Equipment Grant Application (Rural EMS)
data.issuingAgency: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS)
data.summary: Grants to strengthen emergency medical services (EMS) in rural Montana by funding equipment acquisition for eligible EMS agencies. Total first-year grant funding available is $4 million through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP).

data.title: RHTP Mobile App for Pregnancy and Post-Partum Health
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the Tennessee Department of Health for the design, development, and implementation of a mobile application supporting pregnancy and post-partum health in Tennessee's rural and underserved communities. The initiative seeks to enhance healthcare access and delivery for these populations through innovative technology solutions. It is part of the Department's professional service procurements and is listed in the 2026 RFP opportunities, emphasizing competitive selection processes for targeted healthcare improvements.

data.title: Arizona RHTP: Medical Diagnostic Equipment and Technology, including EHR Upgrades & Data Sharing Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)
data.summary: AHCCCS Request for Grant Application under the Arizona Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP): Medical Diagnostic Equipment and Technology, including EHR Upgrades & Data Sharing Initiative. Part of AHCCCS's active RHTP RFGA slate alongside the Opioid Antagonist Distribution Initiative and the Telehealth Digital Transformation, Adoption, and Care Coordination Grant. Total funding $30,100,000.32.

data.title: Development of a Needs and Readiness Assessment and Vendor RFP to Modernize Ten Community Mental Health Centers Via Selection and Adoption of a Common Electronic Health Record (EHR) Platform
data.issuingAgency: New Hampshire Community Behavioral Health Association (NHCBHA), on behalf of the Governor’s Office of New Opportunities & Rural Transformational Health (GO-NORTH)
data.summary: GO-NORTH Initiative 4 (Technology): NHCBHA, funded through the Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Federal program, seeks a vendor to conduct an IT needs and readiness assessment and develop a vendor RFP to modernize ten New Hampshire Community Mental Health Centers via a common Electronic Health Record (EHR) platform. This assessment will drive standardization, interoperability, and sustainability in behavioral health IT infrastructure statewide. The initiative aims to position all ten CMHCs for future Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) certification, improved clinical and financial operations, centralized service delivery, and compliance with Medicaid-heavy payer requirements. The selected vendor will assess current infrastructure, workflows, revenue cycle management, and readiness for digital transformation, ultimately supporting the selection and contracting of an EHR vendor. The work emphasizes long-term sustainability, security, and efficiency while supporting the diverse functional needs of all CMHCs.

data.title: Workforce Retention and Sustainable Ecosystem Development Initiative (WEI/RHTP)
data.issuingAgency: AccelerateMS
data.summary: Funds projects supporting recruitment and retention of healthcare professionals in rural Mississippi and creating sustainable support systems through activities such as recruitment campaigns, bonuses, residency and fellowship expansion, apprenticeships, internship development, and professional development. Four targeted grant tracks are available: workforce retention, secondary education medical career outreach, earn-while-you-learn programs, and preceptor expansion. Applicants must measurably benefit rural communities, and all awards support immediate workforce needs and long-term sustainability through collaboration among healthcare providers, educational institutions, workforce organizations, and community partners. Total funding available: $16,800,000. All activities must be completed within the approved performance period.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program Subrecipient Grant to Healthcare Providers to Transform, Innovate, and Regionalize Care
data.issuingAgency: Vermont Agency of Human Services
data.summary: This opportunity supports Vermont healthcare providers in implementing regional care strategies, advancing technology, enhancing shared operations, strengthening the rural health workforce, and building sustainable rural health networks. Funding is provided under Vermont's $195 million Year One Rural Health Transformation (RHT) grant, entirely federal CMS/HHS funded, to catalyze health system transformation. Proposals must address care innovation, technology and interoperability, shared services, or hospital designation/service transformation that coordinates care across geographic regions. Eligible uses may include redesign of service delivery (e.g., shifts from hospital to outpatient settings, regional workforce models, health IT upgrades), but funds cannot be used for capital construction, duplicative activities, or services reimbursable by insurance. Program goals emphasize improved health outcomes, population health, care quality, provider stabilization, affordability, and workforce sustainability. Grants are for 10-11 months (depending on start), with up to four 1-year extensions possible with AHS/CMS approval.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program - Facility Upgrades to Support Regionalization
data.issuingAgency: State of Vermont Agency of Human Services
data.summary: Grant opportunity for rural health care facilities in Vermont to support facility upgrades and regionalization. The program aims to strengthen rural health care delivery through minor physical renovations and refurbishments, enabling network and workforce enhancements, technology advancement only as part of facility upgrades, and improved access for Vermonters. Eligible projects support service realignment, shared operations, and integrated care delivery envisioned under Vermont’s regionalization strategy. Upgrades must comply with federal and state requirements, including safety standards, building codes (ADA Accessibility Standards), and reporting. Year 1 grants support expenditures within the grant period. Funding restrictions exclude pre-award costs, construction/expansion, demolition, cosmetic upgrades that materially increase property value, and supplanting existing funding.

data.title: Michigan Rural Interoperability Skilled Nursing Facility Data Integration Pilot - 2027
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary:
Synopsis 
 As part of RHTP’s Interoperability in Action Initiative, the Rural Data Integration and Infrastructure Fund aims to the advance technology innovation through reducing duplicative care improving health outcomes through interoperable systems. This funding opportunity will advance interoperability and digital infrastructure for rural and left-behind providers to strengthen care coordination and reduce administrative burden.

data.title: Michigan Rural Interoperability for Local Health Department Access and Connectivity-2027
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary: As part of RHTP’s Interoperability in Action Initiative, the Rural Access and Connectivity Fund aims to advance technology innovation by reducing duplicative care and improving health outcomes through interoperable systems. This funding opportunity will expand access to care, social services, and community resources through connected systems and real-time information sharing.

data.title: Michigan Rural Health Interoperability in Action Initiative - 2027
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary:
Synopsis 
 As part of RHTP’s Interoperability in Action Initiative, the Rural Data Integration and Infrastructure Fund aims to the advance technology innovation through reducing duplicative care improving health outcomes through interoperable systems. This funding opportunity will advance interoperability and digital infrastructure for rural and left-behind providers to strengthen care coordination and reduce administrative burden.

data.title: Workforce Innovation Grant: Healthcare Employment, Access, and Rural Transformation (WIG:HEART)
data.issuingAgency: Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development (DWD)
data.summary: The Workforce Innovation Grant: Healthcare Employment, Access, and Rural Transformation (WIG:HEART) funds competitive regional and partnership-based grants for innovative projects addressing healthcare workforce challenges in rural and semi-rural Wisconsin communities. The program supports recruitment and retention of clinical staff, expansion of health education pathways (including nursing, mental health, and allied health fields), training partnerships, wrap-around services for low-income and underrepresented groups, regional care innovation (such as micro-clinics and telehealth), and technology adoption. Eligible lead applicants are nonprofits and governmental entities serving eligible rural counties; awards range from $500,000 to $10 million for up to four years. Annual renewals are contingent on performance. Activities must directly address workforce gaps and transformative care delivery models aligned with priorities outlined in the Grant Program Announcement.

data.title: Mississippi RHTP: Psychiatric Emergency Services (PES) – EmPATH Units Grant Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: Mississippi Department of Mental Health (DMH) – Rural Health Transformation Program (BRIDGE initiative)
data.summary: Mississippi's Rural Health Transformation Program is seeking proposals to expand psychiatric emergency services in rural communities through EmPATH units. The official funding page publishes the NOFO, public questions-and-answers, a recommended supply list, and the live application link.
applicantTypes: Hospitals meeting HRSA rural eligibility criteria

data.title: Psychiatric Emergency Services - EmPATH Units
data.issuingAgency: Mississippi Department of Mental Health (DMH) in partnership with Mississippi Rural Health Transformation Program (MSRHTP)
data.summary: Supports Mississippi-located hospitals meeting HRSA rural criteria or CAH designation in establishing, expanding, or sustaining Psychiatric Emergency Services EmPATH Units. Part of Mississippi's Rural Health Transformation Plan and funded under the Federal Rural Health Transformation Program Cooperative Agreement. Funding is provided for projects that deliver rapid access, assessment, and care for individuals experiencing behavioral health crises, with a goal of reducing unnecessary inpatient psychiatric admissions and improving rural mental health outcomes. Awardees must meet all federal and state compliance requirements and complete project expenditures by July 31, 2027.

data.title: PATH 1.4: Community Care Hub
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: Utah's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is soliciting applications to design, select, and deploy a data-driven, scalable model for the state's first Community Care Hub (CCH) — an operational backbone connecting local organizations and individuals to address health and social needs in rural communities, aligned with federal RHTP PATH initiative benchmarks. Up to $2,000,000 is available in Year 1, with one anticipated award; total program funding may reach up to $18,000,000 over 5 years, contingent on future CMS/HHS RHTP awards.

data.title: North Dakota Technology as an Extender Funding Opportunity (Solicitation 210-231)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services (ND HHS), through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), offers the Technology as an Extender funding opportunity to support North Dakota rural and tribal health facilities in implementing smart technology, robotics, and AI-based solutions that address provider shortages and advance care delivery for rural residents. This competitive opportunity allocates approximately $5 million in federal funds for up to 20 awards, each averaging $250,000. Funded projects may include acquisition and staff vendor training for remote patient monitoring (facility-based only), AI-enabled digital engagement, care coordination tools, robotics for clinical and environmental efficiency, and electronic caregiver systems. Priority is given to projects introducing equipment not currently owned or in active use by the applicant, particularly those that improve organizational efficiency, enhance safety and care quality, reduce the rural cost burden, and measurably impact Initiative 2 metrics: rural provider capacity, care quality, and access. All equipment and technology purchases must align with eligible uses. Awardees are required to report on workforce and project impact metrics for up to five years, in accordance with Initiative 2 of the state's RHTP, and are subject to quarterly and annual reporting. Award funds cannot supplant existing funding, duplicate other program awards, or support unallowable costs as defined by state and federal guidelines.
applicantTypes: Non-federally operated Indian Health Services facilities
Federally Qualified Health Centers (serving ≥50% ND rural residents)

data.title: DOH61365 SFY27 Rural Hospital Peer Group Funding Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health
data.summary: Ohio Department of Health’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), authorized by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Section 71403 of Public Law 119-21), is offering a one-time, equally divided total of $30,304,539 to eligible hospitals in the rural peer group (per OAC 5160-2-05, excluding those in non-statewide state directed payment programs per 42 CFR 438.6 or Am. Sub. HB 96). This funding supports rural hospital sustainability and participation in clinically integrated networks or rural health hubs. Allowable uses include IT system improvements, workforce and clinical initiatives, integration or formation of networks, quality improvement, behavioral health, specific infrastructure upgrades (excluding new construction), and other activities aligning with CMS RHTP priorities. Recipients must: (1) attend/review the 6/29/2026 pre-application session, (2) submit a letter of interest affirming commitment to RHTP goals and allowable uses, and (3) submit a categorized budget sheet by the deadlines. Funds are distributed on a reimbursement basis and must be fully expended by 6/30/2027. See Attachment A for hospital eligibility and Attachments B/C for specific use and admin cap details.
applicantTypes: Hospitals classified in the rural peer group per OAC 5160-2-05 and listed in Attachment A
Not participating in a non-statewide state directed payment program (42 CFR 438.6, Am. Sub. HB 96)

data.title: Maryland Healthcare Workforce Data Clearinghouse: Phase 1 Requirements Analysis and Future Planning (BPM058186)
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Population Health Improvement
data.summary: The Maryland Department of Health's Office of Population Health Improvement (OPHI) solicits one applicant to conduct a detailed requirements analysis and develop future planning documentation for Phase 1 of the Maryland Healthcare Workforce Data Clearinghouse, a centralized digital repository to collect, validate, and standardize healthcare workforce data. The Clearinghouse will help address Maryland's rural healthcare provider shortages through rapid stakeholder engagement and use of existing state infrastructure such as CRISP. The Phase 1 project will encompass: (1) orientation to the current state and prior planning work; (2) development of immediate use cases for underserved area analysis; (3) churn and trend analysis among primary and specialty care workforce; (4) service commitment tracking for workforce program participants; and (5) creation of a roadmap for clearinghouse build and long-term sustainability. The award is supported via the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) immediate impact funds, is open only to eligible Maryland-based organizations, and will result in one award of up to $649,385 for work conducted from October 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027.
applicantTypes: Maryland public colleges or state universities
Maryland local, state, or federal government agencies

data.title: North Dakota RHTP: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation Acquisition
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: Competitive RHTP funding for existing community-based healthcare organizations to purchase new accessible vans or transportation vehicles for NEMT within or from rural areas to care delivery. Eligible vehicles include small or large chassis vans with wheelchair lifts, passenger seating, and vehicle tracking hardware. Applicants must propose acquisition of new vehicles to expand transportation access for rural and rural tribal Medicaid-enrolled populations; replacing or upgrading existing vehicles is unallowable. Funded projects are expected to support Initiative 3 of North Dakota’s RHTP: improving access to care by reducing avoidable emergency department visits, enhancing care coordination, and improving timeliness of specialist appointments for Medicaid beneficiaries in rural areas. Awards are anticipated to be collaborative in design but financially independent, requiring robust reporting by individual applicants.
applicantTypes: Non-federally operated Indian Health Services facilities

data.title: Coordinating Care Across Wisconsin: Innovating Healthcare Through Partnership Grants (RHTP)
data.issuingAgency: Wisconsin Department of Health Services
data.summary: This five-year Wisconsin Department of Health Services (DHS) opportunity invites applications for partnership grants focused on care coordination and healthcare innovation in rural and semi-rural Wisconsin. The program aims to address primary, specialty, and behavioral health workforce shortages, fragmented systems of care, and improve health outcomes among Medicaid-eligible and other rural populations. Funding is released in two phases: a six-month planning grant (Phase 1) and, for qualified applicants, a four-year implementation grant (Phase 2). Projects must establish or expand innovative and sustainable care partnerships that provide measurable health outcome improvements for rural and semi-rural communities.

data.title: Kansas Dementia-Related Behavioral Supports in Rural Nursing Facilities Pilot
data.issuingAgency: Kansas Department for Aging and Disability Services (KDADS)
data.summary: Pilot program under Kansas's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), issued by the Kansas Department for Aging and Disability Services (KDADS) Aging Services Commission. Six Medicaid-certified rural nursing facilities — one from each KDHE District Office area — will receive funding (up to $200,000 each plus $175 per eligible resident per Medicaid day for up to 90 days, extensions possible) to better support Medicaid recipients aged 60+ with dementia who exhibit complex behaviors. Facilities will use funds for specialized training, technical assistance, subject-matter-expert consultation, and enhanced person-centered care services for eligible residents. Goals include: improving staff capacity and quality of care for individuals with complex dementia-related behaviors, increasing behavioral health supports, and informing future Medicaid program design. Participation requires submitting completed KDADS Supplier Verification and Policy Packet, all federal compliance forms, a program narrative (population, project description, data/outcomes), and a Tax Clearance Certificate. Awardees are classified as CMS federal grant subrecipients and subject to 2 CFR Part 200 compliance.

data.title: CalRHT EHR Modernization Grant Program (Initiative 3: Technology and Tools)
data.issuingAgency: California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI)
data.summary: CalRHT Initiative 3: Technology and Tools — EHR Modernization Grant Program provides subawards up to $2,000,000 for first-time adoption/configuration of a certified EHR, or full replacement of an existing EHR with a certified EHR (incremental upgrades are not eligible). Eligible applicants: rural hospitals (including Critical Access Hospitals and acute psychiatric), FQHCs/FQHC Look-Alikes (including Tribal), Rural Health Clinics, and Tribal/IHS clinics physically located in a rural area. Funded through California's CMS/HHS Rural Health Transformation Program award ($233,639,308.46 total state award). Applications open July 20, 2026; close August 21, 2026 at 3:00 p.m.

data.title: AHCCCS Rural Health Innovative Care Pilot Program RFGA
data.issuingAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)
data.summary: Grant to support innovative care models, mobile and satellite services, and alternative payment initiatives to increase rural health care access in Arizona. Part of the federally funded Arizona Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), this opportunity aims to pilot healthcare delivery models, behavioral health expansions, technical assistance, opioid antagonist distribution, and shared services in underserved rural and Tribal communities. AHCCCS, alongside other state agencies, administers funding awarded under H.R. 1, Title VII, Section 71401 and allocated by CMS to Arizona for FY26. The program emphasizes expanding telehealth, medical technology, rural health education, and rural health resilience.

data.title: Community Health Workers (CHW) Training Providers
data.issuingAgency: Wisconsin Department of Health Services (DHS)
data.summary: The Wisconsin Department of Health Services (DHS) invites applications from organizations to serve as Community Health Worker (CHW) Training Providers for grant-funded activities under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) workforce initiative. Successful applicants will design, deliver, and assess training programs for CHWs and CHW supervisors statewide, including two required components: CHW Core Competency training (minimum 40 hours, competency-based) and CHW Supervisor/Leader training (minimum 20 hours, focused on supervision and leadership in CHW programs). Up to $600,000 per year is available (pending annual CMS approval) across all awards; individual awards anticipated between $150,000 and $300,000 annually. The project period is October 1, 2026 – July 31, 2029. This RFA is for provider organizations delivering CHW and CHW Supervisor training and is distinct from related grants for CHW-employing sites.

data.title: Idaho RHTP Facility Technology Assessment
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
data.summary: Solicitation for a contractor to assess technology at Idaho rural healthcare facilities, guide shared infrastructure strategy, and develop evaluation/reporting systems. Competitive RFP targeting rural and nonprofit providers. Part of Idaho RHTP FY26 facility technology investment initiative.

data.title: Missouri RHTP Home Visiting Funding (Children's Trust Fund RFP)
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Department of Social Services (DSS) / MO HealthNet Division, administered via Children's Trust Fund (CTF)
data.summary: The Missouri Department of Social Services, through the Children's Trust Fund (CTF), seeks applications to fund new nurse-based home visiting services under the Rural Health Transformation Program. Awards support HomVEE-approved evidence-based home visiting models only. Up to $100,000 available for model licensing fees/staff training for organizations starting a new home visiting program, or up to $488,000 for organizations expanding an existing evidence-based program. Funds are expansion-only — may not supplant existing services. Grants are renewable for up to 4 additional years subject to performance and funding availability.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Funding for Home Visiting
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Children’s Trust Fund (CTF)
data.summary: The Missouri Children’s Trust Fund (CTF) is offering $588,000 annually to support the initiation and expansion of nurse-led, evidence-based home visiting in rural Missouri through its Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The program aims to improve maternal and child health for families residing in eligible rural areas, with services to be delivered exclusively by licensed nurses implementing HomVEE-approved home visiting models—including, per Amendment 1, Family Connects—while demonstrating model fidelity. Awardees may request up to $100,000 for model fees and training (cap across all grantees), and up to $488,000 for program expansion, with indirect costs capped at 8%. Funded activities cannot supplant current funding and must represent expansion. Required participation includes regional Hub-based networks (Collective Impact sites), CRIS Referral Partner networks, compliance with REDCap data collection (including custom schedules for Family Connects), quarterly three-tiered CQI activities, and annual FCSR and MOVECHS background checks for all relevant staff/volunteers. Grantees must invoice monthly for reimbursement, retain fiscal and program records, comply with audits and site visits, and protect participant privacy under HIPAA and CTF policy. Contracts have a 1-year base with up to four annual renewals, subject to performance and funding. Awardees must register as MissouriBUYS vendors, participate in E-Verify, be current on state taxes, federally compliant, and able to engage in all required reporting and improvement processes.

data.title: Iowa Rural Residency Program Development (RFP PHTHORC27001)
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is soliciting applications through RFP PHTHORC27001 for the Iowa Rural Residency Program. This initiative, with up to $10.5 million available statewide, aims to support the planning, design, and initial implementation of new or expanded ACGME-accredited rural residency programs or rural training tracks in Internal Medicine or Obstetrics/Gynecology. The program is intended to strengthen Iowa’s rural healthcare workforce by enhancing physician training opportunities in areas meeting federal rural criteria. Individual awards will not exceed $750,000 for the initial three-year base term (September 1, 2026 – August 31, 2029), with up to three additional one-year extensions possible for a maximum six-year contract term (ending no later than October 31, 2032). At least 50% of resident training must take place at sites meeting the Federal Office of Rural Health Policy definition of rural. Eligible applicants include Iowa-based hospitals, health systems, graduate medical education consortia, and non-profit organizations targeting counties with populations under 150,000 and not including university main campuses. Applications must include a detailed budget for the first contract year and be submitted via IowaGrants.gov. Only one application per service area is permitted per organization.

data.title: Michigan Rural Mental Health Care Expansion - 2027
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary:
Synopsis 
 As part of RHTP’s Care Closer to Home Blueprint Initiative, the Advancing Rural Behavioral Health Blueprint aims to transform access to care in rural communities by creating sustainable, community-based pathways that bring health services closer to where people live and work. By connecting partners across health and social sectors, the initiative reimagines care delivery, improve transportation access, and simplify access to primary and behavioral health. Through innovative approaches to chronic disease management, maternal and child health, and behavioral health, it seeks to improve outcomes while making care more efficient, coordinated, and person-centered. This funding opportunity supports innovative adaptations of traditional care models to expand access to community-based behavioral health services in rural areas while reducing costs by avoiding unnecessary hospitalizations and limiting reliance on law enforcement.

data.title: WIC Program Statewide Personnel & Service Delivery
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board
data.summary: The South Dakota Department of Health, Office of Family Nutrition Services (OFNS) seeks proposals from qualified agencies to hire, employ, and manage staff delivering WIC program services across South Dakota. The awarded agency will be responsible for recruiting, supervising, and providing oversight of administrative, nutrition, data, and professional staff essential to WIC operations, as specified in Appendix A. Staff assignments and placements will be coordinated with WIC Dietitian Managers, the Office Administrator, and the Grants/Contract Manager. The agency must maintain staffing levels to meet program needs, adapt to changing funding allocations from the USDA Food and Nutrition Service (FNS), and provide consistent, participant-centered services promoting nutrition and access to resources for WIC-eligible individuals and families.

data.title: West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program Career Pathway Advancement for Healthcare Workers
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health and Human Resources
data.summary: This opportunity requests proposals from eligible entities to support 150 workers in advancing their healthcare career pathway as part of the West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program. The aim is to enhance the healthcare workforce pipeline by funding innovative approaches to career advancement for rural healthcare workers.
applicantTypes: Other entities capable of workforce development

data.title: West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program: Healthcare Career Pathways Outreach
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: This funding opportunity seeks proposals from entities able to expose at least 10,000 high school students in West Virginia to healthcare career pathways through outreach activities. The objective is early engagement to improve rural health workforce development. Successful applicants must demonstrate capacity for broad outreach and engagement, in alignment with the aims of the West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program.

data.title: Pennsylvania Rural Health Transformation Plan Rapid Response Stabilization Payments — Round 2
data.issuingAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services
data.summary: The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (DHS) announces the second round of Rapid Response Stabilization payments under the RHTP. Up to $35,000,000 statewide is available, with a cap of $1,000,000 per eligible location and a minimum request of $10,000 per site. Qualified entities include hospitals licensed as general acute care by the Pennsylvania Department of Health, health care providers as defined in 42 U.S.C. §1397ee(h)(9), or rural health facilities as defined in 42 U.S.C. §1397ee(h)(3)(D), all operating in Pennsylvania since at least December 29, 2025. Projects must target at least one of six RHTP initiatives: Aging and Access, Behavioral Health, Maternal Health, EMS and Transportation, Technology and Infrastructure, and Workforce. Eligible locations are defined by rural county class (4–8) or HRSA rural census tract criteria in counties of the second class A or third class. Entities that received Round 1 payments (May 1–June 1, 2026) are not eligible for Round 2. Submissions open August 17, 2026 at 8:00 AM and close August 24, 2026 at 11:59 PM, or earlier if the statewide cap is met. Initial regional caps limit awards to two payments per RHTP region until all regions have two payments; then the cap lifts. Required attachments include: Entity Location List (if multi-location), license/certificate, documentation of provider/facility status, Budget Narrative and Budget Worksheet (templates), third-party quote/estimate, FFATA data sheet for requests >$30,000, and Funding Disclosure Table. All costs must be for eligible supplies and equipment that stabilize or enhance rural healthcare (no EHRs, ambulances, or ongoing projects requiring departmental monitoring), expended by July 31, 2027, and documented within 30 days of incurrence. Entities must retain audit records until February 27, 2031.

data.title: Mountain State Care Force – Rural Healthcare Apprenticeships
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health, Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: This opportunity, part of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), provides $2 million in Year 1 funding to support West Virginia entities in co-funding paid, entry-level healthcare apprenticeships in rural areas. The program aims to build workforce pipelines for high-need positions (e.g., technicians, EMTs), directly addressing critical rural health workforce shortages through wage and structured training support. Funding is performance-based and tied to employment and retention outcomes. Apprenticeship recipients must commit to a five-year rural service term. Awards will support up to 121 total apprenticeships in Year 1. The opportunity requires submission of a Detailed Line-Item Budget (DLIB) worksheet and a budget narrative as per RHTP DLIB Budget Instructions. Applicant questions are accepted through May 5, 2026, with answers posted publicly.

data.title: NC ROOTS — Trillium: Food is Medicine Community Training Partner (Regions 2 & 5)
data.issuingAgency: Trillium Health Resources (NC ROOTS Hub Lead, Regions 2 & 5)
data.summary: Trillium Health Resources (as the NC ROOTS Hub Lead for Regions 2 and 5) invites applications for the NC ROOTS Initiative 1 — Food is Medicine Community Training Partner. This competitive funding opportunity seeks partners to provide Food is Medicine community training and program development in Regions 2 and 5. The opportunity is supported under a CMS/HHS financial assistance award as part of the NC ROOTS program, aiming to expand nutrition access and services through community partnership. Program details, eligibility, and application guidance are available on the official Trillium Health Resources Region 2 and Region 5 web pages. Funding amount is not specified in the source.

data.title: NC ROOTS — Trillium: NCCARE360 Adoption (Regions 2 & 5)
data.issuingAgency: Trillium Health Resources (NC ROOTS Hub Lead, Regions 2 & 5)
data.summary: RFA# THR-ROOTS2-2026-001, Trillium Health Resources' NC ROOTS Initiative 1 (NCCARE360 Adoption), issued identically for both Region 2 and Region 5. Trillium is the only one of NC's 5 ROOTS hub organizations (Impact Health, Trillium, Vaya Health, UNC Health, Access East) currently showing a live RFA. No funding/budget amount is stated in the source document.

data.title: RHTP Community Health Access and Navigation (CHANT) Call Center
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Community Health Access and Navigation (CHANT) Call Center, a Tennessee Department of Health initiative to improve healthcare access and navigation in state communities. The awarded contractor will provide professional services through a call center system, supporting coordinated health access in compliance with Tennessee's service contract requirements. Selection is through a competitive fee-for-service process as outlined in the RFP. The RFP is posted on the TN General Services portal and is open for application from July 6, 2026 to August 25, 2026.

data.title: Bureau of Maternal Child and Family Health OhioDENTAL Program
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health, Bureau of Maternal Child and Family Health, Oral Health Program
data.summary: This solicitation invites applications for the OhioDENTAL Program, administered by the Bureau of Maternal Child and Family Health (Oral Health Program) under the Ohio Department of Health, as part of the Rural Health Transformation Program. The program aims to expand or establish mobile dental programs in Ohio’s 73 Rural Health Transformation counties, focusing on children in schools where at least 40% of students qualify for free/reduced lunch. Up to $14,868,000 will support up to 20 subrecipients to deliver comprehensive dental services in eligible schools and communities, prioritizing areas lacking a safety net dental clinic. Funded programs can use dental and dental hygiene students to expand workforce capacity. Mobile programs are reimbursed at $200 per visit for uninsured children. Programs must comply with CDC/OSHA standards, provide referrals for services not offered in the mobile setting, and report detailed demographic and service data to ODH. The funded project period is projected for September 7, 2026 – August 31, 2027, with optional renewals for up to four additional years depending on performance, need, and appropriations.

data.title: TN - 2026 - RFP #34320-21227 Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Marketing and Advertising Services Solicitation
data.issuingAgency: Department of Health, State of Tennessee
data.summary: The State of Tennessee is seeking service providers for marketing and advertising services to support the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Applicants must complete a non-disclosure agreement before obtaining the full solicitation details due to confidential information requirements. The goal is to enhance outreach and visibility of RHTP initiatives across rural Tennessee.

data.title: Embedding Substance Use Disorder Support Services in Washington Emergency Departments
data.issuingAgency: Washington State Health Care Authority (HCA)
data.summary: Solicits bids for the embedding of Substance Use Disorder (SUD) Support Service Positions within hospital emergency departments to deliver patient-centered support, facilitate medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder (MOUD), and improve linkages to ongoing care. Hospitals must partner with a local behavioral health agency to embed qualified staff in their emergency departments, utilizing evidence-based practices such as peer support, MOUD facilitation, shared decision making, staff education, and care coordination. The embedded role aims to enhance quality of care for individuals with opioid and other substance use disorders through real-time intervention, team collaboration, and follow-up services after discharge, aligning with ESSB 5998 Section 214(73) and leveraging resources like ScalaNW. Contracts will be awarded for up to $75,000 each, with total program funding capped at $225,000, and will prioritize Washington Small Businesses and Certified Veteran-Owned Businesses for selection. Multiple awards are possible for eligible acute care hospitals statewide.

data.title: Rural Texas Strong Program – Initiative 4 (Round 2): The Next Generation of the Small Town Doctor and Team
data.issuingAgency: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) — Office of Rural Hospital Finance
data.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) is accepting applications for Rural Texas Strong Initiative 4 (Round 2): The Next Generation of the Small Town Doctor and Team. The program is supported by CMS as part of Texas's Rural Health Transformation Program award (100% CMS/USDHHS funded). Purpose: assist eligible rural healthcare providers with recruiting and training healthcare professionals in rural Texas communities by building local education/training pipelines and developing retention strategies for providers practicing in rural areas.

data.title: Washington RHTP OTP Workforce Incentive Program (2026HCA9)
data.issuingAgency: Washington State Health Care Authority (HCA)
data.summary: The Washington State Health Care Authority (HCA), with support from CMS/HHS, is soliciting applications from licensed Opioid Treatment Program (OTP) providers for the Rural Health Transformation – OTP Workforce Incentive Program, RFA #2026HCA9. The program aims to stabilize, expand, and sustain the rural WA OTP workforce through financial incentives—including recruitment and retention bonuses, relocation assistance, childcare stipends, workforce training, capacity payments, infrastructure support for flexible work arrangements, clinician licensure expenses, and other approved incentives associated with a five-year rural service commitment. All incentives must be tied directly to workforce retention for clinicians/positions acting within WA DOH definitions—including SUDP counselors, mental health professionals, nurses, medical prescribers, certified SUD peers, pharmacists, perinatal providers, and related multidisciplinary roles—serving rural populations; applicants may be urban if rural clients are demonstrably served (as per CMS/HRSA/OFM definitions). Applicants are responsible for tracking and reporting rural service and workforce obligations, and hardship waivers and prorated repayment formulas are permitted for incomplete service commitments (see RFA and Fact Sheet guidance). The contract structure uses a Professional Services Contract for the program term, with annual Work Orders for funding and deliverables. Awards for Budget Period #1 range from $100,000–$500,000 per organization (total available: $6.2 million, funds must be expended by September 30, 2027). Budget Period #2 (pending CMS approval) similarly offers $100,000–$500,000 per organization, with funds to be expended by September 30, 2028. Each OTP site may submit only one application. All funds are 100% federal (CFDA RHTCMS332044) with compliance required for federal and state rules. Indirect costs are allowed with documentation of a current federally approved rate. Selected applicants must accept contract terms as provided; modifications require submission of a redlined Word version. See RFA for further program details, eligibility exceptions, and required documentation.
applicantTypes: Behavioral Health Agencies (WA DOH licensed, operating as OTPs)
Licensed Opioid Treatment Programs serving rural clients

data.title: North Dakota RHTP: Coordinating and Connecting Care (Solicitation 210-362)
data.issuingAgency: North Dakota Health and Human Services
data.summary: North Dakota Health and Human Services announces a competitive funding opportunity as part of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Initiative 3: Bring High-Quality Healthcare Closer to Home. This Year 1 award, 'Coordinating and Connecting Care' (Solicitation 210-362), will issue approximately $1,000,000 in federal funds to support planning for a neutral, statewide Community Information Exchange (CIE) and closed-loop referral system focused on rural and Medicaid-serving providers. The grant aims to strengthen cross-sector partnerships, assess care coordination gaps, and lay the groundwork for state-wide decision-making on future care coordination, referral, and secure information exchange infrastructure for rural and tribal populations. Year 1 funding supports planning only and does not authorize implementation or procurement of a statewide system. Eligible applicants include HIE/CIE organizations, rural health networks, healthcare associations, collaboratives, higher education institutions, research organizations, community-based or volunteer organizations, payer/managed-care organizations, and governmental or quasi-governmental entities. Applicants must demonstrate a rural focus, but do not need to be rural-located. Partnerships are allowed with a designated lead applicant/fiscal agent. All applications must be submitted via Qualtrics no later than August 26, 2026, 5:00 p.m. CT.

data.title: West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program — Rural Health Link EMS Collaboratives: Alternative Destination Transportation Year 1 Grant
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health
data.summary:
This competitive grant opportunity supports the establishment, expansion, and operationalization of county and multi-county EMS alternative destination transport programs statewide under the Rural Health Link initiative, part of West Virginia's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Funded by a $2.7 million allocation, the program is designed to catalyze durable, collaborative EMS-led transport models that route low-acuity rural patients to clinically appropriate, lower-cost care settings—including Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), primary care, urgent care clinics, behavioral health, and substance use disorder treatment providers—rather than defaulting to emergency departments. The initiative prioritizes transformation, including new destination models, formal provider partnerships, clinical protocol development, technology integration, workflow redesign, and expansion to areas of greatest need. Activities are strictly intended to launch and support new care delivery approaches and must not duplicate any existing value-based initiatives or mandated programs.

Applicants must demonstrate operational capacity to implement new models, readiness to adopt state-approved clinical protocols, ongoing training for EMS personnel and partners, coordinated data reporting meeting CMS and State requirements, and a sustainability and scale plan for post-award continuation. Applicants are required to either show existing provider partnerships or clear plans to establish MOUs or agreements within 30 days of award. Milestone-based funding will be released according to start-up, protocol approval, launch, ongoing operations, and sustainability planning achievements. Grantees must provide monthly and quarterly reports with detailed metrics—such as reductions in emergency department transports, improved care utilization, partnership development, and operational sustainability. Compliance with Office of Emergency Medical Services (OEMS) requirements and robust data integration are mandatory. Non-compliance or failure to meet performance/milestone requirements may result in claw-back, termination, or reallocation of funds per State discretion. This opportunity is open to eligible applicants in all West Virginia counties and aligns with CMS-approved RHTP frameworks focused on improving access, quality, and sustainability in rural health.
applicantTypes: Volunteer Fire Department with EMS Squad

data.title: RHL Public Transportation
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health – Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: The West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), administered by the West Virginia Department of Health, is soliciting competitive applications for the Rural Health Link (RHL): Public Transportation Collaboratives initiative. Up to $1.5 million will be awarded for Year 1 to establish and operationalize regionally-governed, multi-county public transportation collaboratives. These collaboratives must coordinate non-emergency medical transportation (NEMT) through shared dispatch and scheduling infrastructure across jurisdictions to reduce fragmentation, minimize duplication of services, and measurably improve access to care for rural and underserved populations. Eligible entities must demonstrate operational capacity for managing multi-county coordination, formal governance structures, partnership agreements, and integration with the State's data and mobility technology platform. Priority is given to applicants demonstrating readiness for rapid launch, regional integration, measurable outcomes (e.g., reduced avoidable ED utilization, improved treatment adherence, increased workforce participation), and robust sustainability and expansion plans. All activities must support the RHTP’s model of durable, statewide rural health infrastructure. Fund distribution is milestone-based, and all funded projects must be operational within the grant period and show readiness, data reporting, and compliance with CMS and State requirements.
applicantTypes: Non-profit organizations with NEMT or multi-county transportation experience
Other entities with demonstrated experience coordinating/delivering services across multiple jurisdictions

data.title: DOH61908: OhioSEE & RHT Program Cost Proposal Form
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health, Bureau of Maternal, Child & Family Health
data.summary: ODH's Bureau of Maternal, Child & Family Health is seeking proposals from qualified providers to deliver comprehensive, school-based K-12 vision services (OhioSEE) across eligible Ohio regions, funded under the Rural Health Transformation Program. Bidder Conference: 8/13/2026, 9-11am. Inquiry End Date: 8/20/2026, 3pm (questions to Procurement@odh.ohio.gov, subject line "DOH61908 Inquiry"). Application End Date: 8/27/2026, 3pm (submit to Procurement@odh.ohio.gov, subject line "DOH61908 Proposal Application").

data.title: Washington RHTP Provider Technology Fund (2026HCA12)
data.issuingAgency: Washington State Health Care Authority
data.summary: The Washington State Health Care Authority (HCA) solicits applications for the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) – Provider Technology Fund (RFA #2026HCA12). This fund supports technology adoption, telehealth expansion, data infrastructure improvements, and operational modernization for rural health care providers serving Washington's rural communities. The program aims to drive long-term system transformation, strengthen rural health access, improve care coordination, and foster sustainability and equity in rural health systems. Funding of up to $11.5 million is available per budget/performance period, with individual awards ranging from $200,000 to $500,000 per applicant, per period. Applications outside this range are non-responsive. Organizations may apply for up to $500,000 in each eligible period (Budget Period 1 and Budget Period 2, pending CMS approval), for a combined potential total of $1,000,000. Awarded funds can be used for up-front costs for purchasing/licensing new technology tools, securing technical assistance, facilitating regional coordination, and covering eligible personnel, administrative, implementation, and training expenses as specified in Exhibit D. Subcontractors may be used for service delivery; subawards/subrecipients are not allowed. The contract term spans from date of execution (anticipated September–October 2026, but no later than October 30, 2026) through September 30, 2031, with funding obligated through discrete Work Orders per Budget/Performance Period. All expenditures must comply with federal regulations, including OMB CFDA RHTCMS332044 and 2 CFR Part 200. Detailed eligibility and requirements are provided in the RFA Notice and amendments.
applicantTypes: Nonprofit and private health care organizations

data.title: AZRHTP - Adopt Shared Services Consortiums
data.issuingAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)
data.summary: AHCCCS issues this sixth public solicitation under the Arizona Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP): Request for Grant Applications (RFGA) YH-27-0025, to support Adopt Shared Services Consortiums. This RFGA funds development and implementation of shared service models among rural and Tribal healthcare providers across rural Arizona. Projects may feature shared staffing models (joint employment, traveling clinicians, locum tenens), shared training/education programs, joint IT/data infrastructure, centralized billing/coding, common scheduling, co-located service hubs, supply chain cooperatives, shared compliance functions, and regional service networks, aiming to reduce operational costs, eliminate duplication, and enhance financial and clinical capacity. Three funding tiers support projects from two organizations up to regional hub models. Strict administrative and capital expenditure caps apply. Funded projects must create new or expanded shared-service activities, not supplant or duplicate existing service or funding streams. Tribal partnerships are encouraged and prioritized.
applicantTypes: School-based health centers in rural areas

data.title: Adopt Shared Services Consortiums (Arizona RHTP YH27-0025)
data.issuingAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)
data.summary: This competitive grant opportunity, funded under the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) and administered by AHCCCS, is designed to foster shared service models that increase operational efficiency and sustainability among rural and Tribal health providers in Arizona. Three funding tiers are available, supporting projects from single-function arrangements (e.g., shared billing) to comprehensive regional shared-services hubs. Eligible activities include joint staffing, collaborative training, shared data systems, facilities co-location, joint purchasing, and compliance collaboration. Emphasis is placed on forming self-sustaining rural provider networks and long-term shared service hubs. Funding draws from Arizona’s FY26 RHTP allocation of $166,988,956, subject to a 10% administrative cap (7% for subrecipients), and all proposed activities must represent an expansion or enhancement of current services, not a replacement. Applicants must demonstrate measurable improvements in efficiency, capacity, and scope for rural and Tribal populations, with bonus evaluation points for Tribal engagement and projects serving fully rural counties.

data.title: Re-Open Provider Productivity Support Fund
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: This opportunity provides funding for rural hospitals, clinics, and stand-alone provider offices in West Virginia to help offset their high clinical and administrative operating expenses. The 2026 re-opening of the Provider Productivity Support Fund (RHT-AFA-05-08-2026-SCC) delivers direct financial support for projects that modernize operations, invest in technology, restructure service lines, and establish shared service collaboratives—key focus areas for improving productivity and administrative efficiency under the West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program SmartCare Catalyst initiative.

data.title: CCG EMS Community Paramedicine
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: The West Virginia Department of Health Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Connected Care Grid pillar is soliciting competitive applications from state-licensed EMS agencies to implement or expand community paramedicine, mobile integrated health, and treat-in-place models within WVOEMS Region 1. The aim is to reduce avoidable emergency department utilization, improve access to care in rural areas, and integrate EMS with regional care networks. Funded activities include protocol-authorized on-scene assessment and treatment, care coordination, participation in statewide data and reporting infrastructure, workforce development, and procurement of approved equipment and technology. This is a milestone-based, one-year sub-award totaling $1,033,840, with payments tied to achievement of key deliverables across all counties in Region 1 (McDowell, Mercer, Monroe, Raleigh, Summers, Wyoming). Applicants must ensure compliance with all reporting, data, and partnership requirements and demonstrate ability to serve the full regional footprint, either independently or in partnership.

data.title: MSCF AFA - Rural Graduate Medical Education & Training Capacity
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health, Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: This competitive AFA under the West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) solicits proposals to expand rural graduate medical education and workforce development capacity statewide, with a total of up to $5 million available for Year 1 funding (ending July 31, 2027). The emphasis is on growing faculty and adding rural residency and fellowship slots in critical health professions including medicine, pharmacy, nursing, and physician assistant programs. Priority is given to applicants serving high-need and Health Professional Shortage Area counties. Eligible activities include co-funding faculty positions at regional colleges and technical programs, increasing rural training slots, and supporting long-term workforce pipeline development. Strict reporting, administrative, and federal cost requirements apply. Applications must be submitted via the WV OASIS Vendor Self Service (VSS) portal.
applicantTypes: Qualified Organizations supporting rural health workforce development

data.title: Rhode Island Rural Community Health Network (RCHN) Development Funding – Initial RHTP Community Engagement
data.issuingAgency: Rhode Island Executive Office of Health and Human Services (EOHHS)
data.summary: This opportunity funds the establishment, scaling, and sustainability of Rural Community Health Networks (RCHNs) in Rhode Island. Eligible applicants are municipalities, public or not-for-profit community-based organizations representing one or more of eighteen designated rural communities. The State’s vision is a community-driven system ensuring every rural resident has timely, coordinated, high quality care locally. Funding supports robust, interconnected networks that address local health priorities through community-driven strategies, with $125,000 for initial engagement and $30,000 for public health supplies per community. The initiative emphasizes local capacity building, cross-sector partnerships, and sustained rural health system transformation. Networks are expected to convene healthcare providers, behavioral health providers, schools, municipal agencies, businesses, residents, and other stakeholders to develop coordinated strategies to improve health and wellbeing in partnership with the State. Funding for subsequent years is based on performance, compliance, and availability, aligning with EOHHS' agreement with CMS; a single entity may represent multiple communities, but only one lead organization per community may contract with the State.

data.title: AZRHTP - Expansion of Mobile Digital Services, Training & Recruitment, and Prevention Programs Addressing Suicide, Trauma, Substance Use
data.issuingAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS)
data.summary: This RFGA is the seventh public solicitation by AHCCCS under the Arizona Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). AHCCCS issues this RFGA to consolidate three program areas: (1) expansion of mobile and digital behavioral health services and crisis stabilization infrastructure; (2) training, recruitment, and retention of behavioral health professionals in rural shortage areas; and (3) community prevention programming addressing suicide, trauma, and substance use, specifically targeted to rural and rural Tribal communities in Arizona. The RFGA provides up to $8.5 million in combined funding per budget year across these areas, employing a tiered approach to match organizational capacity and proposed scope. Projects must represent new or expanded activities beyond current operations and are expected to increase access to behavioral health services, strengthen regional workforce pipelines, and improve population health outcomes. Eligible entities include a wide range of rural health and behavioral health agencies, organizations, clinics, health systems, schools, Tribal programs, and coordinated coalitions as detailed within each program area and funding tier.
applicantTypes: Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) serving rural areas
Tribal health facilities and education programs
Anchor institutions (hospitals, universities, nonprofit healthcare systems)
Prevention coalitions and formal collaborative entities

data.title: Rural Health Care Workforce Retention
data.issuingAgency: Montana Department of Labor and Industry
data.summary: A Request for Information (RFI, DLI-RFI-2027-0091) issued by the Montana Department of Labor and Industry (DLI), as part of the Workforce Initiative of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The RFI is exploring opportunities to support rural healthcare worker retention by identifying potential resilience programs to reduce isolation and burnout. As indicated by the official eMACS/bids.mt.gov listing, DLI seeks information on existing data sets regarding workplace wellness, existing programs and pilot initiatives supporting providers in rural and frontier communities, and invites recommendations on structuring a future procurement or grant-funded project. This includes guidance on separating baseline data from intervention work, vendor selection, planning/pilot phases, occupational/regional priorities, and defining deliverables, measures, timelines, and risk considerations. Open: August 12, 2026, 10:00 AM MDT. Close: August 31, 2026, 2:00 PM MDT.

data.title: Michigan Rural Behavioral Health Intellectual and Development Disabilities Pilot - 2027
data.issuingAgency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services — Policy Planning and Access
data.summary: As part of RHTP's Care Closer to Home Blueprint Initiative, the Advancing Rural Behavioral Health Blueprint aims to transform access to care in rural communities by creating sustainable, community-based pathways that bring health services closer to where people live and work. By connecting partners across health and social sectors, the initiative reimagines care delivery, improves transportation access, and simplifies access to primary and behavioral health. The initiative will support innovative behavioral health models that increase access in rural areas, reduce unnecessary hospitalizations and reliance on law enforcement, and improve services for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD). The initiative will also support efforts to establish and maintain accurate data on the prevalence of I/DD in rural communities to inform planning and improve service delivery.
applicantTypes: Other Eligible Entities Serving Rural Communities

data.title: NC ROOTS — Trillium: LOCATe Implementation (Regions 2 & 5)
data.issuingAgency: Trillium Health Resources (NC ROOTS Hub Lead, Regions 2 & 5)
data.summary: Trillium Health Resources, as the NC ROOTS Hub Lead for Regions 2 & 5, is soliciting applications for the NC ROOTS Initiative 2: LOCATe Implementation. This opportunity funds the implementation of the CDC's Levels of Care Assessment Tool (LOCATe) across all birthing hospitals in Region 2 (13 counties) and Region 5 (15 counties) of North Carolina. Supported by the CMS-funded North Carolina Rural Health Transformation Program (NCRHTP), the project aims to establish a standardized baseline of hospital-level maternal and neonatal care capacity, identify regional service gaps, guide facility improvements, and address perinatal health disparities, especially in rural, high-need, and underserved areas. Applicants must engage all eligible birthing hospitals, coordinate survey completion, analyze and report assessment findings, and ensure culturally responsive stakeholder and tribal engagement. The anticipated award per region is $50,000–$100,000 for Year 1, contingent on federal appropriations. Awards will be made via Trillium's standard Subaward Agreement, subject to all federal and state requirements, including compliance with 2 C.F.R. Part 200, data security, and reporting obligations. Multiple awards may be made based on quality, regional fit, and available funding.

data.title: MT - 2026 - Rural Health Care Workforce Retention Request for Information
data.issuingAgency: State of Montana, Department of Labor and Industry
data.summary: The State of Montana, State Procurement Bureau, on behalf of the Department of Labor and Industry, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to gather input and explore available programs supporting rural health care workforce retention. The focus is on identifying potential wellness and resilience programs designed to reduce provider isolation, prevent burnout, and improve behavioral health, with the ultimate goal of retaining medical and dental providers in rural Montana communities. This RFI is for information gathering only; no contract will result from the responses submitted.

data.title: FHC Transformation Technical Assistance Center (T-TAC) RFQ
data.issuingAgency: Foundation for Healthy Communities (FHC); Supported by Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS); Governor’s Office of New Opportunities for Rural Transformational Health (GO-NORTH)
data.summary: GO-NORTH implementation infrastructure: FHC seeks qualified respondents to establish a Transformation Technical Assistance Center (T-TAC) providing technical assistance to RHTP grantees from application through project completion. T-TAC delivers expert technical assistance and consulting support to New Hampshire rural health organizations as part of the GO-NORTH initiative, addressing eight Core Areas including population health, EMS transformation, health IT, cybersecurity, value-based care readiness, and rural hospital finance. Specialists provide needs assessments, direct consulting, peer group learning, and structured support—ensuring vendor-neutral, unbiased advice. Services are funded up to $4,000,000 for Budget Period 1 (BP1), with consultant selection via this RFQ for inclusion in a statewide roster. Awards are for BP1: contract execution through September 30, 2027. Selection does not guarantee minimum contract value or work volume; engagement occurs via individual task orders authorized by FHC or subrecipient.

data.title: Foundation for Healthy Communities RFP - Data Collection and Reporting Consulting Services
data.issuingAgency: Foundation for Healthy Communities (FHC)
data.summary: FHC seeks a data collection and reporting consultant to support the GO-NORTH Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) in New Hampshire. The selected consulting partner will design and implement a statewide data collection and reporting system for over 50 to 100 rural health subrecipients including primary care providers, critical access hospitals, EMS, behavioral and oral health, and community-based organizations, in alignment with CMS/HHS requirements. Core responsibilities include developing comprehensive program reporting frameworks, integrating with FHC's technology platforms (Blackbaud Grantmaking, Blackbaud Financial Edge NXT, Monday.com, Microsoft Power BI), facilitating data governance and privacy compliance (2 CFR Part 200), managing technical assistance for subrecipients, and coordinating with the external program evaluator (NORC). The consultant will develop dashboards and analytics, support longitudinal tracking, and produce key investment-area reports. The initial contract runs through September 30, 2027, with annual multi-year renewals possible through September 30, 2031, subject to funding and performance.

data.title: Virginia RHTP: Provider Interoperability — Where Connection Meets Care
data.issuingAgency: Virginia Health Care Foundation (VHCF)
data.summary: The Virginia Health Care Foundation's Provider Interoperability RFA, part of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) CareIQ initiative and funded by CMS, offers approximately $14 million for rural Virginia health care providers to modernize digital health care infrastructure. Projects must address one or more critical gaps identified in technology needs assessments: deficiencies in network capacity, certified EHR adoption (in line with ONC/ASTP and CMS Health Technology Ecosystem criteria), cybersecurity readiness, and electronic health data exchange capabilities. Allowable uses of funds include implementation-ready investments in certified EHRs, network upgrades, cybersecurity enhancements, and data exchange consistent with federal standards and milestones. Applicants must be able to commence implementation immediately upon award, demonstrating completed technology planning, organizational commitment, identified key personnel, and formalized partner roles if relevant. The program is milestone-driven; applicants must track performance metrics, submit rigorous financial and programmatic reporting to VHCF/DMAS/CMS, and show sustainability plans for benefit continuation beyond the grant period. Award size depends on project scope. Applicants must adhere to federal (including 2 CFR Part 200), state, and program terms, maintain active SAM.gov registration, and provide comprehensive documentation. Reporting requirements include monthly financial reports, quarterly progress reports, and final evaluation data.

data.title: CalRHT Workforce Development Recruitment and Retention Program (WDRR)
data.issuingAgency: California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI)
data.summary: HCAI's CalRHT Workforce Development Recruitment and Retention Program (WDRR) funds eligible rural California organizations—including rural hospitals, clinics, Tribal health entities, and regional collaboratives—to recruit or relocate, and to retain, primary care and maternal health professionals at HRSA-qualifying rural sites. $54,170,000 WDRR Pool for Grant Year 2026. Recruitment and retention bonuses are capped at $150,000 per Health Professional; total award amounts are capped at $1,000,000 per individual facility or $2,000,000 per consortium/collaborative/system. Awards support a five-year rural service commitment for each Health Professional. Bonuses support recruitment, retention, clinical training, faculty/preceptor capacity, shared regional staffing pools, regional coordination, and Tribal health program efforts. Applicants must meet all organizational eligibility requirements and submit comprehensive application documentation. This is the 4th of California's four currently-open CalRHT Budget Period 1 programs, alongside the already-tracked Accelerator Partners RFA, FM-OB Fellowship Subaward Program, and EHR Modernization Grant Program.

data.title: Nebraska RHTP Initiative 5.3: Modification of Existing Clinical Facilities for Mental Health Crisis
data.issuingAgency: Nebraska DHHS Division of Behavioral Health
data.summary: This opportunity provides up to $5,500,000 in federal RHTP funds to support equipment purchases and minor facility renovations aimed at expanding mental health crisis response, stabilization, and substance use withdrawal services in rural Nebraska hospitals and behavioral health facilities. Funding supports minor alterations and renovations to existing spaces, to increase capacity for crisis stabilization, withdrawal management, social detoxification, and crisis response—through equipment, ADA improvements, security and safety upgrades, EMR enhancements, and mobile crisis response vehicles. Only rural entities meeting specific eligibility criteria may apply.

data.title: Healthy Hometowns: High-Risk OB and Neonatal Transport Request For Proposal
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Public Health
data.summary: This RFP invites applications from eligible organizations to establish or expand High-Risk OB and Neonatal Transport programs in rural Iowa, as part of the Healthy Hometowns initiative under the federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The funded programs will enhance emergency transport capacity, training, telehealth integration, and networked connections between rural communities and specialty perinatal care centers. Up to approximately $6,000,000 is available in the first year, with total funding expected around $20M over the contract period for up to three awards.
applicantTypes: Public, private, nonprofit, academic, or governmental entities providing Emergency Medical Services Care

data.title: NC ROOTS — Trillium: Food is Medicine Program Expansion (Regions 2 & 5)
data.issuingAgency: Trillium Health Resources (NC ROOTS Hub Lead, Regions 2 & 5)
data.summary: Trillium Health Resources' NC ROOTS Initiative 2 (Food is Medicine Program Expansion), issued identically for both Region 2 and Region 5. The program is supported by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) as part of a financial assistance award totaling $213,008,356.47, fully funded by CMS/HHS. No funding/budget amount is stated for subawards in the source.

data.title: NC ROOTS — Trillium: I Gave Birth Implementation (Regions 2 & 5)
data.issuingAgency: Trillium Health Resources (NC ROOTS Hub Lead, Regions 2 & 5)
data.summary: Trillium Health Resources, as NC ROOTS Hub Lead for Regions 2 and 5 under the NC Rural Health Transformation Program (NCRHTP), is soliciting applications to implement the 'I Gave Birth' postpartum support program targeting maternal health improvement in rural and urban-rural counties. The initiative focuses on provider training, patient outreach, structured follow-up, stakeholder engagement, and strategies to reduce maternal health disparities through hospital and community partnerships. Successful applicants will collaborate with birthing facilities and NCDHHS, develop training curricula, collect program and enrollment data, engage NC tribal communities, and build sustainable programming in alignment with CMS-funded rural health goals. Awards anticipated at $50,000–$100,000 per region for GAP Year 1; reimbursement basis; activities subject to federal requirements under CMS and NC DHHS. Multiple or no awards possible.

data.title: New York RHTP Initiative 4 — Cybersecurity Resilience Interest Form
data.issuingAgency: New York State Department of Health (RHTP)
data.summary: Initiative 4 of New York's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) — Investments in Technology Innovation and Cybersecurity Resilience. The initiative guides rural hospitals through a cybersecurity assessment to identify gaps and inform future planning. Completing the cybersecurity resilience assessment is required for facilities seeking future RHTP cybersecurity-related funding consideration (future funding subject to CMS review/approval, program eligibility, availability, and NYSDOH guidance). Facilities interested in participating should complete the Cybersecurity Resilience Interest Form by August 31, 2026. The interest form confirms facility contact/interest/readiness and whether a recent assessment already exists — it is explicitly not the full assessment and will not include sensitive technical information, PHI, credentials, or detailed cybersecurity questions. The Year 1 phase is focused on rural hospitals; years 2-5 are planned to expand to pharmacies, nursing homes/long-term care, and school districts, subject to program guidance and funding availability. The assessment itself is estimated to run August–November 2026, with participation required to establish a baseline for next steps, access to future remediation support, and potential RHTP cybersecurity resources.

data.title: Nebraska RHTP 1.1: School Kitchen Modernization Grants
data.issuingAgency: Nebraska Department of Education (NDE)
data.summary: Nebraska Department of Education offers $2,234,048 in federal RHTP grants to rural and frontier school food authorities to modernize school kitchen infrastructure and equipment. Grants are available with no maximum individual award limit; equipment purchases must support increased scratch- and semi-scratch cooking, enhanced nutritional quality of meals, and greater use of minimally processed and locally produced protein. Schools/districts must document existing and proposed menus, provide at least three price quotes per equipment item (minimum $10,000 per item), and justify purchase choices. Projects funded should target at least a 5% monthly reduction in heat-and-serve menu items, a 5% increase in minimally processed/local protein menu offerings, and a 10% increase in student meal participation. Priority is for applicants in food deserts and high-poverty areas. No administrative or major construction costs are allowed. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through August 31, 2026, and all purchases must be completed by June 30, 2027. Funds are provided via reimbursement upon submission of procurement documentation. Post-award, recipients must submit final proof of purchase and updated menus by July 1, 2027.

data.title: PATH 1.1: Rural Food Infrastructure (Utah Food Security Grant Program)
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Agriculture and Food (UDAF)
data.summary: Part of Utah's RHTP PATH initiative (1.1), publicly branded the "Utah Food Security Grant Program." Strengthens Utah's rural food supply chain — agricultural production, processing, storage, cold storage, distribution, and food safety/market access ("farm to consumer"). Up to $9,265,098.80 total available via microgrants, startup awards, and standard awards up to $1,000,000 each. Eligible applicants must be Utah-headquartered with in-state project activity, produce food/beverages using at least 51% Utah-grown agricultural products for commercial sale, hold a UEI, and sell/distribute at least 25% of project output to rural Utah counties (outside Salt Lake, Davis, Utah, and Weber counties).
