Issued by the Utah Department of Agriculture and Food as part of the RHTP PATH initiative under Utah DHHS. Application window: July 21 – August 31, 2026. Estimated project start: October/November 2026.

data.title: Healthy Hometowns Communities of Care Co-Location Program (RFP COMPADM26005)
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: This Request for Proposal (RFP) aims to identify and fund qualified applicants to serve as pilot Communities of Care Co-Location Sites for the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The program establishes rural Co-Location Sites that integrate at least three separate and distinct service delivery entities (including the Site Lead), each providing different types of initiatives or services under one roof. The goal is to expand and sustain access to health and health-related social services; foster new partnerships among local providers; improve outcomes for chronic diseases; and embed preventive and chronic disease management services—such as Community Health Workers (CHWs) for enhanced care coordination—within rural communities. The pilot is part of the Healthy Hometowns Rural Health Transformation Program, financially supported by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) as part of a five-year, $209,040,063.71 federal award under opportunity #: CMS-RHT-26-001. For the initial contract year, a total of approximately $39,558,631 will be available, with an anticipated contract term total of $168,234,514. Awardees must connect with Iowa’s Health Information Exchange and adhere to federal and state eligibility, documentation, and reporting requirements. All activities and funding are subject to CMS approval of the Agency’s year 2 budget, and HHS reserves the right to modify the number and amounts of awards based on need, quality of applications, and geographic distribution.
applicantTypes: Public, private, nonprofit, for-profit, academic institutions, or governmental entities providing health or health-related social needs

data.title: Iowa Maternal Health Hub and Spoke Networks (RFP COMPADM26006)
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The Healthy Hometowns: Maternal Health Hub and Spoke Program (RFP #COMPADM26006) solicits applications to increase and sustain access to high-quality prenatal, labor and delivery, postpartum, mental health, and behavioral health services for pregnant and postpartum individuals in rural Iowa. Applicants may apply under one of three options: (1) Serve as a statewide Hub (Iowa Level III or IV Maternal Care Hospital); (2) Expand an existing Level I hospital’s capacity to Level II and serve as a regional Hub; (3) Establish and coordinate networks of rural Level I or II hospitals as Spoke sites (each network including 3–5 eligible members meeting proximity and referral standards). Awardees must have been open and providing qualifying maternal health services in Iowa since or before January 1, 2026, and remain so through application. Legally executed collaboration/network agreements are required with submission. Projects should propose collaborative, sustainable models—such as telehealth and multi-organizational rural partnerships—to build and maintain local maternal care. This procurement is 100% funded by CMS/HHS under the Rural Health Transformation Program (CMS-RHT-26-001) as part of Iowa's Hometown Connections Initiative, with up to $209,040,063.71 available through September 30, 2031. First-year anticipated funding is $38,591,059, with annual renewals and possible amendments subject to CMS/HHS approval and Agency discretion. Performance of grantees/subcontractors is subject to annual review by the Agency, compliance checks, and availability of funds.

data.title: Rural Ohio Clinically Integrated Networks and Rural Health Innovation Hubs
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health - Center of Public Health Excellence (CPHE)
data.summary: Solicitation for subrecipients to coordinate, develop, or expand rural clinically integrated networks and rural health innovation hubs in Ohio's 73 rural counties, focusing on expanding access to maternal care and establishing sustainable healthcare collaborations under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The total estimated available budget is up to $61.7 million with preference for projects increasing access to maternal care and for rural-based applicants.

data.title: Healthy Hometowns: Mobile Integrated Health (RFP # PHTHOET27001)
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services - Division of Public Health
data.summary: The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services, through RFP #PHTHOET27001, seeks applications to initiate or expand Mobile Integrated Health (MIH) services within rural Iowa. The program supports EMS agencies or community-based clinical providers in launching or broadening treat-in-place care, telehealth-enabled assessments, chronic disease management, post-discharge follow-up, prenatal and postpartum home-based support, medication reconciliation, and other in-home interventions. Applicants may propose to initiate a new MIH program or expand an existing MIH program to additional rural counties. The goal is to improve health outcomes for rural Iowans, reduce avoidable emergency department and inpatient utilization, and strengthen care capacity through coordinated, community-based services. This federally funded initiative, part of the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program (CMS-RHT-26-001), prioritizes projects that cover multiple rural counties and leverage telehealth and care coordination tools.

data.title: ToRCH Care Smart Growth and Service Line Modification (Horizon 2) Invitation For Bid
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Department of Social Services
data.summary: Missouri DSS solicits bids under the federally approved Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) for the ToRCH Care Smart Growth and Service Line Modification (Horizon 2) initiative. Horizon 2 funds eligible rural hospitals and health centers to modernize, renovate, reconfigure, equip, or adapt existing healthcare facilities and access-to-care settings, aimed at expanding or sustaining priority service lines: (1) maternal health (obstetric, perinatal, prenatal, postpartum, and women's health services); (2) behavioral health (inpatient, outpatient, crisis, tele-behavioral health, and integrated behavioral health); and (3) diagnostics/outpatient/chronic disease management (imaging, laboratory services, specialty consults, care coordination). Projects must address documented rural access gaps, demonstrate long-term sustainability, and positively impact service access beyond individual facilities, with a strategic focus on reducing avoidable travel and utilization burdens and strengthening rural health provider sustainability. All funded activities must align with Horizon 2 priorities, complement other rural system transformation efforts, and adhere to federal (CMS/HHS) and state requirements. New construction, major expansion beyond existing footprints, routine administrative, or non-project operations costs are not eligible. Funding subject to compliance with all applicable requirements and final CMS approval.

data.title: SHIFT 3.4 New Models of Care RFGA
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: A formal, competitive grant funding opportunity for rural health providers and eligible border-state organizations to propose new, innovative care models in rural Utah. Projects may address mobile health services, patient transportation, chronic disease prevention/management, team-based integrated care, employer support, and other approaches tailored to local rural needs. The program aims to strengthen rural health system capacity and sustainability, with up to $10M available in Year 1 and $45M total over five years. Up to 12 awards will be made, with up to 5 reserved for tribes or tribal organizations that meet full RFGA criteria.

data.title: SCC PACE
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA) RHT-AFA-08-20-2026-SCC under the Smart Care Catalyst pillar: The State of West Virginia, through the Rural Health Transformation Program, solicits applications to design, implement, and deliver PACE-aligned care model components for older adults with complex medical and functional needs who meet nursing home level of care. Applicants must prioritize expansion of adult medical daycare services in West Virginia counties where such services are limited or unavailable. Funded programs must demonstrate measurable improvements in care access, outcomes, and operational readiness within defined timeframes, rapid establishment and expansion of community-based care capacity, and a credible pathway to full PACE program readiness by Year 5. Awardees are required to align with State and CMS performance reporting, coordinate with Medicaid and community partners, and avoid duplication of existing reimbursed services. Total Year 1 funding of $1.25 million will be disbursed via milestone-based payments contingent on achievement of performance targets. Applications must be submitted through the WVOASIS Vendor Self Service portal by September 2, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. For technical and program questions, contact mike.sheets@wv.gov or gwyndolyn.m.mcgee@wv.gov.
applicantTypes: Other entities capable of operating PACE-aligned care models

data.title: Healthcare Management Consulting Services (RFP #34320-20827)
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The State of Tennessee, Department of Health, is issuing a solicitation for Healthcare Management Consulting Services under RFP #34320-20827. Prospective respondents must sign and submit a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) to obtain access to the detailed solicitation package including statement of work, contract requirements, and evaluation criteria. Vendor registration with the State of Tennessee is required prior to submission and typically takes 10–14 days. The opportunity is coordinated by the Central Procurement Office and responses are due by Thursday, September 3, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Central Time.

data.title: Washington RHTP Activity 1.4: Sustain and strengthen maternal, emergency, and specialty services at risk in rural areas
data.issuingAgency: Washington State Health Care Authority
data.summary: Activity 1.4: Sustain and strengthen maternal, emergency, and specialty services at risk in rural areas We plan to use $9.5 million per year of RHT funding to incentivize hospitals to develop comprehensive strategies to sustain essential services. Prioritized services include: Maternity and obstetrics care Emergency services Other specialty care Example : A hospital may request funds to develop remote monitoring for low-risk pregnancies, paired with capacity payments for midwives and birth centers located in rural areas. RHT funds would support start-up and implementation costs for hospitals, but applications will require a long-term sustainability plan. Learn more in Washington’s RHT Project Narrative .

data.title: Building a Sustainable Rural Healthcare Workforce: Recruit & Retention
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota eSM Solutions Posting Board
data.summary: This RFP, issued under South Dakota’s Rural Health Transformation initiative, seeks proposals from qualified healthcare organizations, facilities, and other eligible entities to implement innovative, coordinated, and outcomes-driven strategies to recruit, deploy, and retain a sustainable rural healthcare workforce across rural, underserved, and frontier communities in South Dakota. The purpose is to address workforce shortages, high turnover, maldistribution, and overreliance on temporary staffing by funding comprehensive models that: accelerate recruitment with targeted incentives; improve retention and stability through structured support and engagement; optimize workforce distribution for equitable care access; reduce dependency on short-term staffing; enhance provider experience; and establish sustainable staffing infrastructure. Proposals should align with the statewide Rural Health Transformation Project and incorporate recommendations from South Dakota’s Strategic Analysis of Rural Healthcare Programs, 2024. Funding must not duplicate existing efforts or other RHT funding and priority will be given to proposals demonstrating strong potential for long-term impact, sustainability, and collaborative partnership across the state.

1.1.1       Background:

The South Dakota Rural Health Data Atlas is a state-led initiative to transform how rural communities access and use health data. Today, critical health data is siloed across numerous systems, requiring communities, hospitals, Tribal Nations, and state agencies to navigate multiple systems and request processes to obtain a complete picture of local health. This fragmentation limits data-driven planning and slows response to emerging chronic disease concerns. To address these challenges, the South Dakota Department of Health (SD DOH) is developing a publicly-accessible, cloud-based platform that consolidates health data into a single, interactive environment. The Rural Health Data Atlas will integrate datasets from South Dakota’s health agencies and other publicly available sources into an intuitive platform featuring maps, charts, tables, and point-and-click analysis tools.

 

The result will be a centralized, state owned Microsoft Azure tenant cloud-based data visualization and distribution platform designed to modernize sharing and exploration of health data. The platform will integrate diverse datasets into a secure, user-friendly environment that supports advances visualizations, role-based access control, real-time ingestion, and accessibility compliance.

 1.1.2    

Goals and Objectives:

The Rural Health Data Atlas will enable access to health data and support data-driven decision-making, including serving as a point of dissemination of Rural Health Transformation outcome measures. The platform will empower:

·            Hospitals to analyze local health trends, justify funding requests, and inform service delivery.

·            Community coalitions to identify service gaps, plan interventions, and measure short- and long-term impact.

·            State agencies to target resources toward preventable health issues and support coordinated public health action.

·            Rural health clinics to strengthen value-based care, risk stratification, and proactive patient management and outreach.

·            Tribal nations to design data-informed programs addressing local health outcomes.

·            Academica and Research Organizations to easily access state data to perform analysis that will empower public health policies and initiatives.

The Rural Health Data Atlas will integrate datasets from South Dakota’s health agencies and other publicly available sources into an intuitive platform featuring maps, charts, tables, and point-and-click analysis tools.   The result will be a centralized, state owned Microsoft Azure tenant cloud-based data visualization and distribution platform designed to modernize sharing and exploration of health data. The platform will integrate diverse datasets into a secure, user-friendly environment that supports advances visualizations, role-based access control, real-time ingestion, and accessibility compliance.   1.1.2      Goals and Objectives : The Rural Health Data Atlas will enable access to health data and support data-driven decision-making, including serving as a point of dissemination of Rural Health Transformation outcome measures. The platform will empower: ·             Hospitals to analyze local health trends, justify funding requests, and inform service delivery. ·             Community coalitions to identify service gaps, plan interventions, and measure short- and long-term impact. ·             State agencies to target resources toward preventable health issues and support coordinated public health action. ·             Rural health clinics to strengthen value-based care, risk stratification, and proactive patient management and outreach. ·             Tribal nations to design data-informed programs addressing local health outcomes. ·             Academica and Research Organizations to easily access state data to perform analysis that will empower public health policies and initiatives .   All written questions should be sent to:   doh.datamodernization@state.sd.us only emailed questions will be accepted.   Each offeror may submit questions via email concerning this RFP to obtain clarification of requirements. No questions will be accepted after the date and time indicated in the above schedule of activities. Email questions to the email address listed above with the subject line “RFP# 26-09RHT-021 ”. The questions and their answers will be sent to all offerors that submitted Letters of Intent, submitted questions, or requested the questions and answers via email before the proposal submittal date and will be sent by the date and time indicated in the above calendar of events. Offeror may not rely on any other statements, either of a written or oral nature, that alter any specification or other term or condition of this RFP that have not originated from the SD RFP Project Contact. Offerors will be notified in the same manner as indicated above regarding any modifications to this RFP. Offerors and their agents may not contact any state employee other than the buyer of record regarding any of these matters during the solicitation and evaluation process. Inappropriate contacts are grounds for suspension and exclusion from specific procurements. [object Object] Response to Offeror Questions document.docx Updated RFP Document _august 24.pdf

data.title: Rooted in New Mexico (RiNM) RFP — Rural Health Workforce
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Health Care Authority
data.summary: The New Mexico Health Care Authority is accepting proposals for Rooted in New Mexico as part of its federally funded Rural Health Transformation Program. This initiative is focused on improving rural health systems by strengthening the workforce, expanding access to care, supporting long-term sustainability, and funding innovative projects for rural, frontier, and Tribal communities. Proposals should build workforce pathways, strengthen rural training and clinical education, and improve recruitment and retention of health professionals. Annual funding is tied to performance, with the goal to engage providers, communities, and regional infrastructure throughout New Mexico.

data.title: RHL-VASO
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: Grant Funding Opportunity GFO-0506-2700000000079-1 (RHT-AFA-08-21-2026-RHL-VASO) under the Rural Health Link pillar: Expand Local Mobility Options – Vehicle Acquisition and Service Operations. This Announcement for Funding Availability (AFA)/Grant is designed to enhance rural health mobility in West Virginia. Applications are sought to expand and strengthen transportation services for rural non-emergency medical transport (NEMT) by investing in fleet acquisition, operational launch, and measurable service improvement. Grantees will deploy vehicles, expand service hours, and integrate with regional dispatch systems to improve access to care, reduce missed appointments, and enhance reliability across rural communities. Applications must be submitted through the wvOASIS Vendor Self Service portal; successful applications will advance transportation options for rural health in partnership with the RHTP. Comprehensive requirements and milestone-based payment instructions are detailed in the solicitation package and related guidance.

data.title: Idaho RHTP Chronic Disease Prevention and Cancer Screenings
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (RHTP)
data.summary: Solicitation No. RHTPDIS1 (Federal Award No. RHTCMS332084, ALN 93.798), addressing RHTP Initiative 4. Total available funding $2,000,000, anticipated 1-2 awards, award range $1,000,000-$2,000,000. Eligible applicants: state/local government agencies, tribal organizations, 501(c)(3) nonprofits, Idaho institutions of higher education, healthcare associations/professional societies, Idaho hospitals/health systems, FQHCs, organizations with statewide clinical-education/workforce-development experience. No cost share/match required. Lead Entities will implement evidence-based chronic disease prevention and cancer screening initiatives for rural/frontier Idaho, including work plans, technology dashboards, community events, and regular reporting. Administrative and indirect cost limit: 10% of total approved budget, on MTDC base. Full detailed, line-item budget and justification required per 2 CFR 200 Subpart E. Subgrantees may serve as pass-throughs for local partners.
applicantTypes: Organizations with statewide clinical education or workforce development experience

data.title: Ohio RHTP: Healthier Ohio Community-Level Chronic Disease Prevention and Management (RO27)
data.issuingAgency: Ohio Department of Health, Center for Public Health Excellence
data.summary: The Ohio Department of Health (ODH), Center for Public Health Excellence, under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), announces competitive grant funding up to $7,000,000 to improve community-level prevention and management of chronic diseases (diabetes, hypertension, overweight, and obesity) in 73 non-urban Ohio counties. This funding fosters innovative, evidence-based, community-driven behavioral health strategies targeting wellness related behaviors including optimal nutrition, physical activity, restorative sleep, stress management, social connectedness, and reducing risky behaviors. Applicants must implement collective impact models with shared agendas and measures, collaborate with diverse partners and health systems, and demonstrate sustainable impact. Minimum award is $100,000. Applications must comply with ODH policies, OGAPP, and federal regulations.

data.title: Idaho RHTP School-Based Family Support Hubs (SBFSHs)
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (RHTP)
data.summary: Solicitation No. RHTPSBFSH (Federal Award No. RHTCMS332084, ALN 93.798). Total available funding: Six Million Dollars ($6,000,000.00) over five (5) years — a total program pool, not a single-year figure. Anticipated up to 15 subawards, award range $80,000-$120,000 ANNUALLY per site (depending on number of applicants awarded). Eligible applicants (schools, not health organizations): county/local/state school districts (independent or public) and schools on tribal land in Idaho, county/local/state charter school districts. Must meet RHTP rural definition and be Idaho-based. No cost share/match required.

data.title: West Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program – Personal Health Accelerator: Increasing Home Dialysis Access (Year 1 Funding)
data.issuingAgency: West Virginia Department of Health
data.summary: This opportunity will fund the development and scaling of a Home Dialysis Access Program to expand access for rural West Virginians with advanced kidney disease. The program seeks sustainable, scalable models that address non-reimbursable barriers for home dialysis, improve early identification and navigation pathways for CKD/ESRD patients, and coordinate with providers, community partners, and caregivers. Activities must not duplicate or supplant existing payer-funded or mandated services, and must support state data integration requirements. Grantees are expected to demonstrate measurable progress in home dialysis initiation and continuation, resolve documented nonclinical barriers, and establish operational and financial sustainability beyond year one. Milestone-based funding structure is used, and a broad range of public or private healthcare and community-based organizations are eligible. Award may go to one or more applicants, not to exceed a combined $2,000,000 pool for 2026-2027.
applicantTypes: Other organizations supporting access to home-based care, chronic disease management, caregiver support, or community-based service delivery

data.title: RHL ERH Establish Regional Hubs
data.issuingAgency: DIVISION OF HEALTH Rural Health Tansformation Program
data.summary: This Announcement of Funding Availability (AFA) invites qualified organizations to design, implement, and operate integrated regional hubs and mobility coordinator models that address transportation and care navigation barriers for rural West Virginians. The program emphasizes measurable improvements in access, utilization, and coordination, prioritizing milestones, data integration, and long-term sustainability. Up to $7.1 million is available in shared funding for eligible public or private entities with demonstrated experience in coordination programs. Funded activities must align with CMS-approved Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) objectives, reducing chronic disease burden, increasing workforce participation, and improving measurable healthcare outcomes in rural communities. The initiative supports operational scalability, real-time data integration, and post-award sustainability, awarding funds based on performance measures and milestone-based deliverables. All data generated through this program must be accessible to the State. Applicants must present credible measurement and reporting plans and ensure no duplication of scope with existing mandated programs. The grant period ends September 30, 2027, with funding based on State-approved milestones, and does not require cost sharing. Applications are evaluated on completeness, alignment with RHTP goals, budget justification, organizational capacity, rural community partnerships, service area impact, and compliance.
applicantTypes: Other Organizations Supporting Statewide or Regional Coordination

data.title: Idaho Cognitive Health Workforce Response Network
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (RHTP)
data.summary: Solicitation No. RHTPCOG2 (Federal Award No. RHTCMS332084, ALN 93.798). Workforce training program expanding provider/care-team/community-professional knowledge of ADOD, cognitive decline, dementia-capable care, caregiver engagement, and referral pathways. Total available funding $2,000,000, anticipated 1-2 awards, award range $500,000-$2,000,000. Eligible applicants: Idaho 501(c)(3) nonprofits, state/local government agencies, tribal organizations/tribal health programs, Idaho hospitals/health systems, rural Idaho healthcare providers, FQHCs/Look-Alikes, Idaho institutions of higher education, Idaho local public health districts, healthcare/provider associations, organizations with statewide workforce-development/dementia/care-coordination experience, multi-org partnerships with qualifying lead. No cost share/match required.

data.title: Idaho Cognitive Care Pathway Network
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (RHTP)
data.summary: Solicitation No. RHTPCOG1 (Federal Award No. RHTCMS332084, ALN 93.798). Addresses early identification of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias (ADOD) in rural Idaho, face-to-face or telehealth delivery. Total available funding $2,000,000.00, anticipated 1-2 awards, award range $500,000-$2,000,000. Eligible applicants: Idaho local public health districts, 501(c)(3) nonprofits, state/local government agencies, healthcare providers serving rural Idahoans, FQHCs/FQHC Look-Alikes, Idaho institutions of higher education, Idaho hospitals/health systems, Area Agencies on Aging/caregiver-service organizations, organizations with statewide aging/dementia/chronic-disease/care-coordination experience, tribal organizations, multi-org partnerships with a qualifying lead applicant. No cost share/match required.
applicantTypes: Statewide Organizations (aging, dementia, chronic disease, care coordination)

data.title: Idaho RHTP Diabetes Prevention and Management
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (RHTP)
data.summary: Solicitation No. RHTPDIA1 (Federal Award No. RHTCMS332084, ALN 93.798). The Idaho Department of Health and Welfare seeks up to two Lead Entities to establish, administer, and oversee a statewide Diabetes Prevention and Self-Management Network under the Rural Health Transformation Program, targeting rural, frontier, and underserved communities in Idaho. Up to $2,000,000 in federal funding is available ($1,000,000–$2,000,000 per award), with a period of performance from 09/30/2026 to 09/30/2027. Awardees will serve as pass-through organizations issuing and managing subgrants to local partners delivering National Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) and Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES) services across Idaho. Eligible applicants include Idaho-based health systems, healthcare organizations, public health districts, universities/academic institutions, nonprofits, community-based organizations, professional associations, pharmacy organizations/networks, tribal organizations, and other qualified public or private entities with a minimum of two years' experience managing federal or state-funded health programs. Applicants must have an active SAM.gov registration and UEI, and be free of exclusions. There is no cost share or matching required. Indirect and administrative costs are capped at 10% of the total approved budget (calculated on MTDC). A detailed line-item budget and justification are required. Applications must be submitted to IdahoRHTP@dhw.idaho.gov; late submissions will not be reviewed.
applicantTypes: Other qualified public or private Idaho-based organizations

data.title: Nevada Statewide Health Care Access and Recruitment Program (SHARP) - Grant Cycle 1 (SFY27)
data.issuingAgency: Nevada Health Authority (NVHA)
data.summary: Competitive Nevada Health Authority grant cycle under the Statewide Health Care Access and Recruitment Program (SHARP) created by Senate Bill 5 of the 2025 Special Session. The SFY27 Grant Cycle 1 RFA supports projects that address Nevada health care workforce shortages, service gaps, and access barriers identified in the Nevada Health Workforce Needs Assessment for 2026. Funding is intended for sustainable workforce capacity, infrastructure expansion, and regional access projects that do not duplicate RHTP-funded investments.
applicantTypes: Behavioral health and substance use entities

data.title: Minnesota State Loan Repayment Program
