data.summary: RFP for the Minnesota State Loan Repayment Program supporting eligible individual applicants under Minnesota rural health funding outreach.

data.title: Rural Health Transformation Program Grantee Marketing and Messaging Technical Assistance Services (RFP #34320-21327)
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The State of Tennessee, Department of Health, is issuing a solicitation to bid for a new twelve (12) month contract to provide Rural Health Transformation Program grantee marketing and messaging technical assistance services, under Solicitation ID 34320-21327. This solicitation has been identified by the Department of Finance and Administration, Strategic Technology Solutions, as containing information confidential under Tenn. Code Ann. section 10-7-504(i) -- prospective respondents must sign a non-disclosure agreement before the substantive solicitation details (scope of work, budget, evaluation criteria) may be disclosed by the State. Vendor registration with the State of Tennessee is required prior to submission and typically takes 10-14 days. Coordinated by the Central Procurement Office; responses due September 10, 2026.

data.title: OSDE PRIMS Project 695: Promoting School Health Services Through Medicaid Billing
data.issuingAgency: Oklahoma State Department of Education
data.summary: Personnel Recruitment for Implementing Medicaid Services (PRIMS) Project 695, issued by the Oklahoma State Department of Education, School Health Services program. This initiative supports rural Oklahoma PK-12 school districts (all except Oklahoma and Tulsa counties) by funding the recruitment and hiring of new credentialed health/mental health staff able to deliver and bill Medicaid-reimbursable services. Eligible positions include school nurses, licensed counselors, speech-language pathologists, physical therapists, and occupational therapists. The grant covers up to 90% of new hire salary/benefits, contingent on Medicaid-billing eligibility, and allows purchase of supplies to set up health offices for the new personnel; funds are not allowed for existing staff. Supported districts receive at-no-cost access to EdPlan Health, a statewide electronic health record system, as well as training and technical assistance. Districts are responsible for ensuring implementation, documentation, and compliance. All funded districts are automatically renewed for the next fiscal year, with renewal priority for those with active, credentialed personnel. Applications must be submitted via the Oklahoma Grants Management System (GMS), under Competitive, between July 9 and September 11, 2026.

data.title: Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO): RHTP SHIFT Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Emergency Medical Services (BEMS)
data.summary: The Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) - SHIFT Initiative (Sustaining Health Infrastructure for Transformation), administered by the Utah Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Emergency Medical Services (BEMS) with support from Utah Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) under a CMS-funded award, will provide $12,500,000 in Year 1 with an estimated $10,000,000 annually for Years 2-5 to sustain and strengthen rural and Tribal EMS infrastructure in Utah. The competitive, multi-year program funds projects that expand EMS access, modernize health communications, and build sustainable EMS capacity by supporting education and workforce development, community paramedicine and telehealth, innovation and technology, and operational/administrative support. Eligible projects must align with at least one of four program areas: Education (including workforce development and training), Community Paramedicine and Telehealth, Innovation and Technology, or Administrative Support. The SHIFT Initiative prioritizes solutions that improve rural EMS service, enhance communication, and foster long-term, sustainable improvements in rural and Tribal communities. Applications are evaluated primarily for Years 1–2. Subgrants are annual, with project periods defined per funding year, and strict budget and use restrictions apply.

data.title: Idaho RHTP Healthcare Infrastructure Support (HIS)
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (RHTP)
data.summary: The Idaho RHTP Healthcare Infrastructure Support (HIS) subaward program provides up to $97,213,653 in funding to rural health providers, clinics, facilities, tribal organizations, and related entities in Idaho's rural and frontier areas to address critical infrastructure, access, IT, workforce, and quality gaps in healthcare. Supported by CMS, eligible activities include technology upgrades, EHR integration or replacement (subject to specific limitations), equipment purchases, cybersecurity updates, minor renovations and alterations (but not new construction or major retrofits), procurement or retrofitting of vehicles for mobile health and patient transport, and practice transformation initiatives. No cost share or match is required. Applications undergo a two-stage process involving assessment of community needs and project impact. Major priorities include telehealth, EHR or digital health upgrades, chronic and behavioral health, maternal/child health, mobile healthcare, and facility safety/readiness. Reporting, collaboration, and compliance with federal grant requirements (2 CFR 200) are required.
applicantTypes: Public health agencies serving rural Idaho

data.title: Provider Productivity: Technology that Makes Time for Care (RFA-RHTP-2026-02)
data.issuingAgency: Virginia Health Care Foundation (VHCF) / Virginia RHTP
data.summary: This RFA supports rural Virginia health care organizations in adopting or expanding digital productivity tools—including decision support, documentation, and workflow automation (including AI solutions)—to return provider time to care, reduce burnout, and strengthen operational sustainability. Successful applicants will implement or expand proven technologies that reduce administrative burden, document measurable improvements in provider time savings, and support workforce retention. Funded projects must track and report metrics including adoption rates, time savings, impact on revenue/billable services, and reduction in clinician burnout. VHCF will provide technical assistance and expects awardees to participate in program evaluation and reporting. Projects must serve FORHP-designated rural Virginia communities, with partnerships documented by formal letters/MOUs where applicable.

data.title: Request for Proposals: Needs Assessment and Design Proposal for a Potential Rural Telehealth Services Center (RTSC) in Minnesota
data.issuingAgency: Minnesota Department of Health
data.summary: The Minnesota Department of Health, through the federally funded Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), seeks qualified vendors to conduct a comprehensive needs assessment and develop a design proposal for a potential Rural Telehealth Services Center (RTSC) or alternative telehealth models in Minnesota. The initiative aims to address gaps and fragmentation affecting rural healthcare providers, emergency medical services, and communities, with a focus on better linkages among providers and patients. The assessment will identify service, technological, regulatory, and workforce barriers, followed by a design proposal outlining options for a Minnesota-based RTSC or alternative solutions that coordinate and support regional telehealth needs. Deliverables include a detailed project work plan, project management with regular progress check-ins, an interim needs assessment at six months, a final report, and a summary presentation of findings and recommendations. Preference is given to vendors with substantial experience in rural healthcare needs assessment, coalition development, and Minnesota's telehealth landscape. The project is 100% funded by CMS/HHS under Minnesota’s RHTP award, with an anticipated contract period from September 2026 through September 2027, and possible extension for one year.

data.title: Virginia RHTP: Homegrown Health Heroes — Allied Health Degrees (VFCCE)
data.issuingAgency: Virginia Foundation for Community College Education (VFCCE), in partnership with Virginia Community College System (VCCS)
data.summary: RFA Reference Number RFA-RHTP-2026-02 (RFA #2), issued by the Virginia Foundation for Community College Education (VFCCE) in partnership with the Virginia Community College System (VCCS). VFCCE is a subrecipient of DMAS (Virginia's primary RHTP recipient) under Subrecipient Agreement #RHT26-003-VFCCE, with a Year 1 subaward of $5,934,931. $4.4 million is available under this RFA to expand enrollment capacity in six existing high-demand healthcare degree programs at rural-serving VCCS community colleges (18 institutions within the Rural Virginia Horseshoe). Funded activity types include hub-and-spoke instructional partnerships, dual-funded instructor positions shared with hospital partners, a shared mobile training lab, stand-alone equipment, technology upgrades for synchronous distance learning, and rural recruitment. All funded expansions must result in additional students enrolled by Fall 2027. The initiative aims to add approximately 1,200 health graduates by 2031. Award range: $50,000–$2,500,000 per award. No cost share or match required. Colleges must partner with hospitals or health systems and propose expansion in one or more of six eligible programs: Behavioral Health, Dental Hygiene, Diagnostic Medical Sonography, Nursing, Physical Therapy Assistant, Radiology Technology.
applicantTypes: Virginia Community College System member colleges

data.title: Virginia RHTP: CareIQ Remote Patient Monitoring Initiative
data.issuingAgency: Virginia Hospital Research and Education Foundation d/b/a Virginia Hospital & Healthcare Association Foundation (VHHAF)
data.summary: The Virginia Hospital & Healthcare Association Foundation (VHHAF) invites applications for the CareIQ Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) Initiative under Virginia’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), supported by CMS/HHS. This RFA seeks licensed hospitals, health systems, or academic medical centers to design, implement, or expand hospital-based RPM programs serving rural communities, as defined by the Federal Office of Rural Health Policy (FORHP). The initiative targets technology-enabled chronic disease management and post-acute follow-up, aiming to reduce avoidable hospitalizations and readmissions, strengthen care coordination, and improve patient engagement and outcomes through RPM devices, EHR integration, and clinical workflow redesign. $14.3 million is available for Budget Period 1 (10/30/2026–9/30/2027), with 2–3 awards anticipated; subsequent funding may be available for up to four additional years based on demonstrated measurable outcomes. No cost sharing or match is required. Applicants must provide detailed implementation plans, sustainability plans, and comply with federal subrecipient, reporting, and risk assessment requirements.

data.title: Idaho RHTP Statewide Chronic Disease Education Network
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (RHTP)
data.summary: This competitive funding solicitation from Idaho's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) targets rural and frontier populations and healthcare workforce, with a focus on chronic disease prevention and management. The aim is to establish a Statewide Chronic Disease Education Network that expands workforce education, improves access to evidence-based clinical practices, and addresses priority chronic diseases including cardiovascular disease, stroke, diabetes, cancer, Alzheimer's disease, obesity, neurodevelopmental and mental health conditions, and immune-related conditions. The anticipated single award totals $2,000,000, with a project period through 2031. Required activities include education, technical assistance, partnership development, and data-driven evaluation. Applicants must demonstrate federal grant compliance, capacity to administer statewide networks, and strategies to reach Idaho's rural communities through partnerships, subawards, learning collaboratives, and virtual platforms. Administrative and indirect costs are capped at 10% of the budget as required by CMS.
applicantTypes: Other organizations capable of administering a statewide education network

data.title: Virginia RHTP: Homegrown Health Heroes — Attract & Retain Physicians (GME)
data.issuingAgency: Virginia Hospital Research and Education Foundation d/b/a Virginia Hospital & Healthcare Association Foundation (VHHAF)
data.summary: This RFA, as part of Virginia’s Rural Health Transformation Program—Homegrown Health Heroes initiative, provides substantial support for expanding or creating rural physician residency programs in high-need specialties via hospitals and health systems serving rural Virginia. Under the 'Attract & Retain Physicians' sub-initiative, up to $200,000 per resident slot is available (estimated 47 awards in Budget Period 1: 10/30/2026–9/30/2027). Funds support both capacity expansion (Tier 1) and new program creation (Tier 2) for eligible specialties including primary care (family/internal medicine), OB/GYN, psychiatry, general surgery, pediatrics, nurse midwifery, and other locally justified specialties. Funded residents must commit to a five-year rural service obligation (including residency), bolstering the workforce pipeline and sustainable rural care access. All awards are cost-reimbursable with a 4% cap on administrative expenses and no matching/cost-share requirement. Applicants must be licensed hospitals/health systems in or serving eligible rural Virginia localities, maintain active SAM.gov/UEI, demonstrate federal fund management capacity, and hold or obtain ACGME accreditation as required per tier. Preference is given for recruiting/retaining trainees from rural Virginia. See RFA-RHTP-GME-1 for full details, eligibility, documentation, requirements, required milestones, and funding structure.

data.title: Idaho RHTP Healthcare Career Advancement (RHTPWBLCA1)
data.issuingAgency: Idaho State Board of Education (in partnership with Idaho DHW RHTP)
data.summary: Solicitation No. RHTPWBLCA1 (Federal Award No. RHTCMS332084, ALN 93.798). Total available funding: $12.52 million, anticipated 10 awards, award range $200,000–$4,500,000 per subaward. Supports Initiative 3 (Sustaining Rural Workforce) of Idaho's RHTP plan — Healthcare Career Exploration/Advancement and Work-Based Learning/Clinical Training components. No cost share/match required. Indirect + admin costs capped at 10% of total approved subaward budget.

data.title: Solicitation for Substance Use Prevention (RHTP)
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
data.summary: The Idaho Department of Health and Welfare, through its Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) and with funding from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), invites eligible organizations to apply for subgrants supporting the implementation of evidence-based behavioral health and substance misuse prevention programs focused on parent, family, and home-visit interventions in previously unserved rural communities across Idaho. Successful projects will align with the RHTP strategic plan, strengthen family-focused prevention capacity, expand access for youth, adults, and families in rural counties, and build local rural prevention infrastructure. Recipients must address all solicitation objectives, support federal compliance requirements (2 CFR Part 200), and participate in mandatory training and evaluation. Up to four awards are anticipated, with subgrant funding ranging from $100,000 to $400,000.

data.title: Idaho Rural Health Transformation Program – Behavioral Health Prevention Programs Grant
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
data.summary: This solicitation seeks applications from eligible organizations to implement evidence-based behavioral health prevention programs throughout rural and underserved communities in Idaho. Projects should expand access to prevention services, promote protective factors, reduce behavioral health risk, support early identification and intervention, and strengthen the behavioral health continuum of care. Funding supports new or enhanced prevention services, workforce development, and innovative service delivery models to improve community health. All activities must comply with relevant state statutes, including the Idaho Parental Rights Act. Administrative/indirect costs are limited to 10% of Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC), per CMS requirements. Awards will be made based on the criteria outlined herein, and the Department reserves the right to fund applications out of rank order to ensure equitable geographic distribution and population reach.
applicantTypes: Hospital or health system in Idaho

data.title: Idaho Crisis Intervention Training
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
data.summary: The Idaho Crisis Intervention Training initiative, led by the Idaho Department of Health and Welfare, invites applications from eligible organizations to provide Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) training and related programs for law enforcement and first responders statewide. The program specifically targets expansion and standardization of evidence-based CIT curricula, with the goal of improving mental health crisis response, reducing use-of-force incidents, and fostering effective community partnerships. Successful applicants will develop and deliver CIT instruction, supply necessary materials, partner with local agencies for program sustainability, and formally evaluate impact according to established metrics.

data.title: GO-NORTH School-Based Oral Health Programs (SBOHP) - Three Funding Goals
data.issuingAgency: Foundation for Healthy Communities (FHC)
data.summary: The GO-NORTH School-Based Oral Health Programs (SBOHP) RFA, administered by the Foundation for Healthy Communities, provides competitive grants to New Hampshire-based organizations for three core goals: (1) Stabilize and strengthen existing rural school-based oral health programs (Goal 1, awards $50,000–$80,000 per application); (2) Launch new rural school-based oral health programs to expand access in underserved rural schools or districts (Goal 2, awards $350,000–$500,000 per application, up to 3 awards in total, with a focus on site identification, staffing, equipment, outreach, and sustainability); (3) Purchase and implement electronic dental record (EDR) systems for school-based oral health programs (Goal 3, approx. $20,000 per application, up to 10 awards; may be applied for standalone or with Goals 1/2, technical assistance provided). Eligible uses and requirements for each goal are specifically detailed in the solicitation. All activities and costs must comply with 2 CFR Part 200, and certain categories (e.g., equipment over $10,000) have special pre-approval requirements. Applicants must submit a narrative linking their proposal to program criteria, a work plan (using FHC's template), a project budget (using the template), letters of support from partners, and appropriate organizational documentation. Awards may be partial or full, and FHC may require budget or scope adjustments prior to contracting. The initial term runs through September 30, 2027, with possible non-competitive renewals through September 30, 2031, subject to performance and funding. The application process and evaluation criteria are designed to advance rural health transformation priorities through sustainable, evidence-based, and measurable approaches.

data.title: Community Stabilization Services Infrastructure Expansion
data.issuingAgency: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS)
data.summary: The Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS) is soliciting proposals to expand the capacity for community-based stabilization services across Montana through investments in needed infrastructure. Eligible applicants are counties, municipalities, or multi-county entities within Montana. The RFP aims to reduce the likelihood of individuals being placed on the Forensic Mental Health Facility waitlist by enhancing local stabilization capabilities. Proposals must meet all mandatory requirements and respond thoroughly to the detailed scope of work. Funding will support infrastructure for mental health and addiction services, with an emphasis on increased access, especially in rural areas, and reducing wait times for forensic mental health facilities. Applicants must submit documentation including a business information form, offeror qualifications, detailed budget, and other required disclosures. Bonus points are available for certification under Montana's Equal Pay for Women Executive Order.

data.title: Iowa School Based Services (RFP MEDIOMC26023)
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) announces a forthcoming Request for Proposal (RFP MEDIOMC26023), anticipated for release in July 2026, for the provision of medical, mental/behavioral, and dental health services in rural Iowa schools. This initiative is part of Iowa's Healthy Hometowns Rural Health Transformation Plan, with contract(s) awarded October–November 2026 and estimated total funding of approximately $209,040,063.71 in 100% federal funds. A question and answer period will follow the RFP release (July-August 2026), proposals will be due September 2026, and full details including eligibility and evaluation criteria will be specified in the official RFP documentation.

data.title: Iowa High-risk Obstetric and Neonatal Transport Projects (RFP PHTHOET27002)
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will support approximately three projects aimed at strengthening Iowa's rural perinatal system by expanding EMS capacity to safely transport high-risk pregnant individuals and newborns to appropriate levels of care. Projects will equip EMS agencies with specialized training, tele OB support, and neonatal-specific equipment, with the ultimate goal of establishing consistent, reliable transfer patterns across a statewide hub-and-spoke network. This initiative, backed by over $209 million in CMS/HHS funding, seeks to improve outcomes and ensure timely, coordinated access to advanced maternal and neonatal services.

data.title: GO-NORTH Rural Primary Care Transformation Funding Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: Foundation for Healthy Communities (FHC) – GO-NORTH Program
data.summary: Supports rural primary care transformation projects in New Hampshire across FQHCs, RHCs, Critical Access Hospitals, and other rural clinics through team-based, technology-enabled, value-driven, and sustainable models. Provides direct funds for three program stages: Project Development, Preparatory Investments, and Program Ready implementation projects. Higher awards are available for regional, multi-organization partnerships demonstrating shared infrastructure, service delivery, or risk. Proposals must address all four Rural Primary Care Focus Areas: 1) Innovative care models, 2) Technology adoption with ROI, 3) Transition to value-based care, and 4) Financial sustainability and operational efficiency. Priority given to organizations serving Medicaid, with clear sliding fee policies, and those demonstrating strong partnerships for integrated, scalable change.

data.title: Iowa Cardiovascular Health Hub and Spoke Networks (RFP COMPADM26007)
data.issuingAgency: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services will release RFP COMPADM26007 in July or August 2026 to establish Cardiovascular Health Hub and Spoke Networks statewide. The procurement will support rural provider strategic partnerships, telehealth, referral networks, provider recruitment, equipment acquisition, minor renovations, and maternal health care enhancement. Applicants will be required to demonstrate collaborative partnerships through executed hub-spoke agreements. The initiative is part of the $209 million CMS/HHS Healthy Hometowns statewide rural health transformation effort. Activities may specifically include forming rural provider strategic partnerships, advancing telehealth for cardiovascular health, establishing referral networks among non-affiliated provider organizations, provider recruitment, purchasing equipment and associated minor renovations, and enhancing maternal health care provision at hub and spoke sites.

data.title: ROOTS (Rural Opportunities for Optimal Transformation in Students' Health) — Year 2
data.issuingAgency: Oklahoma State Department of Education (OSDE)
data.summary: OSDE's ROOTS Competitive Grant, Year 2: a 12-month grant running November 2026–October 2027, for the same 60 rural PK–12 schools as Year 1. Schools receive professional development, mentoring, and up to $10,000 for approved equipment, contingent on completing required activities (trainings, coaching sessions, collaborative learning opportunities).
applicantTypes: School districts (rural, previously participating in Year 1)

data.title: Critical Access Hospitals to Rural Emergency Hospitals Conversion Grants
data.issuingAgency: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: Nebraska RHTP Initiative 2.5 provides funding for Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) and Rural Emergency Hospitals (REHs) to complete infrastructure, technology, and equipment improvements that support expanded service lines, promote quality improvement, and strengthen financial stability. Funding must be used for minor improvements and does not support major construction or operating costs. Awarded projects are selected based on demonstrated need, projected impact, and a strategic financial plan with return-on-investment analysis. The maximum award per application is $67,600; all funds must be expended by July 31, 2027.

data.title: Rural Health Link (RHL) Initiative: Medical Transportation Capacity Expansion Funding Opportunity
data.issuingAgency: State of West Virginia - Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: The State of West Virginia, through the Rural Health Link (RHL) initiative of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), is announcing a funding opportunity totaling approximately $2.34 million. This initiative aims to expand non-emergency medical transportation capacity by supporting the acquisition of vehicles and expanding transportation operations. The goal is to increase the number of vehicles, drivers, and rides available for West Virginians—particularly residents in rural areas needing reliable access to healthcare. This funding is specifically targeted at expansion and is distinct from previous RHL opportunities focused on coordination and collaboration. Eligible organizations include transportation providers, public transit agencies, healthcare-affiliated transportation organizations, and other entities capable of rapid service expansion.

data.title: Rural Health Data Hub (New Mexico RHT Program)
data.issuingAgency: New Mexico Health Care Authority (HCA)
data.summary: New Mexico’s Rural Health Data Hub is a planned RHT initiative to support secure data integration, analytics, transparency, and rural health performance monitoring. HCA currently lists the related RFP as coming soon; the solicitation deadline and vendor budget are not yet published.

data.title: Missouri RHTP: Support EMS - Pillar 3: EMS Agency Consolidation
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Emergency Medical Services Association (MEMSA)
data.summary: Missouri RHTP Support EMS Pillar 3: funding to support EMS agency consolidation and regional coordination, as part of Missouri's three-pillar Support EMS RHTP initiative (Pillar 1: Workforce, Pillar 2: MIH-CP System Expansion, Pillar 3: Agency Collaboration/Consolidation). Funding supports both planning (Phase 1) and implementation (Phase 2) of EMS collaboration and consolidation projects to enhance sustainability, governance, operational efficiency, and service delivery for rural and at-risk regions. Agencies may apply for Phase 1 only (assessment/readiness and planning/design), or for both Phase 1 and Phase 2 together (implementation/optimization). Priority is given to applications demonstrating urgent regional need, risk due to hospital closures, willingness to consolidate or regionally align, and alignment with ToRCH Hubs and MIH-CP expansion efforts. Selection is based on need, project design, readiness, sustainability, and cross-sector partnerships. Applications are reviewed monthly on a rolling basis, and initial awards fund up to 12 months; continuation funding is subject to availability, performance, and need.

data.title: Missouri RHTP: Support EMS - Pillar 1: Workforce Development & Sustainability
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Emergency Medical Services Association (MEMSA)
data.summary: Missouri RHTP Support EMS Pillar 1 provides noncompetitive funding for EMS workforce development and sustainability. The program offers direct funding to accredited training entities to expand the EMT and Community Health Worker (CHW) education pipeline, as well as cost-based student scholarships for AEMT, Paramedic, and Community Paramedic training. Funding covers tuition, books, fees, and approved wraparound supports. Programs must demonstrate workforce outcomes through required reporting on course completion, certification, licensure, and job placement, and ensure rural service commitments for scholarship recipients. Annual participation is contingent on the availability of state appropriations and satisfactory performance.

data.title: Maryland RHTP Pillar 2 Award Offers — Budget Period 1 ($78.6M to 41 Organizations)
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission; Maryland Health Care Commission
data.summary: Maryland RHTP Pillar 2 ("Promote Sustainable Access and Innovative Care") issued Budget Period 1 award offers totaling $78,625,071 to 41 organizations across all rural and semi-rural counties. Awards are split between two sub-programs: Transformation Funds (33 organizations, $72,412,038 issued by the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission) and Expand Primary Care Access (8 organizations, $6,213,033 issued by the Maryland Health Care Commission). Pillar 2 supports advancing technology enablement, integrated primary and behavioral care, care navigation, oral health, paramedicine, closed-loop referrals, and rural practice expansion. Awarded projects include EHR modernization, infrastructure for behavioral health, oral healthcare, chronic disease management using paramedicine and CHW networks, and the launch or expansion of primary care clinics incorporating telehealth, behavioral health integration, and workforce transformation. The program prioritizes upstream prevention, data-driven innovations, new clinical networks, sustainable financial models, and addressing rural health disparities.

data.title: Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $160.7M (Preliminary) Across 161 Projects Through Week 3 (More Pending)
data.issuingAgency: Alaska Department of Health
data.summary: The Alaska Department of Health (DOH) announced on August 7, 2026, the first Notices of Intent to Award through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), delivering over $4.59 million to 19 projects across Alaska. This marks the start of a series of rolling weekly awards aiming to expand access to care, strengthen the health workforce, improve healthcare infrastructure, advance technology, and foster innovative solutions tailored to rural and hub communities. Project selection is based on alignment with RHTP goals, transformational potential, rural impact, sustainability, and contribution to a balanced statewide portfolio. Awarded amounts and project terms remain subject to completion of budget review, resolution of award conditions, and grant agreement execution. Additional award notices are announced each Friday. For up-to-date program information, visit the Alaska RHTP website.

data.title: Maine Rural Hospital Efficiency Fund
data.issuingAgency: Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), in partnership with the Office of Affordable Health Care
data.summary:
Maine DHHS, in partnership with the Office of Affordable Health Care, announced $30 million in RHTP funding to strengthen the long-term financial health and sustainability of rural hospitals. This is NOT a competitive application — DHHS identified and invited 11 specific rural hospitals based on an analysis of hospital financial data from the Maine Health Data Organization. Invited hospitals receive individualized technical assistance from industry experts on financial efficiency and sustainability, then use that assistance to develop individualized sustainability plans identifying priority projects.

Funding runs in two phases: Phase 1 (~$3M) supports hospital staff participation in technical assistance and development of sustainability plans, due January 2027 (unused Phase 1 funds roll into Phase 2). Phase 2 (~$27M) funds approved hospital-identified efficiency projects, evaluated on quality, anticipated impact, and compliance with federal/state requirements, implemented by August 2027. Program runs September 2026 through August 2027.

data.title: Award Recommendation for RFP 26-86529: Centralized Billing Office and Cost Report
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Administration
data.summary: Following a competitive RFP process, Blue & Co., LLC is recommended for contract negotiations to administer Indiana’s Centralized Billing Office and Cost Report program. The award covers an initial 4-year term valued at $3,984,000 with two optional one-year extensions, potentially reaching $6,175,200 in total. A minimum of 3% of contract value will be subcontracted to GenTech Associates, an Indiana Veteran Owned Small Business. Proposals were reviewed for adherence to mandatory requirements, management assessment/quality, cost, and subcontractor commitments as detailed in the RFP. Blue & Co., LLC submitted the highest-scoring proposal following evaluation and BAFO rounds.

data.title: Mississippi HIE Procurement Design — Consultant Opportunity (Knowledge Services Posting 162359)
data.issuingAgency: Mississippi State Department of Health (MSDH), via Mississippi Department of Information Technology Services (ITS) Knowledge Services Managed Services Provider Program
data.summary: The Mississippi State Department of Health (MSDH) is procuring consulting services through the Managed Services Provider Program ("Knowledge Services"), administered by the Mississippi Department of Information Technology Services (ITS). The selected consultant will provide subject matter expertise and technical assistance to develop a competitive solicitation for the future procurement of a comprehensive statewide Health Information Exchange (HIE). This is a planning/design engagement — it covers designing the eventual HIE procurement, not building or operating the HIE itself.

data.title: Missouri RHTP: Mobile Integrated Healthcare & Community Paramedicine (MIH-CP) System Expansion — MEMSA Partnership
data.issuingAgency: Missouri Emergency Medical Services Association (MEMSA), in partnership with Missouri Dept. of Social Services (RHTP) and Dept. of Health & Senior Services' Office of Rural Health and Primary Care
data.summary: The Missouri Department of Social Services, through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), partnered with the Dept. of Health and Senior Services' Office of Rural Health and Primary Care and the Missouri Emergency Medical Services Association (MEMSA) to expand Mobile Integrated Healthcare and Community Paramedicine (MIH-CP) services across rural Missouri. MEMSA administers the funding directly: rural EMS agencies apply to start up or expand an MIH-CP program or Regional MIH Network, integrating with ToRCH Care Hubs and Regional Coordinating Networks (RCNs).

data.title: Oregon RHTP: Transformation Funds
data.issuingAgency: Oregon Health Authority (OHA)
data.summary: Direct, non-competitive funding to Oregon's 35 rural hospitals for stabilization — distinct from the competitive Catalyst Awards pool.

data.title: Oregon RHTP: Immediate Impact Awards — Wave 2
data.issuingAgency: Oregon Health Authority (OHA)
data.summary: 33 new projects funded — mobile health units, a new family-medicine residency program, and food/nutrition connection programs. Combined Wave 1+2 = $23.5M across 45 projects.

data.title: Oregon RHTP: Immediate Impact Awards — Wave 1
data.issuingAgency: Oregon Health Authority (OHA)
data.summary: 12 projects funded addressing mental health/SUD prevention, chronic disease management, and workforce training — non-competitive, targeted at urgent rural needs.

data.title: Delaware Statewide Health Information Technology Infrastructure for Real-Time Insurance Verification and Prior Authorizations
data.issuingAgency: Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) / Delaware Health Care Commission / Delaware Health Information Network (DHIN) / Smart Health Network
data.summary: The Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) and the Delaware Health Care Commission have launched a new Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) initiative to support real-time insurance verification and prior authorization capabilities statewide. Leveraging the Delaware Health Information Network (DHIN) and Smart Health Network, the project provides a shared connection point for participating providers and payers to exchange information using common standards, thereby reducing administrative burdens, improving care coordination, and supporting faster access to care. The initiative is part of the RHTP and specifically aims to decrease administrative workload for providers and increase efficiency in Medicaid and rural healthcare settings. This is a direct partnership, not subject to competitive bidding.

data.title: Georgia RHTP: Consumer Engagement Enhancements
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH)
data.summary: Extends the State Health Benefit Plan's consumer wellness platform—including an AI-generated Geospatial Health Risk Profile, diet and wellness coaching tools, and integrated behavioral health components—to the AHEAD-model population in 126 HRSA-designated rural counties. The initiative is part of a broader technology-driven effort to improve care coordination, patient engagement, and health outcomes, supported by partnerships with academic institutions, healthcare providers, and technology firms. Expansion to rural health clinics and FQHCs is planned in Years 2-5 as budget permits.

data.title: Georgia RHTP: AHEC Training and Housing
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH)
data.summary: Supports Area Health Education Center (AHEC) training and short-term housing for job shadowing, expansion of the Preceptor Tax Incentive program, and Digital Health Navigator training. Initiative Four is part of a coordinated statewide strategy to address multiple stages of the rural healthcare workforce pipeline, aiming to increase provider retention, reduce EMT turnover, expand residency slots, and enhance dementia care across 126 HRSA-rural counties in Georgia.

data.title: Georgia RHTP: Public Health Investments — Newborn Screening Program
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Public Health
data.summary: This initiative funds expansion of a second newborn screening laboratory site in Waycross, Georgia, ensuring that Atlanta is no longer the sole statewide newborn screening lab. The program is designed to reduce wait times for newborn screening results and expands laboratory capacity to benefit rural populations across Georgia's 126 HRSA-designated rural counties. The initiative emphasizes sustainability through third-party payers and user fees and is part of the Georgia GREAT Health Program's strategic effort to strengthen the health care continuum.

data.title: Georgia RHTP: Support for Acquired Brain Injury (ABI) Survivors
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH)
data.summary: Statewide expansion of the Side-By-Side (SBS) Clubhouse survivor-centered care model, opening Georgia's first rural ABI clubhouse. Covers 126 HRSA-designated rural counties/portions. Initiative aims to improve care outcomes and reduce long-term costs, emphasizing sustainability through user fees and payer reimbursements within rural Georgia for acquired brain injury survivors. Estimated funding is $3,475,000 total, including $257,000 in Budget Period 1.

data.title: Georgia RHTP: Nursing Care Improvements
data.issuingAgency: Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH)
data.summary: Five-part nursing workforce strategy: faculty advancement and tuition assistance, GA-CARE tuition reimbursement, nurse summer camps, and simulation training expansion at Georgia College & State University. Part of a coordinated rural health workforce effort targeting increased rural provider retention and expanded training capacity in Georgia’s HRSA-designated rural counties. Initiative Four operates under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) strategic goal of strengthening workforce in rural and underserved areas. Funded activities must serve rural populations and support the state's vision to address the needs of healthcare workforce development across career stages.
applicantTypes: Public or private higher education institutions

data.title: Indiana RHTP: Growing Access to Hospital Post-Discharge Medications (Meds-to-Beds)
data.issuingAgency: Indiana Department of Health (IDOH)
data.summary: Grow Rural Health Initiative 6 ensures rural Indiana hospital patients receive prescribed medications at bedside prior to discharge, removing barriers associated with accessing outpatient pharmacy services. Medications are provided at outpatient prices and paired with bedside counseling. This noncompetitive, CMS/HHS-funded program aims to improve recovery outcomes, reduce hospital readmissions, and addresses transportation and access issues. IDOH, alongside a new statewide Meds-to-Beds steering committee, oversees implementation, resource development, and technical assistance for participating hospitals. Year 1 activities include the award of $20,000 planning grants to 43 identified hospitals, the formation of a steering committee in July 2026, required baseline data reporting by October 31, 2026, hospital-specific implementation plans by December 31, 2026, and provision of medications at discharge by July 31, 2027. Additional implementation funding may be available for hospitals prepared to provide bedside medications by the 2027 milestone.

data.title: South Dakota Medicaid PACT (Primary Accountable Care Transformation) Vendor RFP
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Social Services (DSS) — Division of Medical Services
data.summary: The awarded vendor will support South Dakota Medicaid in transforming primary care reimbursement under the Primary Accountable Care Transformation (PACT) model: (1) Reimbursement design — actuarial support to design a population-based alternative payment methodology replacing primary care E&M billing with a monthly Prospective Primary Care Payment, plus methodology for ongoing updates; (2) Provider value-based quality payments — a quality-based payment methodology tied to provider performance on HEDIS or other quality measures, funding yearly value-based payments; (3) Population health and case management tools — a recipient rewards program and investment in case management/population health infrastructure to support the model, plus facilitation of stakeholder engagement meetings. Requested funding: $62,735,000 over five years. This single vendor RFP covers all three facets — reimbursement design, VBQ payments, and population health/case management tooling are described as one integrated scope of work, not separate solicitations.

data.title: South Dakota RHTP: Chronic Disease Self-Management Programming
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health (DOH)
data.summary: Expands chronic-disease self-management programs in rural/western South Dakota, including lay-leader training, community workshops, and marketing components. Distinct from the existing DB 'Chronic Disease Remote Monitoring in Schools' record (id afbf6630-5ba0-4522-88e8-df852b36405e), which covers a school-based remote-monitoring program rather than adult community self-management workshops. Part of the RHT program's First Round RFPs.

data.title: South Dakota RHTP: Doula Workforce Advancement Program
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health (DOH)
data.summary: Strengthens the doula workforce and improves maternal and infant health outcomes via training and community/Tribal doula program expansion across the perinatal period. Part of the RHT program's Second Round RFPs.

data.title: South Dakota RHTP: Rural Health Forward Training Hub
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health (DOH)
data.summary: Statewide training/resource hub ('Rural Health Forward') closing education/training gaps between urban and rural clinicians, developed/hosted/maintained by a South Dakota-based partner organization. SD-based applicants only. Part of the RHT program's Second Round RFPs.

data.title: South Dakota RHTP: Expand and Strengthen Rural Community Health Worker Workforce
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health (DOH)
data.summary: Technical assistance and professional development for Community Health Workers/Representatives, part of the RHT program's First Round RFPs.

data.title: South Dakota RHTP: Statewide Maternal Health Access and Services Assessment
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health (DOH)
data.summary: Assesses the maternal health landscape in South Dakota to identify strengths, gaps, and opportunities to improve access to maternal and infant care across the prenatal and postpartum periods — part of SD's 'Regional Maternal and Infant Health Hubs' initiative, from the RHT program's Second Round RFPs.

data.title: South Dakota RHTP: Behavioral Health Modernization (CCBHC) Systems Evaluation and Technology Roadmap
data.issuingAgency: South Dakota Department of Health (DOH)
data.summary: Systems evaluation and technology roadmap for CCBHC/EHR integration, part of South Dakota's behavioral health RHTP track. Distinct scope from the already-tracked 'Rural BH Modernization (CCBHC) Infrastructure & Sustainability Grant' (id 95b40ebd-20c5-468d-a24b-a68efea3f244) — that record covers infrastructure/sustainability grant funding, while this record covers the CCBHC systems evaluation and technology roadmap consulting engagement.

data.title: Maryland RHTP: NourishMD Expansion — Small Grocers and Mobile Markets
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Population Health Improvement, State Office of Rural Health
data.summary: Expands the NourishMD program to small grocers and mobile markets serving rural food deserts.

data.title: Maryland RHTP: Mobile Health Expansion
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Population Health Improvement
data.summary: Funds mobile health unit expansion administered through regional Local Health Departments as part of the Maryland Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The program, supported by CMS/HHS, aims to modernize and strengthen care in Maryland’s 18 state-designated rural areas through subawards for innovative projects that bolster sustainable healthcare access, workforce development, and community health. Funding emphasizes potential for impact on access, affordability, and innovative models consistent with CMS core principles. RHTP is supported by a $168,180,837.61 federal award from CMS/HHS, with 100% federal funding, and is implemented in five-year renewable budget periods (2025–2030). Projects must align with one or more of the program's three pillars: rural health workforce transformation, sustainable access & innovative healthcare, and empowering healthy food systems.

data.title: Maryland RHTP: Increase Efficiency of Local Agency Operations
data.issuingAgency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Population Health Improvement (on behalf of the State Office of Rural Health, in partnership with Garrett County Health Department)
data.summary: Two application windows in 2026 supported projects to increase the efficiency of local agency operations under the Maryland Rural Health Transformation Program's Pillar 2 (Promote Sustainable Access and Innovative Care). The RHTP is funded with federal support to strengthen and modernize healthcare in Maryland’s 18 state-designated rural areas. Subawards are available through competitive application, prioritizing projects with clear potential impact on sustainable health care access, innovation, and local operational efficiency. The RHTP seeks to advance CMS principles of choice and competition, with all funds 100% provided by CMS/HHS through 2025.
applicantTypes: Health system partner (serving a state-designated rural area)

data.title: Maryland Rural Health Connectivity Program
data.issuingAgency: CRISP (Chesapeake Regional Information System for our Patients)
data.summary: Offsets EHR vendor connectivity costs for rural providers, administered by CRISP. Rolling/first-come-first-serve basis; no fixed deadline.

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Expansion of Area Health Education Center (AHEC) Career Pathways Programming
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Illinois HFS describes this as a named Rural Health Transformation Program implementation allocation to UIC Area Health Education Center (AHEC) for expansion of career-pathways programming for rural high school students, rather than a public competitive funding opportunity.
applicantTypes: Named Sub-awardees in State RHTP Plan

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Expansion of Training and Certification Programs for Healthcare Support Workers
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Training/certification program expansion for healthcare support workers via community colleges and community-based training programs. Initiative 3.B under the Illinois Rural Health Transformation Program, supported by CMS/HHS, aims to strengthen the rural healthcare workforce through targeted funding for selected training and certification programs. Programs are sub-awarded through formula allocations to community colleges and University affiliates, with funds obligated according to the program timeline.

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Expansion of Incentives and Training Programs for Clinical Professionals
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Incentive and training program expansion for clinical professions across state universities, community colleges, and hospitals. Target: award Q3 2026. Per official RHTP documents, Initiative 3.A funds will be distributed via formula/subaward (not open competition) to named higher education institutions and rural hospital consortia for clinical workforce incentive and education initiatives in Illinois.

data.title: Illinois RHTP: EMS Enhancement Grants to Resource Hospitals
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Grants to EMS Resource Hospitals serving rural patients through the Illinois Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Funding supports capital and workforce training enhancements to improve EMS service delivery, targeting rural and frontier hospital systems. Year 1 awards are planned for Q2 2026, with required budget obligation by October 30, 2026. The program operates as a formula-based sub-award directly to eligible hospitals through the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH), as specified in the state's CMS-approved RHTP implementation plan.

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Investment in Technological Infrastructure for Rural Providers
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Technology infrastructure investment for rural hospitals, RHCs, FQHCs, pharmacies, and clinicians. Target: award to hospitals Q4 2026. This is part of Initiative 2.B Technological Innovation for Virtual Care, under Illinois's Rural Health Transformation Program, a five-year CMS-supported effort to improve rural healthcare access and delivery through major infrastructure and workforce investments. Awards are allocated via formula and sub-award to ICAHN (via Illinois Connected Care Collaborative, IC3).

data.title: Illinois RHTP: EMS and Mobile Healthcare — Mobile Health Infrastructure Funds
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Funds mobile health infrastructure for primary care and behavioral health providers. Target: release funding opportunities/select providers Q3-Q4 2026.

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Healthcare Transformation Collaborative (HTC) Expansion
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Awards 4 rural Healthcare Transformation Collaborators as subrecipients. Target: award Q1 2026 (may already be awarded by now — set status OPEN).

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Hospital Technical Assistance
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Provides facilitation and technical assistance services to hospital grantees implementing transformation plans under the Illinois Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). This sub-award supports hospitals as they develop and execute regionally focused care delivery reforms, with services provided for the duration of the RHTP initiative. The effort is intended to advance healthcare access, quality, and outcomes for rural Illinois communities in alignment with federally-approved transformation strategies.
applicantTypes: Named sub-awardee (Office of Medicaid Innovation at University of Illinois)

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Team-Based Care Grants for Primary Care and Behavioral Health Providers
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Supports the implementation of team-based care models in rural Illinois by providing funding through IPHCA and CBHA to primary care and behavioral health providers. This program aims to improve healthcare access, quality, and outcomes as part of Illinois' participation in the Rural Health Transformation Program, with a Year 1 budget allocation of $20 million.

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Primary Care and Behavioral Health Technical Assistance
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Planned Illinois Rural Health Transformation Program initiative for primary care and behavioral health practices. The Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS) March 9, 2026 program update identifies the Office of Medicaid Innovation at the University of Illinois System as the sub-awardee and describes technical assistance to help practices transition to integrated care teams and value-based payment models. The update lists preliminary initiative funding of $2.5 million per year. No provider-facing application, solicitation, deadline, or award opportunity has been published yet; provider rollout is planned for Q3 2026 and ongoing.

data.title: Illinois RHTP: Disease Prevention Grants to Hospitals
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)
data.summary: Formula-based grants to rural hospitals for chronic-disease programming (diabetes prevention, mental health first aid, tobacco cessation). Target: award via formula Q3 2026.

data.title: Rural Healthcare Access Modernization Program (RAMP) — Tennessee
data.issuingAgency: Tennessee Department of Health
data.summary: The Rural Healthcare Access Modernization Program (RAMP) is a Tennessee Department of Health initiative supported by approximately $104.4 million in TennCare Shared Savings, complementing the federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The Tennessee General Assembly allocated $104.4 million to TDH in the FY27 budget (from a $125M total; $20.6M funds a separate TennCare-administered Rural Health Clinic track). RAMP deploys three main funding priorities: (1) Rural Capital Projects — awards include one $40M, one $20M, two $10M, and four up to $2.5M (renovations, expansion, new construction; IT/equipment max 20% of grant, subject to approval for items >$10K); (2) Competitive Grant Extensions — supplemental funding for eligible RHTP-aligned projects needing to continue or complete implementation; (3) Primary Care Seed Funding — eight $500K awards and one $427.5K award (per-site cap $500K) to establish or expand rural primary care with emphasis on pediatric and obstetric care. Eligible applicants include governmental, nonprofit, for-profit organizations, and Tennessee state agencies serving rural populations in any of Tennessee's 95 counties. Multi-site operators are eligible, subject to per-applicant caps. Matching required for capital projects except for applicants in distressed/at-risk counties. Grantees must attend mandatory training on invoicing/reimbursement within 90 days of contract. Application process is forthcoming; further eligibility and application details will be published as available.

data.title: EMR Modernization Provider Funding (Year 1)
data.issuingAgency: Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
data.summary: Under Maine RHTP's Technology & Innovation initiative: the state's first provider funding opportunity, approximately $30 million in Year 1 funding to help eligible rural health care providers replace, upgrade, and enhance electronic medical record (EMR) systems. Unlike a competitive award, all eligible organizations that submit a qualifying application are expected to receive an award; final amounts depend on applicant/site count and rural designation (rural sites get ~50% higher funding than comparable non-rural sites). Application process hosted by MCD Global Health, anticipated to open mid-July 2026.
applicantTypes: General hospitals with a dedicated ED

data.title: Colorado eHealth Solutions Challenge — Three Winning Projects Announced
data.issuingAgency: Colorado Governor's Office / Colorado Office of eHealth Innovation
data.summary: Colorado announced three winning projects under the eHealth Solutions Challenge as part of implementation-focused rural health innovation activity. This is an award/update signal rather than an open solicitation.

data.title: RHTP – Education and Outreach Services
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)
data.summary: The Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) has released a Request for Quotes seeking Education and Outreach Services under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). The program, funded by a $209 million federal award from CMS, aims to strengthen rural health care through education and outreach to assist Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries in selecting integrated health plans. This solicitation is limited to current Florida DMS State Term Contract holders, per Ch. 287, Florida Statutes, and focuses on supporting the adoption of integrated health care options in rural communities.

data.title: RHTP – Independent Evaluation Services
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration
data.summary: Request for Quotes (RFQ) for independent evaluation services under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), focusing on monitoring compliance, data governance, and the efficacy of the RHTP initiative. data.title: Louisiana Rural Tech Catalyst Fund (RTCF) Launch
data.issuingAgency: Louisiana Economic Development / Rural Health Transformation Program
data.summary: Louisiana has launched the Rural Tech Catalyst Fund under the Rural Health Transformation Program to advance rural health care through public-private partnerships and innovation. The RTCF will provide support for new health care models, technology deployment, and workforce development across rural Louisiana. Applications are now open.

data.title: Value-Based Care Models for Rural Health Facilities
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: Forecasted opportunity for a Utah-based 501(c)(3) healthcare organization to develop and implement value-based care models for rural health facilities. Single award of up to $6,000,000 (up to $15M over 5 years).

data.title: Behavioral Health–Primary Care Integration (PATH 1.5, 1.G)
data.issuingAgency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.summary: 3–6 awards of up to $2M each to integrate behavioral health into primary care settings in rural Utah. Requires collaboration from 3+ local agencies. Estimated total funding up to $15,000,000 over 5 years. Activities include implementing an integrated behavioral health and primary care model using a stepped-care approach and offering intensive technical assistance at rural sites.

data.title: Idaho Pediatric Psychiatry Access Line (PPAL)
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare, Division of Behavioral Health
data.summary: The Idaho Pediatric Psychiatry Access Line (PPAL) is a competitive subgrant solicitation by the Idaho Department of Health and Welfare, Division of Behavioral Health. The opportunity seeks to establish a statewide psychiatric teleconsultation program operated by a public Idaho university. The subgrant supports improved behavioral health access for rural pediatric providers through direct psychiatric consultation, workforce integration, training, and real-time support. The resulting access line aligns with Idaho's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Initiative 4: implementing population-specific, evidence-based projects to enhance access and outcomes in rural and underserved communities. Requirements include lead coordination, program and technology capacity, and non-duplication of funds attestation, with ongoing financial and programmatic reporting.

data.title: Idaho RHTP Project Management Support
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
data.summary: Contractor to provide comprehensive project management services to administer operational oversight and task-tracking support for the RHTP plan and all the proposed initiatives. Key deliverables include comprehensive project support.

data.title: Graduate Medical Education (GME) Expansion for Rural Idaho – FFY26
data.issuingAgency: Idaho Dept of Health and Welfare (DHW)
data.summary: The Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (DHW), in coordination with the Idaho State Board of Education, seeks to fund one (1) lead organization to expand Graduate Medical Education (GME) in Idaho in accordance with statewide Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) priorities for FY26. The award targets expansion of existing rural residency programs and creation of new tracks, including but not limited to OB/Gyn, behavioral health, and geriatrics, to strengthen rural provider workforce. Agreement anticipates a single subgrant for $8,000,000 for FFY26. Implementation will support RHTP Initiative 3: Sustaining rural workforce with training, recruitment, and retention. Reporting requirements include approved implementation plans, partner agreements, quarterly progress reports tracking residents trained, rotations, incentives, retention documentation, and feedback from preceptors.

data.title: Healthcare Transformation Capital Investment Grant Program
data.issuingAgency: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services & Illinois Capital Development Board
data.summary: The Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS), in coordination with the Illinois Capital Development Board, is offering the Healthcare Transformation Capital Investment Grant Program. This competitive grant program supports capital improvements for Illinois hospitals and other qualified healthcare providers serving underserved areas. Applicants may request up to $80 million per project, with $200 million available in total funding. See official guidelines and application instructions via the Illinois Catalog of State Financial Assistance (CSFA Number 511-00-3381): https://gata.illinois.gov/grants/csfa.html.

data.title: Alabama RHTP: Application Preparation Workshops
data.issuingAgency: Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA)
data.summary: ADECA is hosting statewide roadshow workshops in May 2026 to inform potential applicants about the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHT) and eleven related initiatives. Participants will receive guidance, resources, and Q&A opportunities to help prepare for competitive applications ahead of the first Notice of Funding Opportunities on June 1, 2026. Event locations include Bay Minette, Troy, Gadsden, Florence, and Montgomery.

data.title: Florida RHTP Application Preparation Resources
data.issuingAgency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)
data.summary: This guidance suite provides in-depth application preparation materials for entities seeking to participate in Florida's RHTP. Resources include: example outcome measure frameworks (quality improvement, financial/operational, EMS, population health); planning templates; work plan appendices; checklists; data sources; best-practices for needs assessment; and state-specific support tools. These documents are to be used for aligning RHTP proposals with state and federal expectation areas, outcome evaluation strategies, and compliance with the FY24-28 EMS Supplement.

data.title: GO-NORTH Rural Community Health Infrastructure Program (RCHIP)
data.issuingAgency: Governor's Office of New Opportunities & Rural Transformational Health (GO-NORTH), administered by NH Community Development Finance Authority (CDFA)
data.summary: New Hampshire was awarded $204 million from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to implement the first budget period of its five-period Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Plan. The Governor's Office of New Opportunities and Rural Transformational Health (GO-NORTH) contracted with the Community Development Finance Authority (CDFA) to invest more than $40 million per year through the Rural Community Health Infrastructure Program (RCHIP), a competitive program funding rehabilitation of key rural health infrastructure: county-run nursing home renovations to reduce hospital discharge barriers, community mental health center and FQHC renovations, childcare capacity renovations to support rural healthcare workforce recruitment/retention, and renovations to house ambulances and expand EMS capacity. CDFA also provides technical assistance from application through project completion.

data.title: Kentucky Federal RHTP Award (FY2026-FY2030)
data.issuingAgency: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
data.summary: Federal RHTP award as documented in the CMS 50-State Spotlights for FY2026. Supports Kentucky's strategies to address rural health barriers, including workforce training, telehealth expansion, maternal care, chronic disease, and value-based payment reform. State initiatives focus on rural hospital support, technology modernization, and population health improvements, enabled by federal-state cooperative agreement. Includes policy commitments and milestone-driven implementation.
